items.title: Accord sur le diesel russe : l’UE estime que cette décision donne à la Russie «les moyens de faire la guerre»
items.summary: L’annonce du président américain Donald Trump intervient après une discussion qualifiée par lui de « très fructueuse » avec son homologue russe Vladimir Poutine.
items.body_text:
Accord sur le diesel russe : l’UE estime que cette décision donne à la Russie «les moyens de faire la guerre»
L’annonce du président américain Donald Trump intervient après une discussion qualifiée par lui de « très fructueuse » avec son homologue russe Vladimir Poutine.
Passer la publicité Passer la publicité
Donald Trump a annoncé vendredi que son homologue russe Vladimir Poutine s’était engagé à fournir plusieurs millions de tonnes de diesel «pour le marché américain et mondial», sur plusieurs mois, après une «discussion très fructueuse». «La Russie va immédiatement fournir plus de 300.000 tonnes de diesel au marché américain et mondial, 500.000 tonnes de plus en novembre et 1.000.000 de tonnes immédiatement après. Par ailleurs, selon l’état de ses raffineries, la Russie va livrer rapidement 3.000.000 tonnes de diesel», a-t-il écrit sur son réseau Truth Social.
«Les prix du diesel pour les Américains et, en réalité, pour le monde, VONT BAISSER RAPIDEMENT DANS DES PROPORTIONS RECORD ! Des prix plus bas pour les Américains et surtout nos formidables paysans, éleveurs et transporteurs routiers, c’est ma plus grande priorité», a ajouté Donald Trump. Le président américain sait que le prix élevé des carburants est une cause majeure du mécontentement des électeurs avant des législatives très importantes le 3 novembre aux États-Unis. Le Parti républicain redoute de perdre le contrôle du Congrès lors de ces élections.
Passer la publicité
La Russie étant frappée de sanctions sur ses exportations d’hydrocarbures, le ministère des Finances américain a dans la foulée précisé avoir donné une autorisation provisoire pour cette mise sur le marché. Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky, lui, a dénoncé une «décision indigne» et «faible». «Vous savez, cela ressemble à un beau cadeau d’anniversaire pour Poutine. C’est absolument horrible», a déclaré Volodymyr Zelensky au média américain Axios en référence au 74e anniversaire mercredi du président russe. «Cela ne fait qu’alimenter Poutine et lui donne la possibilité de mener une guerre encore plus intense», a-t-il aussi déclaré à la presse, regrettant que l’équipe ukrainienne en déplacement en Floride ait «simplement servi de façade» pour cet accord avec Moscou.
La cheffe de la diplomatie de l’UE, Kaja Kallas, a déclaré samedi que la levée de sanctions sur le diesel russe contribuait à alimenter la guerre menée par le Kremlin contre l’Ukraine, après l’accord annoncé par Washington avec Moscou concernant ce carburant. «Suspendre les sanctions sur le diesel russe offre à Moscou davantage de revenus pour faire la guerre. Ce n’est pas le moment de relâcher la pression sur la Russie, et l’Europe ne le fera pas», a écrit Kallas sur les réseaux sociaux.
L’annonce de Donald Trump coïncide avec la reprise de discussions en Floride entre Américains et Ukrainiens vendredi et samedi, auxquelles les Européens ont été conviés, sur une résolution du conflit avec la Russie.
Préparer l’hiver
A Miami, la délégation ukrainienne a rencontré Steve Witkoff, l’émissaire spécial de Donald Trump, et Jared Kushner, le gendre du président américain qui agit en qualité de médiateur informel, en présence de représentants européens. Steve Witkoff a évoqué sur X des «discussions constructives», sans préciser si elles se poursuivraient samedi comme initialement prévu.
Les échanges ont notamment porté sur «des mesures à court terme liées à la préparation à l’hiver (résilience énergétique, exportations de céréales), des garanties de sécurité, ainsi que des dispositifs à plus long terme pour la sécurité de l’Ukraine et de l’Europe», a précisé l’émissaire.
Passer la publicité
Depuis mercredi, des attaques russes ont fait environ 60 morts en Ukraine, dont au moins 30 jeudi dans une frappe qui a touché deux bus à Kramatorsk (est), dans l’une des attaques les plus meurtrières des dernières semaines.
Les récents bombardements russes ont aussi causé des «dommages considérables» au réseau électrique ukrainien, a déploré vendredi M

items.title: Communes rurales : Sébastien Lecornu annonce une aide de 50 millions d’euros et des mesures pour faire baisser le prix du gazole
items.summary: Près de 9000 communes bénéficieront d’un nouveau soutien financier. Le gouvernement promet également des solutions adaptées à 339 stations-service isolées pour leur permettre de répercuter la baisse attendue des prix des carburants.
items.body_text:
Communes rurales : Sébastien Lecornu annonce une aide de 50 millions d’euros et des mesures pour faire baisser le prix du gazole
Près de 9000 communes bénéficieront d’un nouveau soutien financier. Le gouvernement promet également des solutions adaptées à 339 stations-service isolées pour leur permettre de répercuter la baisse attendue des prix des carburants.
Passer la publicité Passer la publicité
Sébastien Lecornu a annoncé samedi que les communes rurales bénéficieraient d'une «dotation nouvelle» de 50 millions d'euros et qu'il allait apporter une «réponse spécifique» aux stations-service de leurs territoires pour qu'elles puissent baisser les prix du gazole. Le gouvernement va «créer une dotation nouvelle, originale» pour les communes rurales qui «représentera 50 millions d'euros pour près de 9000 communes, dont 381 dans le département du Gers», a détaillé le premier ministre dans une vidéo diffusée devant le congrès de l'Association des maires ruraux de France (AMRF) qui se tient à Auch (Gers).
«Moins d'habitants, cela ne fait pas moins de kilomètres ou d'espaces naturels à entretenir. Les routes, les chemins, les hameaux restent là, mais les habitants sont moins nombreux pour en partager le coût», a justifié Sébastien Lecornu. Cette dotation pour les communes rurales s'ajoute à la hausse prévue, dans le projet de budget pour 2027, de 150 millions d'euros de la dotation globale de fonctionnement (DGF) pour les collectivités locales.
Passer la publicité
Une «réponse spécifique»
Face à la hausse des prix des carburants, qui affecte particulièrement les stations-service en zones rurales, Sébastien Lecornu a également promis de leur apporter une «réponse spécifique» pour les aider à baisser leurs prix sur le gazole après la libération de stocks stratégiques. Les préfectures vont ainsi contacter les 339 stations repérées comme isolées pour leur proposer «une solution ad hoc» et «tenir compte de leurs contraintes» d'approvisionnement, afin qu'elles puissent répercuter la baisse attendue de 12 à 18 centimes par litre, après le déblocage, sur trois mois, de 10 millions de barils de gazole issus des stocks stratégiques.
Sébastien Lecornu doit recevoir lundi les distributeurs de carburants à Matignon à cet effet. L'ancien ministre de la Ruralité, Michel Fournier, qui a quitté le gouvernement fin septembre, doit reprendre à ce congrès la présidence de l'AMRF.

items.title: Hausse des carburants : les auto-écoles contraintes d’augmenter leurs tarifs, le prix du permis pourrait grimper de 200 euros
items.summary: Exclues des aides gouvernementales, les écoles de conduite voient leurs marges fondre. Pour limiter leurs dépenses, certaines misent sur les simulateurs ou les véhicules électriques, mais ces solutions restent difficiles à généraliser.
items.body_text:
Hausse des carburants : les auto-écoles contraintes d’augmenter leurs tarifs, le prix du permis pourrait grimper de 200 euros
Exclues des aides gouvernementales, les écoles de conduite voient leurs marges fondre. Pour limiter leurs dépenses, certaines misent sur les simulateurs ou les véhicules électriques, mais ces solutions restent difficiles à généraliser.
Passer la publicité Passer la publicité
«On va devoir augmenter nos tarifs» : mises sous pression par la hausse du prix des carburants mais exclues des aides gouvernementales, les auto-écoles tentent de s'adapter pour continuer à rouler. Les prix à la pompe, gonflés par la guerre au Moyen-Orient, ont récemment battu des records, mettant à mal les trésoreries des quelque 11.000 écoles de conduite du pays. La facture «carburant» explose, avec des voitures dont le compteur affiche 45.000 à 60.000 km parcourus chaque année, selon plusieurs gérants interrogés par l'AFP.
Les frais d'approvisionnement en essence ont «augmenté de 30 à 40%» depuis le début de la crise, estime Vincent Rageul, gérant d'établissements à Rennes et président régional de l'École de conduite française (ECF). À l'auto-école rennaise Republik, cela signifie «10.000 euros de hausse du budget carburant sur les neuf derniers mois», selon le co-gérant, Morgan Poriel. Si l'écoconduite ou un recours accru aux simulateurs - dans la limite de dix heures - permettent d'économiser du carburant, la plupart des auto-écoles prévoient d'augmenter le prix du permis pour absorber les surcoûts.
Passer la publicité
«À l'os»
«On n'a pas d'autre choix que d'augmenter nos tarifs», passés de 52 à 55 euros l'heure, déplore Morgan Poriel. La faute à des marges très faibles, entre 2 et 4 euros sur un cours de conduite, que la hausse du carburant réduit encore, selon Lorenzo Lefebvre, président de la branche éducation et sécurité routière du syndicat Mobilians. «On est à l'os», résume-t-il. «Il y aura fatalement une augmentation du coût de la formation», regrette-t-il, en s'inquiétant : «On est dans un piège, parce que si ça augmente, les jeunes vont moins venir», dans un contexte de pouvoir d'achat en berne.
Alors que 36% des jeunes de 18-24 ans ne possèdent pas le permis de conduire, principalement «pour des raisons de coût», selon le baromètre Wimoov de septembre, la hausse à venir du prix du permis serait de «150 à 200 euros sur un forfait de 1600 euros actuellement», prévoit le président de l'ECF, Patrick Mirouse. Il demande ainsi à l'État d'accorder «des aides ponctuelles aux écoles de conduite, avant de rentrer dans une démarche beaucoup plus pérenne de verdissement de la flotte» grâce à l'électrification pour s'affranchir des énergies fossiles.
Électrification
L'école de conduite ADav a choisi cette dernière option «pour moins dépendre du carburant». Quand il s'est installé il y a 18 mois, le gérant, Dave Abissoina, déjà inquiet de l'évolution des prix de l'essence, a fait poser une borne de recharge sur les murs de son auto-école pour alimenter une voiture électrique. «Pour 320 km d'autonomie, le plein d'électricité me revient entre 5 et 9 euros», contre «80 euros le plein» d'une voiture thermique pour 600 km d'autonomie, se félicite-t-il.
Si ce choix va «dans le sens de l'histoire», juge Patrick Mirouse, il est difficile à généraliser en raison du manque de bornes de recharge et d'une demande de permis en boîte manuelle encore majoritaire. «Nous sommes basés en plein centre-ville, c'est infaisable car il faudrait que les salariés aillent recharger les voitures chez eux le soir», tranche Morgan Poriel. Du côté des élèves, en tout cas, la flambée de l'essence entraîne des remises en question. Pour Nora Hennebert, 27 ans, le choix d'un véhicule thermique une fois le permis en poche semblait évident. «Mais du coup je vais réfléchir car avec les prix c'est compliqué», concède cette développeuse web qui souhaite s'installer à la campagne.

HAC
Après trois semaines de trêve internationale, retour au championnat avec le match entre Lille et Le Havre ce samedi après-midi pour le compte de la 6e journée de Ligue 1. Le Losc, 4e, sera favori face au HAC, 18e, mais les Dogues devront se méfier de l'équipe normande. Suivez la rencontre en direct commenté sur le site et l'appli RMC Sport. Coup d'envoi à 17h15 au stade Pierre-Mauroy.
Regarder sur 12h58
Olivier Giroud, qui dispute très certainement la dernière saison de sa carrière, explique devoir s'astreindre à un traitement spécifique pour soulager les douleurs de son corps, éprouvé par sa longue carrière.
>> "Ça couine un peu": Olivier Giroud contraint de se faire des injections pour continuer à jouer
12h56
Bienvenue sur RMC Sport pour suivre le match de la 6e journée de Ligue 1 entre Lille et Le Havre. Le coup d'envoi sera donné à 17h15 au stade Pierre-Mauroy par l'arbitre Bastien Dechepy. Le Losc, 4e du classement, partira favori face à la lanterne rouge du championnat même si les Dogues restent sur une défaite face à Nice (2-1) avant la trêve internationale. De son côté, le HAC, 18e, n'a toujours pas gagné le moindre match depuis la reprise (3 défaites, deux nuls).

items.title: Richard Ferrand met en garde ceux qui, comme Marine Le Pen ou Bruno Retailleau, aimeraient faire du référendum une arme contre l’État de droit
items.summary: Nombreux sont les candidats à la présidentielle qui veulent réviser la Constitution. Certains espèrent même, s’ils sont élus dans six mois, faire de la consultation des électeurs une arme pour la contourner. Le patron des Sages leur répond.
items.body_text:
Richard Ferrand met en garde ceux qui, comme Marine Le Pen ou Bruno Retailleau, aimeraient faire du référendum une arme contre l’État de droit
Alors qu’un sondage OpinionWay pour Sciences-Po ne donne au Conseil constitutionnel que 39% de confiance, soit à peine 4 sur 10, Richard Ferrand, le président des Sages de la République, répond à Laurent Neumann, pour Quid Juris, le podcast du Club des juristes, aux critiques et emportements contre cette institution.
Selon le baromètre du Conseil constitutionnel publié en juillet 2026 (réalisé par Toluna Harris Interactive), un tiers des Français jugent qu'un régime autoritaire serait peut-être plus efficace qu'une démocratie libérale. À six ou sept mois de la présidentielle, c'est de nature à inquiéter le président du Conseil que vous êtes?
Cet élément, qui est issu effectivement du baromètre que le Conseil constitutionnel a lui-même mis en œuvre, est inquiétant. Mais il y a d'autres éléments dans cette étude qui le sont beaucoup moins. De manière paradoxale — sinon nous ne serions pas Français —, nous proclamons à plus de 95% notre attachement à la liberté d'aller et venir, à la liberté de croire ou de ne pas croire, à toutes sortes de libertés. Et à côté, on dit: quand même, il faudrait que les choses soient plus efficaces.
C'est l'occasion de lever une ambiguïté qui crée parfois du trouble. Nous sommes souvent irrités par des règles de plus en plus sophistiquées, par un accès au droit de plus en plus numérisé, par des dispositifs qui complexifient tout. On se dit: il y a donc trop de droits, c'est le droit qui m'empêche. On confond alors l'empilement des normes — que je comprends aisément et vis comme tout citoyen de notre pays — et les principes fondamentaux. Par amalgame, parfois nourri par un certain nombre de discours publics, s'installe l'idée que le droit empêcherait plus qu'il ne protège. On ne peut pas confondre les irritants du quotidien dans la relation aux administrations et les principes fondamentaux de la République.
Et parfois, on en vient à dire du Conseil constitutionnel: il m'empêche de mener l'excellente politique publique que je voulais conduire et qui aurait réglé tous les problèmes.
Marine Le Pen promet, en cas d'accession au pouvoir, un référendum sur la révision constitutionnelle. Le Conseil constitutionnel peut-il, doit-il, s'opposer à l'usage de l'article 11 pour réviser la Constitution?
Les emportements contre le Conseil constitutionnel ne sont pas vraiment nouveaux. Et puis, toute construction humaine est critiquable, y compris les décisions d'une juridiction et celles du Conseil constitutionnel. D'ailleurs, c'est nous qui protégeons l'article 11 de la Déclaration des droits de l'homme, celui relatif à la liberté d'expression: nous n'allons pas, en même temps, nous indigner que cette liberté d'expression s'exprime, fût-ce à notre détriment.
Ensuite, il est vrai que lorsqu'un pouvoir exécutif devient illibéral, il commence toujours par s'attaquer aux organes constitutionnels qui, comme disait Tocqueville, évitent la tyrannie de la majorité. Ils ne le font pas de front, d'ailleurs, mais de manière subreptice. Nous l'avons vu récemment en Pologne, où l'on a soudain bidouillé — passez-moi l'expression — l'âge obligatoire de départ à la retraite des juges pour en faire sortir certains, puis où l'on s'est gardé d'en nommer d'autres, ce qui a créé un problème de quorum: une manière de mettre à l'arrêt le fonctionnement de la cour. À l'inverse, sous la présidence de Viktor Orbán, l'idée a été de multiplier le nombre de juges, naturellement choisis sur un mode tout à fait militant, pour en quelque sorte engloutir l'indépendance des juges en place.
Ça ne lui a pas porté chance, d'ailleurs, puisqu'il a fini par perdre la direction de son pays.
C'est ce que je dis souvent: ça ne porte pas chance et ça ne dure pas longtemps. Il faut s'en réjouir. Au fond, ce que certains pouvoirs exécutifs ne supportent pas, c'est qu'il y ait des limites à l'exercice de leur pouvoir. E

items.title: Des millions de barils, un effet incertain sur les prix, l'Ukraine en colère... Quatre questions sur l'accord sur le diesel russe entre Donald Trump et Vladimir Poutine
items.summary: Le président américain a annoncé vendredi que les Etats-Unis allaient acheter du diesel produit par la Russie, pour la première fois depuis le début de la guerre en Ukraine, revenant sur les sanctions visant l'économie russe.
items.body_text:
Des millions de barils, un effet incertain sur les prix, l'Ukraine en colère... Quatre questions sur l'accord sur le diesel russe entre Donald Trump et Vladimir Poutine
Le président américain a annoncé vendredi que les Etats-Unis allaient acheter du diesel produit par la Russie, pour la première fois depuis le début de la guerre en Ukraine, revenant sur les sanctions visant l'économie russe.
On connaît le goût du président américain pour les "deals", mais celui-ci était inattendu. Donald Trump a annoncé, vendredi 9 octobre, avoir négocié avec Vladimir Poutine une livraison massive de diesel russe aux marchés américain et mondial, dans l'espoir de faire baisser les prix à la pompe à quelques semaines des élections de mi-mandat aux Etats-Unis. Cette décision, à rebours de la stratégie de sanctions américaines adoptées contre le Kremlin depuis le début de la guerre en Ukraine, a été qualifiée d'"indigne" par le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky. Franceinfo répond à quatre questions sur cet accord dévoilé après un échange téléphonique entre les dirigeants russe et américain.
1 Que prévoit cet accord sur le diesel russe ?
Le président des Etats-Unis a publié un message sur Truth Social, vendredi, pour annoncer avoir eu une "discussion très fructueuse" avec Vladimir Poutine. "La Russie va immédiatement fournir plus de 300 000 tonnes de diesel au marché américain et mondial, 500 000 tonnes de plus en novembre et 1 000 000 de tonnes immédiatement après. De plus, selon l'état de ses raffineries, la Russie livrera ensuite, dans une courte période de temps, 3 000 000 de tonnes de diesel", a-t-il ajouté. Soit un objectif total de 1,8 million de tonnes de diesel mises en vente cet automne-hiver, et 3 millions supplémentaires à une échéance non précisée. "La partie russe a réaffirmé sa volonté de fournir du pétrole et des produits pétroliers aux marchés américain et mondial", a ensuite déclaré le Kremlin, confirmant les chiffres avancés par Donald Trump.
Dans la foulée, le ministère des Finances américain a publié une licence intitulée "Autorisation des transactions liées à la vente, à la livraison, au déchargement et à l'importation de carburant diesel originaire de la Fédération de Russie". Elle prévoit une exception aux sanctions contre les exportations russes d'hydrocarbures, mises en place depuis l'invasion de l'Ukraine en février 2022. Le Congrès américain avait d'ailleurs durci en septembre les mesures visant les acheteurs de produits pétroliers russes, afin d'amoindrir la capacité de financement militaire du Kremlin. Elles sont désormais levées pour le diesel, jusqu'au 7 avril 2027.
2 Comment Donald Trump justifie-t-il cet accord ?
Sur son réseau social, le président américain promet que les prix du diesel aux Etats-Unis et dans le monde "vont baisser, avec des chiffres record, et vite". "Des prix plus bas pour les Américains, et en particulier nos grands fermiers, ranchers, et chauffeurs routiers, sont ma plus grande priorité", assure-t-il. Depuis les premières frappes américaines en Iran, en février, les tensions au Moyen-Orient et le blocage du détroit d'Ormuz ont fait grimper les prix du carburant. Celui du diesel a doublé aux Etats-Unis, dépassant pour la première fois les 6 dollars le gallon en septembre [environ 1,4 euro le litre], selon les données de la Banque fédérale de réserve de Saint-Louis aux Etats-Unis.
Or le président républicain est en difficulté à l'approche des élections législatives de mi-mandat, les midterms, le 3 novembre. Le Parti républicain redoute de perdre le contrôle du Congrès lors de ces élections, dont le résultat aura un impact sur la deuxième moitié du mandat de Donald Trump. Sans soutien du Parlement, le président américain risquerait de voir certaines de ses nominations bloquées ou les requêtes législatives se multiplier contre lui.
"C'est la même échéance des midterms qui a poussé Donald Trump à soutenir la libération de 100 millions de barils par le G7", rappelle auprès de franceinfo Patric

Après une semaine agitée dans l'Éducation nationale, marquée par deux grandes journées de contestation lycéenne, des blocus et la participation de certains étudiants, quelles seront les conséquences de la mobilisation lors de la dernière semaine avant les vacances de la Toussaint ? À Paris, une vingtaine d'établissements réunissent collège et lycée au sein de cités scolaires ; dans l'une d'entre elles, le collège-lycée Voltaire, dans l'est de la capitale, les collégiens n'ont presque pas eu cours cette semaine.
Vendredi matin, Matthieu accompagne son fils Thomas, élève de 6e, devant le collège-lycée. "Je pense qu'il a manqué au moins cinq jours de cours pour l'instant", constate son père. À la maison, le petit garçon a tué le temps comme il a pu. "La plupart du temps, je lisais, des fois je faisais des devoirs, comme les profs en donnaient en plus, et des fois je faisais des jeux vidéo", raconte Thomas.
Lycéens et collégiens, même combat ?
Ce vendredi matin, les lycéens se sont entendus pour que les petits puissent aller en classe. "Ils ont fini par laisser entrer les collégiens. Je pense que c'est une bonne chose, que ça ne peut que servir leur mobilisation, d'autant que les collégiens n'ont pas la même autonomie que les ados qui sont au lycée", estime Matthieu.
Content que la situation s'apaise, au moins pour une journée, il soutient totalement le mouvement lycéen. Lui-même est professeur dans une université, elle aussi bloquée. "C'est des problèmes endémiques depuis des années, en fait. On considère mal les enseignants, on profite de notre bonne volonté, toutes ces réformes qu'on nous impose et qu'on applique..."
"On ne demande pas l'avis aux enseignants, nous qui serions les mieux placés pour savoir ce qu'il faut mettre en place."

"Je suis en 5e, on a raté plusieurs cours", témoigne une collégienne. Lorsqu'on leur demande s'ils soutiennent la mobilisation, ils acquiescent : "Oui, bien sûr !" "En fait, les lycéens, ils ont de mauvaises conditions de travail, donc ils font un blocus pour obtenir des droits !", explique une collégienne. Et lorsqu'on lui demande ce qu'elle en pense, elle répond : "C'est gentil, pour les générations d'après."
"Il faut une égalité pour tout le monde"
Des collégiens solidaires, comme Suzon, la fille de Marie, qui vient d'entrer en 6e. "On en parle : elle a même fait un bout de manif mardi avec sa copine et les parents de sa copine", raconte-t-elle. "Moi, je trouve ça super bien que la jeunesse d'aujourd'hui, dont on dit qu'elle est complètement accro aux écrans et à TikTok, se lève pour son futur, ses besoins, et je trouve ça super important !"
Elle aimerait tout de même que cela n'empêche pas les plus petits d'aller en classe, comme dans cette cité scolaire où tous les niveaux sont réunis. "Le problème, c'est qu'il y a une différence de traitement entre les collégiens qui ne sont pas dans les lycées et ceux qui sont dans les cités scolaires comme ça et qui n'ont pas accès aux cours. items.body_text:
"Les larmes suivent la pesanteur maintenant" : l'astronaute Sophie Adenot prononce un émouvant discours après son retour sur la terre ferme
La Française peinait encore à tenir debout, samedi, deux jours après son amerrissage dans les eaux du Pacifique. Mais elle avait suffisamment d'énergie pour lancer un appel à l'unité, depuis le tarmac de l'aéroport de Cologne.
Emue et fatiguée. La Française Sophie Adenot a prononcé ses premières paroles en public, samedi 10 octobre à Cologne (Allemagne), deux jours après son amerrissage au large de la Californie. "J'ai traversé tout le spectre des émotions humaines", a-t-elle notamment déclaré sur le tarmac de l'aéroport, peu après son atterrissage en Europe. "J'étais en orbite autour de la Terre et maintenant je me retrouve avec les pieds sur Terre", a-t-elle souri, tout en soulignant qu'il était encore difficile pour elle de se tenir debout.
Une période de repos plus longue lui avait été accordée à Houston, a précisé l'Agence spatiale européenne (ESA), afin qu'elle puisse entamer "la dernière et aussi la plus longue étape de son voyage de retour vers l'Europe". "Je n'ai pas pu faire le vol transatlantique avant d'être stabilisée", a commenté Sophie Adenot, soutenue par deux médecins de l'ESA, David Kim et Bimba Hoyer.
Elle a évoqué une "mission pleine de joie", sans cacher des moments plus difficiles. Le discours de la Française a été interrompu à plusieurs reprises par des larmes d'émotion. "Les larmes suivent la pesanteur maintenant, je n'en avais plus l'habitude", a-t-elle plaisanté. "Je suis allée dans l'espace pleine de rêves, et je suis revenue pleine de gratitude", a-t-elle ajouté, saluant "ce sens de l'unité entre les personnes qui ont décidé d'être unies". A 400 km de la Terre, il n'y a "pas de divisions, pas de frontières" et l'on voit "juste une précieuse planète que nous partageons tous".
Sophie Adenot avait amerri jeudi au large de la Californie, après plus de 27 heures de voyage à bord de la capsule Dragon. Les dernières minutes de vol ont offert à la Française, aux deux Américains Jessica Meir et Jack Hathaway et au Russe Andreï Fediaïev d'ultimes sensations fortes, avec une traversée de l'atmosphère à toute vitesse puis leur ralentissement par de puissants parachutes, le tout avec une coupure des communications.

items.title: Markets digest bank earnings after recent turmoil
items.body_text:
Stocks slid Friday after a slate of earnings beats from big banks fueled concerns that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its next two meetings.
    
            Still, the major indices gained for the week. The Dow rose 400 points, or 1.2%. The S&P 500 gained 0.8% and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.3%.
    
            JPMorgan Chase on Friday reported first-quarter profit and revenue that crushed expectations, boosted by the Fed’s interest rate hiking campaign. Citigroup, Wells Fargo and PNC Financial also reported strong results.
    
            CEO Jamie Dimon warned investors in the company’s post-earnings conference call that they should prepare for interest rates to be higher for longer than expected.
    
            Wall Street seems to have taken note. Analysts increased their bets on a quarter-point rate hike at the Fed’s meeting in May and another in June.
    
            Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said Friday that the central bank needs to continue tightening monetary policy, further weighing down markets.
    
            Austan Goolsbee, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, said that it’s “definitely” possible the United States enters a mild recession after the tumult in banking last month.
    
            Meanwhile, retail sales data declined more than expected, suggesting that Americans’ spending power and the US economy are weakening.
    
            Consumer sentiment held fairly steady in April, even as concerns about a recession linger, according to the University of Michigan’s latest monthly survey.
    
            “There was too much news to digest this morning, but the key takeaway is that the Fed has room to do more harm,” Edward Moya, senior market analyst at OANDA, said in a note.
    
            The Dow slipped 144 points, or 0.4%.
    
            The S&P 500 tumbled 0.2%.
    
            The Nasdaq Composite sank 0.4%.
    
            As stocks settle after the trading day, levels might still change slightly.
items.normalised_title: markets digest bank earnings after recent turmoil

items.title: Still haven't filed your taxes? Here's what you need to know
items.summary: So far this tax season, the IRS has received more than 90 million income tax returns for 2022.
items.body_text:
So far this tax season, the IRS has received more than 100 million income tax returns for 2022.
That means tens of millions of households have yet to file their returns. If yours is among them, here are some last-minute tax-filing tips to keep in mind as the Tuesday, April 18 deadline approaches.
Not everyone has to file on April 18: If you live in a federally declared disaster area, have a business there — or have relevant tax documents stored by businesses in that area — it’s likely the IRS has already extended the filing and payment deadlines for you. Here is where you can find the specific extension dates for each disaster area.
Thanks to many rounds of extreme weather in recent months, for instance, tax filers in most of California — which accounts for 10% to 15% of all federal filers — have already been granted an extension until Oct. 16 to file and to pay, according to an IRS spokesperson.
If you’re in the armed forces and are currently or were recently stationed in a combat zone, the filing and payment deadlines for your 2022 taxes are most likely extended by 180 days. But your specific extended filing and payment deadlines will depend on the day you leave (or left) the combat zone. This IRS publication offers more detail.
Lastly, if you made little to no money last year (typically less than $12,950 for single filers and $25,900 for married couples), you may not be required to file a return. But you may want to anyway if you think you are eligible for a refund thanks to, for instance, refundable tax credits such as the Earned Income Tax Credit. (Use this IRS tool to gauge whether you are required to file this year.) You also are likely eligible to use IRS Free File (intended for those with adjusted gross income of $73,000 or less) so it won’t cost you to submit a return.
Your paycheck may not be your only source of income: If you had one full-time job you may think that is the only income you made and have to report. But that’s not necessarily so.
Other potentially taxable and reportable income sources include:
- Interest on your savings
- Investment income (e.g., dividends and capital gains)
- Pay for part-time or seasonal work, or a side hustle
- Unemployment income
- Social Security benefits or distribution from a retirement account
- Tips
- Gambling winnings
- Income from a rental property you own
Organize your tax documents: By now you should have received every tax document that third parties are required to send you (your employer, bank, brokerage, etc.).
If you don’t recall receiving a hard copy of a tax form in the mail, check your email and your online accounts — a document may have been sent to you electronically.
Here are some of the tax forms you may have received:
- W-2 from your wage or salaried jobs
- 1099-B for capital gains and losses on your investments
- 1099-DIV from your brokerage or company where you own stock for dividends or other distributions from their investments
- 1099-INT for interest over $10 on your savings at a financial institution
- 1099-NEC from your clients, if you worked as a contractor
- 1099-K for payments for goods and services through third-party platforms like Venmo, CashApp or Etsy. The 1099-K is required if you made more than $20,000 in over 200 transactions during the year. (Next year the reporting threshold drops to $600.) But even if you didn’t get a 1099-K you still must report all the income that you made over third-party platforms in 2022.
- 1099-Rs for distributions over $10 that you received for a pension, annuity, retirement account, profit-sharing plan or insurance contract
- SSA-1099 or SSA-1042S for Social Security benefits received.
“Be aware that there’s no form for some taxable income, like proceeds from renting out your vacation property, meaning you’re responsible for reporting it on your own,” according to the Illinois CPA Society.

items.title: Retail spending fell in March as consumers pull back
items.summary: Spending at US retailers fell in March as consumers pulled back amid recessionary fears fueled by the banking crisis.
items.body_text:
Spending at US retailers fell in March as consumers pulled back after the banking crisis fueled recession fears.
Retail sales, which are adjusted for seasonality but not for inflation, fell by 1% in March from the prior month, the Commerce Department reported on Friday. That was steeper than an expected 0.4% decline, according to Refinitiv, and above the revised 0.2% decline in the prior month.
Investors chalk up some of the weakness to a lack of tax returns and concerns about a slowing labor market. The IRS issued $84 billion in tax refunds this March, about $25 billion less than they issued in March of 2022, according to BofA analysts.
That led consumers to pull back in spending at department stores and on durable goods, such as appliances and furniture. Spending at general merchandise stores fell 3% in March from the prior month and spending at gas stations declined 5.5% during the same period. Excluding gas station sales, retail spending retreated 0.6% in March from February.
However, retail spending rose 2.9% year-over-year.
The effect of smaller tax returns
Smaller tax returns likely played a role in last month’s decline in retail sales, along with the expiration of enhanced food assistance benefits, economists say.
“March is a really important month for refunds. Some folks might have been expecting something similar to last year,” Aditya Bhave, senior US economist at BofA Global Research, told CNN.
Credit and debit card spending per household tracked by Bank of America researchers moderated in March to its slowest pace in more than two years, which was likely the result of smaller returns and expired benefits, coupled with slowing wage growth.
Enhanced pandemic-era benefits provided through the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program expired in February, which might have also held back spending in March, according to a Bank of America Institute report.
A slowing labor market
Average hourly earnings grew 4.2% in March from a year earlier, down from the prior month’s annualized 4.6% increase and the smallest annual rise since June 2021, according to figures from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The Employment Cost Index, a more comprehensive measure of wages, has also shown that worker pay gains have moderated this past year. ECI data for the first quarter of this year will be released later this month.
Still, the US labor market remains solid, even though it has lost momentum recently. That could hold up consumer spending in the coming months, said Michelle Meyer, North America chief economist at Mastercard Economics Institute.
“The big picture is still favorable for the consumer when you think about their income growth, their balance sheet and the health of the labor market,” Meyer said.
Employers added 236,000 jobs in March, a robust gain by historical standards but smaller than the average monthly pace of job growth in the prior six months, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The latest monthly Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, or JOLTS report, showed that the number of available jobs remained elevated in February — but was down more than 17% from its peak of 12 million in March 2022, and revised data showed that weekly claims for US unemployment benefits were higher than previously reported.
The job market could cool further in the coming months. Economists at the Federal Reserve expect the US economy to head into a recession later in the year as the lagged effects of higher interest rates take a deeper hold. Fed economists had forecast subdued growth, with risks of a recession, prior to the collapses of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank.
For consumers, the effects of last month’s turbulence in the banking industry have been limited so far. Consumer sentiment tracked by the University of Michigan worsened slightly in March during the bank failures, but it had already shown signs of deteriorating before then.

items.title: Inside the protest playbook to vilify Israel on 'global day of action'
items.summary: Global Alliance for Palestine distributed a detailed playbook urging groups to shut down city squares and blockade corporate hubs across continents.
items.body_text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – As demonstrators, including the headline-grabbing CodePink agitators, descend on the nation's capital late Saturday afternoon for a "coordinated global day of action" against Israel, they will join a worldwide wave of marches and planned disruptions that may appear to be unfolding independently.
In Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, on Friday, anti-Israel demonstrators carried signs deploying emotionally charged language against Israel, including one featuring a Palestinian flag and a bloodied hand with the message, "STOP GENOCIDE." Nearby, two women carrying mock machine guns flanked a cardboard image of a handcuffed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with a noose around his neck.
But a Fox News Digital investigation has found that, long before the first demonstrators gathered, the messages for the protest's "communications framing" and transnational action plan had already been written, the banners designed, the tactics circulated and the media strategy laid out to "turn public outrage into collective leverage."
The campaign documents reveal that coalition organizers instructed participating groups to direct protesters to "shut down city squares," "encircle government buildings" and "blockade complicit corporate hubs."
The document declares, "This is not a symbolic march and not a routine protest."
Fox News Digital identified 179 organizations in the coalition, while an interactive Google Map published by the network lists 322 events scheduled across three days through Sunday. They include a rally on an "Intifada Trail" in Saint John, New Brunswick, Canada, a protest in Bangladesh by the "Bangladesh Intifada Youth Collection" and actions in South Africa by "Social Intifada." All three use "intifada," a term associated with Palestinian uprisings against Israel, including periods marked by deadly terrorist attacks. Activists describe the term as a call for resistance.
The global coordination illustrates how contemporary protest movements combine international leadership, local activist networks, standardized visual branding, emotionally charged messaging and traditional news outreach into a single mobilization infrastructure in which professional political organizing amplifies the sincerely held convictions of individual demonstrators.
LAWMAKERS THROW OUT 'TROJAN HORSE' ACTIVISTS THEY SAY ARE ENGAGED IN AMERICAN SUBVERSION
Among the participating organizations is CodePink, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that has received $1.33 million from Neville Roy Singham, a Shanghai-based tech tycoon who has funneled $278 million into a network of nonprofits under scrutiny by the House Ways and Means Committee and its chairman, Rep. Jason Smith, over allegations that some operate as "Trojan horses" and proxies for the Chinese Communist Party and other malign foreign interests. CodePink and other organizations under scrutiny have denied wrongdoing.
Two days ago, CodePink co-founder Medea Benjamin and D.C. coordinator Olivia DiNucci dispatched a letter to members, directing them to join the "Feminist Contingent" at the Library of Congress for the "global day of action."
"And don't forget to WEAR PINK!" they noted.
The network's connections were also visible last week, when CodePink co-founder Jodie Evans, who married Singham in 2017, joined an anti-Israel protest in New York City, marching behind a band of activists from Revolutionary Communists of America as they chanted, "Long live the intifada."
Evans told Fox News Digital Singham supports CodePink's efforts and the "amazing work" nonprofits are doing to "stand up when violent things are happening."
Taken together, the documents reveal a coordinated protest and influence campaign spanning continents, combining accusations of Israeli "genocide," attacks on the news media, workplace and university walkouts, blockades, political lobbying and carefully orchestrated publicity.

items.title: France is devouring itself as school riots reveal a crisis far bigger than broken classrooms
items.summary: France student protests over crumbling schools expose deep tensions as Jean-Luc Mélenchon's La France Insoumise allegedly exploits the growing unrest.
items.body_text:
Student protests over crumbling schools despite billions in public spending are fueling a broader crisis in France, as experts warn that the country's mounting financial troubles, President Emmanuel Macron's weakened political center and radical movements are pushing the unrest far beyond its original educational grievances.
Simone Rodan-Benzaquen, the Foundation for Defense of Democracies' senior envoy for Europe, told Fox News Digital in an interview from Paris that what began in September with legitimate complaints about school conditions has increasingly been exploited by political forces seeking confrontation with the state.
"Overall I'd say the anger is real but the violence I would say is organized," she said, adding that destroying schools would do nothing to improve the education system.
FRANCE EXPLODES AGAIN AS STUDENTS RIOT OVER EDUCATION
Seventy-two percent of education expenditure went toward salaries, social contributions and pensions for teaching and non-teaching personnel, while just 8.5% went toward investment, including infrastructure and equipment. The figures cover the entire education system, not just high schools, according to France's Education Ministry's 2026 statistical overview.
Harvey Feigenbaum, a professor of political science and international affairs at George Washington University and an expert on French politics, told Fox News Digital that France's underlying problem is a government caught between expensive social commitments, sluggish economic growth and mounting pressure to cut spending.
"France is in deep debt. It wants to cut its expenses," Feigenbaum said, explaining that years of financial pressure and neglected school facilities have fueled frustration among students.
The scale of the financial predicament is striking. According to Eurostat, French public debt stood at 117.6% of GDP in the first quarter of 2026, the third-highest ratio in the European Union, behind Greece and Italy.
Reuters reported October 8 that rising borrowing costs and investor concerns have severely limited the government's ability to resolve unrest through additional spending, a strategy employed during previous waves of French protests.
The financial squeeze has collided with an increasingly fragmented political system, creating opportunities for parties at both ends of the political spectrum to capitalize on public dissatisfaction.
FRENCH SCHOOL RIOTS DEEPEN AS EXPERTS POINT TO FAR-LEFT ALLIANCE FUELING ‘BROADER CONFRONTATION’
Macron's political center collapses
For Feigenbaum, the long-term roots of the crisis lie in Macron's political legacy.
When Macron won the presidency in 2017, he promised to move beyond France's traditional left-right divide, combining policies from both sides into a new centrist political movement.
But Feigenbaum argues that the strategy produced an unintended consequence: weakening France's established moderate parties without creating a durable governing coalition to replace them.
"What he ended up doing was attracting the moderate voters from the parties of the moderate left and the parties from the moderate right, and essentially destroyed those parties," Feigenbaum said.
He argued that the collapse of the traditional political center helped create space for more ideologically polarized movements. "Macron is a smart man, but he's a terrible politician," the professor added.
Macron's controversial pension reforms illustrate the difficulty of persuading French voters to accept reductions in longstanding public benefits, Feigenbaum argued. Those efforts triggered widespread protests, while implementation of the 2023 retirement changes has since been suspended until 2028.
The situation became especially difficult after Macron called snap parliamentary elections in 2024, producing a deeply divided National Assembly without a governing majority.
"Even if the government wanted to do something coherent, they simply don't have the votes to do it," Feigenbaum said.

items.title: Massive 7.7 magnitude earthquake strikes Panama as officials investigate potential tsunami threat
items.summary: A powerful earthquake struck Panama's southern coast Friday, prompting officials to investigate a possible tsunami threat after the USGS lowered its magnitude estimate from 8.0 to 7.7.
items.body_text:
A powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck off Panama's southern coast Friday, shaking the country's capital as officials investigated a potential tsunami threat.
The U.S. Geological Survey initially measured the earthquake at magnitude 8.0 before lowering its estimate to 7.7. The quake struck at 1:56 p.m. ET, at a depth of 7.8 miles, near Pitaloza Arriba, Panama.
A 5.5 magnitude aftershock followed, with its epicenter approximately 50 miles east of the initial earthquake.
The Panama Canal said operations were continuing normally following Friday's earthquake, with emergency protocols activated and technical teams inspecting facilities for possible damage. Canal officials said their priority was ensuring the safety of workers, vessels, crews and nearby communities as assessments continued.
The earthquake was felt in Panama City and in San José, the capital of neighboring Costa Rica, according to Reuters.
Tsunami officials warned that waves reaching 3 to 10 feet above tide levels were possible along some coastal areas of Panama, while parts of Ecuador could experience waves of approximately 1 to 3 feet.
Smaller tsunami waves of less than 1 foot above tide levels were forecast for coastal areas of Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Mexico, Nicaragua and Peru.
COLOMBIA BUILDING COLLAPSES ON CAMERA AS EARTHQUAKE BRINGS DEATH, DESTRUCTION
Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino said in a series of posts on X that he was visiting areas affected by Friday's earthquake and coordinating emergency assistance with government officials.
Mulino said he had ordered the mobilization of personnel, resources and aid for affected communities, along with structural assessments to determine the extent of the damage. He also thanked neighboring countries for their support and said assistance from the Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean (CAF) would go toward helping those affected.
The president said he was traveling through Penonomé with government officials to coordinate relief efforts and thanked the United States and other countries for their offers of assistance.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a Friday post on X that the State Department was rapidly mobilizing resources and personnel to assist Panama at the request of the Panamanian government. Rubio said the U.S. was closely monitoring the earthquake and directed Americans needing assistance to the department's 24-hour consular hotline at +1-202-501-4444 from abroad or +1-888-407-4747 from the U.S. and Canada.
The U.S. Embassy in Panama also said it was assessing potential damage and working to account for the safety and whereabouts of visitors and personnel. In a separate X post, the embassy urged Americans in Panama to enroll in the State Department's Smart Traveler Enrollment Program at STEP.State.gov and follow its social media accounts for updates.
Despite the potential danger to coastal communities near the earthquake, officials said a Pacific-wide tsunami was not expected.
Earthquakes measuring between 7.0 and 7.9 can cause serious damage, according to Michigan Technological University.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Information about possible damage or casualties from Friday's earthquake was not immediately available.

items.title: A year of ceasefire in Gaza through the lens of NPR's reporter
items.summary: It has been one year since Hamas released the remaining Israeli hostages and President Trump promised an end to the war, but Palestinians say the past 12 months have been a ceasefire in name only.
items.body_text:
NPR's Anas Baba captures one year of ceasefire in Gaza : The Picture ShowIt has been one year since Hamas released the remaining Israeli hostages and President Trump promised an end to the war, but Palestinians say the past 12 months have been a ceasefire in name only.
A Palestinian mother mourns her son, who was killed in an Israeli airstrike just over a month into the ceasefire, at Al-Shifa Hospital, in Gaza City, on Nov. 20, 2025.
Anas Baba/NPR

Anas Baba/NPR
Editor's note: This story contains graphic images of violence and death.
GAZA STRIP — President Donald Trump promised an end to Israel's war in Gaza after he pushed Israel to agree to a ceasefire and Hamas to release remaining Israeli hostages. The deal came into effect on Oct. 10, 2025.
A year later, however, there's still no international peacekeeping force in Gaza as promised and no reconstruction. Instead, Israel's military has expanded its control to roughly 70% of Gaza, squeezing more than 2 million Palestinians near the sea's edge.
Israel has also continued targeting Hamas throughout the ceasefire. Those attacks have killed more than 1,400 Palestinians this past year, nearly 500 of them women and children, according to Gaza's Health Ministry.
Although the bombings have not stopped, they have slowed down during the ceasefire.
That has given people in Gaza a chance to recover from what U.N.-backed experts declared was a famine in the north of the territory last year. More food is now entering, reversing starvation across Gaza.
NPR's reporter in Gaza, Anas Baba, has been capturing moments of respite and continuous grief over the past 12 months of the ceasefire. Below are a selection of his photos.

items.title: India cracks down on youth protests as anger grows against Modi and election chief
items.summary: Indian authorities have launched a major security crackdown in New Delhi, detaining thousands of protesters who intended to hold a mass demonstration against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.
items.body_text:
India cracks down on youth protests as anger grows against Modi and election chief
Indian authorities deployed a sweeping security crackdown across New Delhi and detained thousands of protesters Saturday as India's youth "Cockroach" movement sought to intensify a nationwide campaign against a contentious voter list revision that has fueled anger at Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Hindu nationalist government and election authorities.
Police intercepted demonstrators before they could reach Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in the heart of India's capital, chasing off some and detaining many others. Some were dragged away before being bundled into police vehicles and taken to temporary detention centers. Several "Cockroach" movement leaders were detained before arriving, effectively crippling the protest ahead of its start.
The crackdown extended beyond the protest venue, with police stopping buses, cars and other vehicles at checkpoints on routes into the capital and searching for demonstrators.
Jantar Mantar was barricaded, while anti-riot vehicles equipped with tear gas launchers were stationed along key routes. Restrictions on mobile internet and access to parts of the city added to the hurdles facing protesters.
Police said Friday they had denied permission for the protest because the request was submitted late.
The scale of the crackdown underscored the authorities' determination to disrupt a fast-growing protest campaign that has mobilized thousands of young people, drawn opposition support and intensified scrutiny of Modi. The protests also come at a politically sensitive time, months after demonstrations led by the "Cockroach" movement over exam paper leaks forced Modi's education minister to resign in July.
Police detain leaders and tighten grip around protest site
Leaders of the "Cockroach" movement Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were expected to be at the forefront of the protest, were detained after arriving at Delhi airport from Mumbai on Saturday. A video shared by the "Cockroach Janta Party" on X showed police boarding the aircraft and detaining the three men.
"The pre-planned interception by Delhi Police aims to cripple the leadership of today's peaceful demonstrations before they even reach the protest site," the movement said in a statement.
Loudspeakers around the protest site warned that gatherings of five or more people were banned in parts of New Delhi, as authorities imposed sweeping security restrictions rarely seen in the capital. Journalists also faced restrictions in some areas.
Some protesters nevertheless broke through police cordons, chanting slogans against Modi and election authorities before being detained.
"We are a democracy, yet peaceful protests are being crushed by force. Shouldn't we fight for our rights," said Tanya Negi, a college student who traveled from Mumbai with two friends and arrived early Saturday. "Why is Modi afraid of India's young people?"
The crackdown drew criticism from opposition leaders, who accused the government of curbing dissent.
"Is there a democracy in this country? A total siege over the city. Citizens are being driven out," opposition lawmaker John Brittas told The Associated Press.
India's voter list dispute raises election fairness concerns
The protests center on India's Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision, which the opposition says has disenfranchised millions of eligible voters. Protesters demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and an end to the change, which has removed more than 130 million names from voter lists so far.
The Election Commission and the government reject allegations of voter manipulation, saying the revision is intended to eliminate duplicate and ineligible entries.
The dispute has become a rallying point for opposition parties seeking to challenge Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
Saturday's planned demonstration follows days of protests in the Indian cap

The “Cornell 7” case has reignited a longstanding debate about consent, sexual regret, and #MeToo, roiling the already tense dynamic between the sexes to an extent they may never recover. While much outrage has centered on the young men’s alleged behaviors, which were indeed egregious, we must hold young women to the same standard.
Jane Doe’s lawsuit, which alleges she was plied with drugs and alcohol and sexually assaulted for several hours by seven fraternity brothers, has spurred a new wave of activism on Cornell’s campus and online. Women have taken to social media in solidarity, posting videos with the caption, “I Am Jane Doe,” or, “We Are All Jane Doe,” to act as decoys to protect Doe’s anonymity. Some users have shared their own stories of being sexually abused or assaulted in the context of date rape.
As unfortunate and tragic as these disclosures are, these women share little in common with Jane Doe, who says she was coerced into group sex. More importantly, Doe’s own actions point to her sexual experience being consensual.
A woman who has been sexually assaulted does not text her attacker afterward to tell him that she loves him and will use violence to defend him, or that “none of the sexual stuff was illegal.”
It was only after Doe suffered reputational damage from gossip spreading around campus and the fraternity disinvited her from an upcoming party, that her tone changed and she went to the police.
What led Doe to make decisions that were — to any objective observer — not in her best interest, and then, instead of reflecting on them, double down and blame everyone else involved? My answer is: sex positivity. And the sooner young women reject this way of thinking, the better off they will be.
Doe showed up to the fraternity house, by herself, at nearly midnight to meet a male friend to whom she was attracted. The male friend asked if she’d be interested in having a threesome, to which she agreed before ascertaining whom the second male partner would be.
After consensually consuming alcohol and ketamine, by her own admission, Doe swapped in new male partners as necessary to facilitate multiple threesomes. When one of the accused men appeared concerned upon entering the bedroom, Doe told him, “This was normal in the medieval times.”
Sex positivity tells women to lead with their sexuality. Popular female podcasters, influencers, and mainstream sex educators tell young women that sexual permissiveness and open-mindedness are the way to a man’s heart. They advise women to have sex on the first date, and if a man can’t handle a woman’s high “body count,” he’s insecure and unworthy of her time.
Pair that with early exposure to pornography, and it’s no wonder so many young women are confused about what healthy sexual values look like and don’t believe they have the right to demand respect from themselves and their partners.
A man who is genuinely interested in a woman isn’t going to proposition her to have sex with him and his friends. Men have a hard-wired aversion to female promiscuity because it obscures the paternity of potential offspring. It would be a complete waste of a man’s resources and effort to invest in raising a child, only to find out later he isn’t the father.
If a woman agrees to sleep with multiple men without knowing anything about them, not only does this increase a man’s likelihood of being cuckolded, but it also leads him to question her judgment. She thereby becomes less attractive as a potential girlfriend and wife.
A man will typically invest little in a woman he deems promiscuous and will, quite frankly, treat her as a “sex doll,” as Doe succinctly observed.
Research shows that women are more likely to experience regret and feeling used after casual sex. Women are also more likely to be shamed by both sexes for promiscuity.

Weekend Plans is our exclusive lifestyle feature where we highlight the real off-duty routines of the most exciting people in culture.
This weekend, actor and producer Kevin Sorbo — who electrified audiences around the world by slaying monsters while wearing leather pants and a muscle shirt for the hit TV series “Hercules: The Legendary Journeys” — lends his time to The Daily Wire to discuss why he thinks every movie is faith-based, his winning philosophy on choosing your path, and why even the varsity football star should never write off high school drama class.
* * *
Kevin Sorbo enters our chat with an energized flurry. He’s been doing press for one of his latest projects, the faith-based feature “Elijah Peel,” in which he plays the semi-cynical, seasoned talent manager to a drug-addled rock star on the road to redemption. At 68, having spent most of his life in the biz, Kevin lends a certain industry greasiness to the role. It’s not his first rodeo.
“I tell people all the time I’m a 13-year overnight success,” Kevin laughs. “I know what it’s like in Hollywood. Rejection is part of the norm.”
He’s certainly no stranger to controversy, either. Kevin is often portrayed as a Hollywood outcast who ruffles feathers by speaking out on his faith and values. He was “canceled” before it was cool and dropped by his agent and manager at the height of his career. Even though the tide may finally be shifting, as far as Kevin’s concerned, he’s always been himself. A Christian since childhood, he unwittingly disrupted a system that demanded upending. Getting dragged for it on X doesn’t change the fact that some tables need to be flipped.
But Kevin managed to forge an exciting path running parallel to the mainstream, and that path has brought him riches beyond a box office take. With the founding of his own production company Sorbo Studios, he could finally tell the kind of positive stories the whole family could watch. And collaborations with other boutique production houses, like the upcoming “Eating with the Enemy” — a biblical depiction of the Last Supper, which Kevin narrates — only beefs up his ever-expanding portfolio.
As we speak, he’s still babying the knee he recently had replaced. Somehow that hasn’t kept him from his golf game, his gym sessions, or his jet-setting itinerary. He’s about to head out with his wife on another tour of Israel — an immersive experience they open up to the public. “We’ve had atheists and agnostics come on the trip because they don’t deny there was a person named Jesus,” he says. “If you love history, come to Israel. It’s amazing and you’ll have a blast.”
If you see a guy zipping around Florida in a golf cart, blasting Led Zeppelin, it’s probably Kevin — one of those Hollywood outlaws on the hunt for the good kind of trouble.
New roots
He’s a Minnesota native, but Kevin spent the majority of his career in Los Angeles working as a model and leading hit TV series such as “Hercules” and “Andromeda,” along with a deep roster of movies. But after spending over three decades in Tinseltown, he wanted something more.
“We escaped in January of 2019,” Kevin phrases it. “We live in the free state of Florida and we love it here. I don’t miss the taxes and the traffic. I don’t miss the majority of the people.” But some relics of his SoCal chapter still pull on his heartstrings. “I miss some of my dear friends that are still there suffering. I miss the house I lived in.” He’s talking about his Mediterranean villa with the pool, spa, and gym, along with miles of fruit trees and a million-dollar view.
“I miss the weather,” he adds. Once he finds out I left LA too, he asks if I also relocated to Florida. I’m in Nashville — “the other one,” I say, noting the popular destination for California expats including buddies of Kevin’s, like actors Kirk Cameron and Gary Sinise.

items.summary: HBO’s new television series “Lanterns” is revealing to a broader audience the limits of the superhero genre. items.body_text:
HBO’s new television series “Lanterns” is revealing to a broader audience the limits of the superhero genre. The show tries to capture the spirit of the first season of “True Detective” (perfect television) while being shackled to Green Lantern’s expectations. Put those aesthetics on Batman or The Question, and it would work; slap them on a cosmic superhero whose power is fueled by imagination and a magic ring, and they begin to break under the weight of expectation.
The show is dour, but uplifted by a cast whose charisma tends to break what the script asks the viewer to believe and think. Kyle Chandler is obviously magnetic and shakes off any negative connotations some writers wanted to saddle the character with (old, racist, privileged, etc.; roll the clip). John Stewart is played well by Aaron Pierre and is given the reverse problem from Chandler: we are told he’s going to be great at the job, but his actions tend to say otherwise. It’s an odd framing for a story ostensibly about a superhero who comes with lots of baggage and expectations. Nathan Fillion’s Guy Gardner at least feels like he’s playing in the same sandbox his source material requires.
This problem of missing expectations and weighing down heroes with such bleak, morally dubious problems and decisions is something of a hallmark of Tom King. Since his rise to prominence in the comics scene, he has been handed the reins to many a superhero property. King is a good writer; his stories are generally well received (except, of course, from his extremely vocal critics who think he single-handedly waged the war in Iraq); it’s just that his stories tend to be ill-suited to the expectations of the superhero genre.
In this interview, King namechecks his, and the writers’ room’s, desire to fit in the film noir aesthetic, removed from the old Hollywood code where ill deeds must go punished. However, film noir and Green Lantern are clearly poor bedmates. Gabriel Hardman’s “Green Lantern: Earth One” was cited as a reference for the show – and while aesthetically the book is darker and grimmer, it still primarily happens in outer space, the fantastical exists, and ultimately Hal Jordan and the Lanterns prove they can do heroic stuff. The rings are used (though admittedly with less of the imaginative constructs and more “energy blast” stuff), and while they’re suffering from low power, they still work.
The issue with King’s writing and themes in the TV world is that his styling is finally running up against budget limitations. When paired with artists like Greg Smallwood on “Human Target,” Doc Shaner and Mitch Gerards on “Strange Adventures,” and Mitch Gerards again on “Mister Miracle” (these three being the closest analog tonally to “Lanterns”), the dour writing is buoyed by colorful, exciting visuals, even when the staging can become mundane (see the relatively low dynamics in “Mister Miracle” compared to the Jack Kirby high dynamism source material). Those visuals are entirely absent from “Lanterns”, the suits are drab, the power use is limited, this isn’t the big space opera stuff that is expected from the character.
King tends to mine the hero for guilt and regret, rather than heroics. His take on Adam Strange is a compromised man who ended up in over his head, making sacrifices that he couldn’t handle; His Mister Miracle is suffering from crippling depression and anxiety; Christopher Chance in “Human Target” is dealing with a terminal poisoning and trying to solve his own pending murder (spoilers: his murderer shares a good deal with Hal Jordan’s in “Lanterns”). His DC series “Heroes in Crisis” places all of the superheroes in therapy, and one of them is unable to handle all the pain that they are holding onto, thus creating a murder mystery.

items.title: Trump Announces Deal with Putin to Deliver Russian Diesel to U.S.
items.summary: President Donald Trump announced Friday that Russia has agreed to supply millions of tons of diesel fuel to the American and global market, following a call with Russian President Vladimir Putin. items.body_text:
President Donald Trump announced Friday that Russia has agreed to supply millions of tons of diesel fuel to the American and global market, following a call with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The president said the first shipments would begin immediately, with larger deliveries scheduled through November and beyond in a post on Truth Social.
Trump laid out a delivery schedule that escalates over time:
I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter.
The president said Russia would then deliver up to 3,000,000 additional tons, depending on the condition of its refineries.
He tied the arrangement to U.S. leverage in the Persian Gulf, where American forces have operated throughout the war with Iran.
“Between our TOTAL CONTROL of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!” Trump wrote.
Trump named lower prices for American farmers, ranchers, and truckers as his priority and closed the announcement with a line on Tehran.
“Iran will not have a Nuclear Weapon!” Trump added.
The announcement follows the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which the president signed into law last month. The statute takes effect Oct. 19, directs tariffs of up to 500 percent on Russian goods, and allows secondary sanctions on countries that purchase Russian fuel.
Many of the law’s provisions can be waived by the president.
Trump imposed major oil sanctions on Russia last October but issued waivers this year, citing disruptions from the Iran conflict that drove up energy costs and inflation.
The deal lands as diesel sits near a record of roughly $6.50 a gallon weeks before the November midterms. Last week, Trump said Europe had agreed to release diesel reserves “immediately,” and days later he signed an order expanding access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel at a rally in Nebraska.

items.title: Hurricane Isaias Brings 96 MPH Gusts to Florida as Flooding Threat Grows
items.summary: Hurricane Isaias brought strong winds and heavy rain to Florida Friday night, with gusts reaching 96 mph reported at Pensacola Bay. The post Hurricane Isaias Brings 96 MPH Gusts to Florida as Flooding Threat Grows appeared first on Breitbart.
items.body_text:
Hurricane Isaias brought strong winds and heavy rain to Florida Friday night, with gusts reaching 96 mph reported at Pensacola Bay.
Fox News shared footage featuring FOX Weather senior correspondent Robert Ray reporting from Destin as strong winds moved through the area.
“Hurricane-force winds are hammering Destin, Florida,” the outlet wrote. “FOX Weather Senior Correspondent Robert Ray is braving the blast as dangerous Category 3 Hurricane Isaias bears down on the Gulf Coast just hours before landfall.”
The report showed the storm’s effects reaching coastal communities before its center came ashore. Isaias had strengthened into a Category 3 hurricane earlier Friday, but the National Hurricane Center’s 8 p.m. Eastern advisory placed it at Category 2 strength, with maximum sustained winds of 110 mph.
FOX Weather’s subsequent coverage described the hurricane as making landfall along the northern Gulf Coast. Its report did not provide a confirmed time and location for the center crossing the shoreline.
Destin and nearby Fort Walton Beach were under a flash flood emergency Friday night as heavy rain threatened life-threatening flooding, according to FOX Weather. The outlet reported a wind gust of 96 mph at Pensacola Bay and a gust of 72 mph in Orange Beach, Alabama.
Water levels were also rising around Panama City and Apalachicola. Forecasters warned that storm surge could produce up to nine feet of inundation along portions of the coast between the Alabama-Florida border and Grayton Beach.
More than 365,000 customers in Florida and Alabama were without electricity Friday evening, the Associated Press (AP) reported, citing PowerOutage.com. Officials in Mobile reported fallen trees and power lines, while Florida’s Emerald Coast Utilities Authority issued a boil-water notice for its customers.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis warned earlier Friday that residents should prepare for electricity failures and dangerous weather even outside the hurricane’s direct path.
“We prepared for the worst,” DeSantis said.
Evacuation orders were issued in portions of Florida’s Okaloosa, Escambia, and Walton counties, as well as Dauphin Island in Alabama. DeSantis, Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey, and Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp declared states of emergency ahead of the storm.
Forecasters expected the hurricane’s effects to spread inland through the weekend. Rainfall totals of 4 to 8 inches were projected across southern Alabama, northwestern Florida, Florida’s Big Bend, and southwest Georgia, with isolated amounts reaching 15 inches.
The tornado threat was expected to extend into Georgia and the Carolinas Saturday. Forecasters warned that the most destructive conditions would occur near the storm’s center and to its east. Air travel was disrupted across northwestern Florida.
All Friday arrivals and departures at Destin-Fort Walton Beach Airport were canceled. Pensacola International Airport recorded 74 cancellations, while Northwest Florida Beaches International Airport had 47, according to FlightAware figures reported by AP.

items.title: ATF’s New Suppressor Rules Are In. Here’s What They Say
items.summary: ‘ATF and the Department of Justice have very limited authority as it relates to changing, making or repealing federal laws’
items.body_text:
The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) released new guidelines Friday on items no longer covered under the National Firearms Act (NFA), noting that state and local rules remained unchanged.
United States District Judge James Wesley Hendrix of the Northern District of Texas, a Trump appointee, handed down his ruling striking down the NFA requirements on Aug. 5 on the grounds that the reducing the transfer tax to $0 in 2025’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act rendered the registration and processing requirements of the NFA unconstitutional. The new guidance, released Friday in an open letter and a more detailed “frequently asked questions” (FAQ) document, was sent to all federally-licensed firearms dealers (FFLs) about how STF would implement the federal laws impacted by the ruling, while steering clear of overriding local rules. (RELATED: Trump DOJ Confirms It Will Not Appeal Historic Ruling Ending Red Tape For Gun Suppressors)
“Effective October 9, 2026, ATF will no longer require individuals to seek ATF approval under the NFA before making or transferring short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns, silencers, and ‘any other weapon[s]’ as defined in 26 U.S.C. § 5845(e),” ATF said in the letter. “ATF will also no longer require such items to be registered in the National Firearms Registration and Transfer Record. These policies apply uniformly to anyone otherwise subject to these requirements, not just to the plaintiffs in the litigation.”
ATF states in the document that it will no longer require Form 4s for the transfer of suppressors, short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns, and “any other weapons,” a legal category to cover other firearms not defined in federal law. However, it also noted that state and local laws were not affected by the injunction, nor did the court strike down laws regarding transportation of certain items.
LEGAL ALERT: The ATF has issued an open letter with guidance regarding the NFA ruling. You can read it here: https://t.co/uSX50GV2Ys https://t.co/8hQfGw9pQB
— Firearms Policy Coalition (@gunpolicy) October 9, 2026
“What we did with the Department of Justice was focus on, okay, the judge’s injunction applied to a very specific group of people that were protected as plaintiffs and we thought, ‘Hey, our job is to protect the American people,’” ATF Director Robert Cekada told the Daily Caller News Foundation in one of his first interviews regarding the guidance issued to FFLs. “The judge, as it relates to other Supreme Court findings, was not able to go beyond his authority. And we’re in the same place. ATF and the Department of Justice have very limited authority as it relates to changing, making or repealing federal laws. So we had to work diligently but carefully to come forward with the path. And the path that we’re on today with the long answer I’m giving you is giving the American people equal treatment under the law.”
The FAQ document went into greater detail about what the ATF was no longer enforcing as a result of the case. Cekada acknowledged some people were frustrated the ATF didn’t move faster, but noted the agency’s powers were limited.
Cekada and ATF Chief Counsel Robert Leider told the DCNF that they expected the new guidance would affect other pending cases involving challenges to the NFA provisions at issue in Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF.
“We’re going to have to see how this plays out. The publication of the enforcement guidance will undoubtedly affect these cases, although how it affects what arguments get raised will be a question for the attorneys of the Department of Justice,” Leider said. “It’s a little bit premature to speculate on exactly what will happen there. But undoubtedly, the status conference will discuss the guidance and there will likely be some effect on the case, although it’s hard to predict at this moment precisely what that effect will be.”

items.body_text:
The Trump administration’s Department of Homeland Security (DHS) redacted deportation data in response to the Oversight Project’s lawsuit, according to documents obtained exclusively by the Daily Caller.
The first document received by the independent 501(c)(4) organization had every data field redacted.
2026-HQLI-00056- Final Response Records October 2026.pdf by ashley
The two-page document, titled “CBP Home Voluntary Self-Departures Summary,” dated Sept. 30, 2026, was fully redacted by DHS under FOIA exemptions (b)(5), which covers deliberative process and attorney-client privilege, and (b)(7)(E), which covers law enforcement techniques and procedures. (RELATED: Oversight Project Charts Path Forward To Combat Birthright Citizenship)
The agency redacted every number, chart and label, leaving only its seal, the document’s title and date, and one footnote visible.
The redactions come amid a broader effort by the Oversight Project to obtain federal deportation figures.
The group launched its Two Commas Compliance Tracker in May and filed eight FOIA requests with DHS, ICE and CBP, including requests for data on self-deportations through the CBP Home app.
After the agencies failed to provide the records, the group filed a lawsuit in July.
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has not published its Fiscal Year (FY) 2025 annual enforcement report, more than a year after that FY ended on September 30, 2025.
The agency’s annual report page still lists the FY 2024 edition as the latest and was last updated July 27, 2026.
ICE released the FY 2024 report on December 19, 2024, about two and a half months after that year closed; following that same timeline, a FY 2025 edition would have been expected around December 2025 on the same schedule.
The Oversight Project launched a second investigation in September covering the period from May 2026 onward, while ICE’s FY 2025 annual enforcement report remains months overdue.
