items.title: Trump Makes Deal With Putin On Diesel Exports. Ukraine Calls It A 'Gift'
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said he reached an agreement with President Vladimir Putin to temporarily ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports, a move Ukraine immediately criticized as a "gift" to the Kremlin.
items.body_text:
WASHINGTON -- US President Donald Trump said he reached an agreement with President Vladimir Putin to temporarily ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports, a move Ukraine immediately criticized as a "gift" to the Kremlin.
Seeking to contain soaring energy prices, Trump said in a social media post on October 9 that the two leaders agreed to release 300,000 tons of diesel immediately, followed by 500,000 tons in November and another million after that.
The move will see prices "COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!" Trump wrote.
Diesel futures fell about 4 percent after the announcement but remained more than 110 percent higher than at the start of the year. Brent crude traded at around $104 a barrel, down just 0.3 percent on the day.
The decision came as Ukrainian, US, and European officials held talks in Miami aimed at ending Russia’s war against Ukraine. The discussions concluded without a breakthrough.
The waiver drew critical comments from Kyiv to lawmakers in Washington, who warned that easing restrictions could provide Moscow with additional revenue to sustain its war against Ukraine.
It also raised questions about US policy toward Russia following Trump’s recent signing of legislation intended to tighten sanctions against countries supporting Moscow’s energy trade.
"Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote in a post on social media.
"Russia will 'repay' the diesel with further terror and perfidy. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged. What is needed is real de-escalation with Russia on a reciprocal basis."
To enable the flow of diesel, the US Treasury Department issued a temporary general license authorizing the sale, delivery, and import of Russian-origin diesel fuel through April 7, 2027.
Trump said that after the initial flows, Russia would supply a further 3 million tons “within a short period of time.”
Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Moscow was ready to increase supplies in October, with exports expected to rise in November and December as refineries resume operations after maintenance.
Diesel prices have climbed since the United States and Israel launched air strikes on Iran in February, sparking a conflict that is now in its eighth month.
Trump has blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for pushing prices higher and urged Zelenskyy to stop targeting Russian energy facilities.
“The problem I have with Ukraine and Russia is that, you know, a lot of the diesel comes … from Russia, and the Russia plants are being hit by Ukraine,” Trump told reporters recently.
Ukrainian officials have said they are prepared to stop attacking Russian oil refineries if Moscow halted its recent barrage of strikes on Ukraine’s energy and other civilian infrastructure installations.
As Ukraine’s negotiating team was in Florida, Zelenskyy also questioned the purpose of the Miami talks while Washington was allowing Russia to earn money from fuel exports.
“I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen,” he said.
Earlier on October 9, Zelenskyy welcomed a bipartisan delegation of US senators to Kyiv and called for stronger pressure on Moscow.
Meanwhile, on Capitol Hill, the waiver for Russia drew the ire of several lawmakers.
“It surely looks bad. The president has always had a moral blindness when it comes to Putin. Propping up Russia’s war economy is terrible,” Republican Representative Don Bacon told RFE/RL.
Democrat Senator Richard Blumenthal, a co-author of the bipartisan Russia sanctions legislation, called the decision an embarrassment, arguing that it would benefit Russia and China while undermining congressional efforts to pressure Moscow.

items.title: India’s ‘Cockroach’ leaders detained; New Delhi in lockdown
items.summary: Indian police crackdown appears to have prevented mass protests against the country's election chief from taking place.
items.body_text:
India’s ‘Cockroach’ leaders detained; New Delhi in lockdown
Indian police crackdown appears to have prevented mass protests against the country’s election chief from taking place.
Police in India’s capital New Delhi have detained more than 1,000 protesters, opposition politicians, journalists, student union leaders, lawyers and the founders of the “Cockroach” youth movement in an effort to quash their demonstration demanding the resignation of the election chief.
The satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other youth groups had announced a protest in the subcontinent’s capital for Saturday, aimed at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of India’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
The protesters accuse the governing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of using the SIR to sway election results, in collusion with its appointees in the election commission, including Kumar.
Meanwhile, opposition parties say the voter deletions also affected the outcome of some recent state elections won by the BJP, and have cast a shadow on elections in the world’s largest democracy.
The CJP had planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site in central Delhi.
But on Saturday, the area was sealed off by security forces before the demonstration began.
The Indian capital was also in lockdown with thousands of police and paramilitary personnel deployed across the city, trains to New Delhi cancelled, mobile internet services suspended and metro stations and markets shuttered, in an effort to stop the protests.
BJP spokesman Sambit Patra has dismissed the demonstrators as “anarchic elements”.
“Their flop show has been completely demolished,” Patra said. “What is happening at Jantar Mantar, what you can see on TV and a few social media handles, is not India’s story. India is calm and going ahead under good governance,” he told reporters.
Police detained the founder of the CJP Abhijeet Dipke, as well as his associates Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, in an aeroplane upon arrival at New Delhi from Mumbai.
Dipke shared a video on his Instagram channel, showing a team of police officers entering the Air India plane after it landed. As they came closer, he said: “I have come to get arrested. I am not afraid of you guys.”
In another video shared by Ranka, Dipke was seen addressing the other passengers on the flight.
“It was nice to know you all. We can see where the nation is heading,” he said. “This is dictatorship where Delhi police has entered in the flight and trying to arrest us.”
Delhi police also detained other CJP members, YouTuber and Modi critic Dhruv Rathee, Neha Bora, the national president of the All India Students’ Association (AISA), a leftist group affiliated with the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist), Dipankar Bhattacharya, the general secretary of the party, Prashant Bhushan, a senior lawyer at the Supreme Court, politicians Yogendra Yadav and Mamata Banerjee, among others.
Despite the detentions of the founders of the youth movement, small protests took place elsewhere in the city, including at the popular crafts market “Dilli Haat”.
But journalists trying to cover these protests and people attempting to protest anywhere in the capital were also detained and whisked away in police buses.
Shranaya, a state committee member of the left-wing Students’ Federation of India (SFI), who goes by her first name, told Al Jazeera that their office in New Delhi had been under surveillance for hours, but members inside had managed to escape and protest.
“This is dictatorship live and in front of us, just to protect a bureaucrat who steals elections for the BJP on Modi’s behest. They are murdering democracy in the daylight in the Indian capital,” she said.

items.title: Child among seven killed by Israel in Gaza on ‘ceasefire’ anniversary
items.summary: At least 1,481 Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks since last year's 'ceasefire', Gaza's Health Ministry says.
items.body_text:
Child among seven killed by Israel in Gaza on ‘ceasefire’ anniversary
At least 1,481 Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks since last year’s ‘ceasefire’, Gaza’s Health Ministry says.
At least seven people, including an eight-year-old girl, have been killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to medical sources, a year after the United States-backed “ceasefire” came into effect – “in name only”.
Shahd Abdul-Razzaq al-Najjar, 8, was killed on Saturday by an Israeli quadcopter drone in the al-Jawazat area of western Gaza City, according to a source in ambulance and emergencies speaking to Al Jazeera.
In the same part of Gaza City, four people were killed and several injured in a separate Israeli bomb attack near Haider Abdel Shafi roundabout, the city’s al-Shifa Hospital said.
One more Palestinian was killed in an Israeli drone attack in the Tuffah neighbourhood of northeastern Gaza City, the hospital said.
In the southern city of Khan Younis, a woman succumbed to injuries sustained in an Israeli attack earlier on Saturday.
Also on Saturday, the enclave’s Ministry of Health said at least 1,481 Palestinians have been killed and 5,254 injured since the so-called ceasefire came into effect on October 10 last year.
Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza has killed at least 74,370 people and injured 175, 371 since October 7, 2023, the ministry added.
In the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed at least nine people and injured 65, it said, adding that one more person succumbed to injuries sustained in previous Israeli aggression.
Al Jazeera’s Tareq Abu Azzoum reported from Gaza on Saturday that the “ceasefire” has only heightened uncertainty in the enclave.
“The rhythm of the genocide has not changed,” he said. “The danger has not gone away completely, and that’s why people believe that it has more consequences, far beyond the immediate loss of life.”
On Friday, more than 100 humanitarian, human rights and civil society organisations said in a joint statement that the ceasefire in Gaza exists only in name.
“The ceasefire exists in name only, with Israeli forces continuing to kill and injure Palestinians daily, and restrictions on aid, equipment and rebuilding materials preventing families from recovering,” the statement said.
In the occupied West Bank, at least 12 Israeli settler pogroms were recorded on Saturday morning, according to the Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission.
Israeli settlers assaulted Palestinian farmers through beatings, spraying them with pepper spray, stealing their property and attacking homes, the Wafa news agency reported. They also detained several Palestinians during the attacks with the help of the Israeli military forces.
In the Ramallah and el-Bireh Governorate, settlers, along with the army, forced farmers to leave their lands and threatened them against returning. Two farmers were beaten and pepper-sprayed, as settlers stole a vehicle and their phones.

items.title: England international Cole Palmer signs new Chelsea deal until 2034
items.summary: Attacking midfielder Palmer has become a key figure in Chelsea's squad since his arrival from Man City in 2023.
items.body_text:
England international Cole Palmer signs new Chelsea deal until 2034
Attacking midfielder Palmer has become a key figure in Chelsea’s squad since his arrival from Man City in 2023.
Chelsea attacking midfielder Cole Palmer has signed a contract extension that will keep him at Stamford Bridge until 2034, the Premier League club announced on Saturday.
The 24-year-old England international has become a key figure since joining Chelsea from Manchester City in 2023, scoring 91 goals in 138 appearances across all competitions.
He was part of the squad that won the Club World Cup in 2025 and the 2024-25 UEFA Conference League.
“Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and obviously the manager, they gave me a lot of confidence so it was only right to sign,” Palmer said. “Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions.
“I feel like we win major trophies here consistently.”
Chelsea have agreed long-term contracts with several first-team players and emerging talent. Forward Joao Pedro recently signed a deal through 2034, and winger Pedro Neto agreed a six-year contract last month.
Chelsea boss Alonso says Palmer is committed to England
Earlier on Friday, Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso insisted Palmer remains committed to playing for England after the attacker drew criticism for missing the recent international break due to injury.
Palmer, left out of England’s World Cup squad this year after a persistent groin injury affected his form, was called up by Thomas Tuchel for Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia and Croatia.
However, Palmer was forced to pull out of the squad due to a recurrence of the issue, with Tuchel saying the midfielder “misses too many opportunities” to play in an England shirt.
Asked about Tuchel’s comments, Alonso told reporters: “The most important thing for Cole is to be fully fit, that he enjoys his game, that he is feeling OK.
“Whenever he is not, like in the Brentford game, we could see that he was struggling. He’s committed but he needs to be fully fit to play. We need him – the club and the national team,” the Spaniard added.
“Now he’s fine. He’s been feeling better this week. We use the first two weeks for him to recover. It’s a little bit from the pubalgia (groin injury) he had.”
Chelsea, 10th in the Premier League standings, host 17th-placed Bournemouth later on Saturday.

items.title: Lithuania eyes permanent US military base, Russia warns of escalation
items.summary: Lithuania said Tuesday that it stands ready to cover the costs of hosting a permanent US military base, while Russia said that any deployment of NATO infrastructure or nuclear weapons on Lithuanian soil would further escalate regional tensions.
items.body_text:

A Russian Navy strike group conducting combat drills in the Baltic Sea, June 23, 2025. /VCG
Lithuania said on Tuesday that it stands ready to cover the costs of hosting a permanent US military base, while Russia said that any deployment of NATO infrastructure or nuclear weapons on Lithuanian soil would further escalate regional tensions.
Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius said on Tuesday that Lithuania is ready to pay the cost to set up a permanent US military base if Washington should âagree to establish one there, a day after US President Donald Trump said he would consider Lithuania's request for a permanent base.
Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov, on the same day, said that the possible deployment of a NATO military base and nuclear weapons in Lithuania would further escalate tensions.
"Both of these things will not contribute to stability and predictability on the European continent. On the contrary, they will become another significant round in the escalation of tensions," Peskov said.
Peskov added that if such deployment occurs, Russia would be forced to take retaliatory measures to ensure its national security.
A constitutional amendment to lift a ban on weapons of mass destruction, potentially opening the way for stationing NATO nuclear weapons in Lithuania, passed the first reading in the Lithuanian parliament earlier on Tuesday. A final vote on the amendment has been scheduled for January 12, 2027.
Lithuania, a member of the EU and NATO, shares a border with Russia's exclave of Kaliningrad. The United States has kept an armored battalion of almost 1,000 troops there since 2019, in overlapping rotations, meaning âthe troops arrive and leave every few months. Sinkevicius said he proposed turning this into a permanent presence at a meeting with Trump's envoy John Coale last month in Vilnius.
The latest development comes as Russia recently issued a warning over NATO's military activities in the Baltic region, saying it is prepared to use all means at its disposal, including nuclear weapons, to defend its territory if NATO attempts to blockade Russia's Kaliningrad region.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte responded last week by describing NATO as a "defensive alliance" and condemning what he called Russia's "nuclear threats." Moscow said it poses no threat to anyone.
The exchange has remained largely rhetorical, but highlights rising tensions around Kaliningrad and the broader Baltic region.
The recent tensions in the Baltic appear to be directly linked to repeated drone disputes between Russia and Baltic coastal states, while NATO has increasingly pressured Russia by targeting its socioeconomic stability, said Chen Yu, deputy director of the Institute of Eurasian Studies at the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations.
More fundamentally, Chen said, this is the inevitable result of a shift in NATO's Baltic strategy: after the outbreak of the Russia-Ukraine conflict since February 2022, NATO's presence in the Baltic has gradually upgraded from rotational deterrence to permanent basing, pushing military pressure right up to Russia's border.
Chen said the Baltic states hope to use nuclear deterrence to offset Russia's military power, driven by rising security anxiety and a desire to align with US strategic agenda, as Washington actively discusses expanding its nuclear deployment plans in Europe.
In response, he said, Russia is likely to further strengthen its nuclear forces in Kaliningrad, deploy more tactical nuclear weapons and hypersonic weapons, and enhance the nuclear-conventional strike capability of its

items.title: Ethiopian parliament approves new cabinet of 23 members
items.summary: Of the 23 ministerial positions, including the deputy prime minister, more than 10 positions remained unchanged, as nine ministerial positions were taken by women.
items.body_text:
By continuing to browse our site you agree to our use of cookies, revised Privacy Policy and Terms of Use. You can change your cookie settings through your browser.
                            
                            I agree
                        
                        Africa
                    
                    
    22:31, 09-Oct-2026
                    
                
CGTN
                    
                    Africa;Ethiopia
                
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed speaks during a session of the Ethiopian Parliament in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, Monday, October 5, 2026./VCG
Ethiopia's House of Peoples' Representatives (HoPR), the lower chamber of the parliament, on Thursday unanimously approved a 23-member cabinet proposed by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
Unveiling members of the new cabinet, Abiy told the parliament that the nominees were chosen based on their educational background, professional experience, execution capacity, previous career and commitment to fighting corruption and delivering high-quality public service.
Of the 23 ministerial positions, including the deputy prime minister, more than 10 positions remained unchanged, as nine ministerial positions were taken by women.
"The appointment has taken into consideration the appointees' cleanness from corruption and commitment to service delivery, gender, ethnicity and religion disparities," Abiy said, noting that the nominees are believed to help realize the government's "Medemer" philosophy, an Amharic word for "coming together" or "synergy."
He urged the appointees to advance public service delivery and protect national interests of more than 54 million citizens who cast their ballots in the June 1 general elections.
Accordingly, Temesgen Tiruneh has been reappointed as deputy prime minister and Gedion Timothewos has been reappointed as minister of foreign affairs, while opposition party member Berhanu Nega has been reappointed as education minister.
"This isn't the most ideal nomination," Abiy told the parliament while responding to questions raised by members of the parliament. "This is the best we could come up with based on the agreed criteria."
The formation of the new cabinet comes after the appointment of Abiy Ahmed as Prime Minister of Ethiopia on Monday during the inaugural session of the seventh HoPR tenure.

items.title: Xi, Brunei's Sultan exchange congratulations on 35 years of ties
items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Sultan of Brunei Haji Hassanal Bolkiah Mu'izzaddin Waddaulah on Wednesday exchanged congratulations on the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.
items.body_text:
By continuing to browse our site you agree to our use of cookies, revised Privacy Policy and Terms of Use. You can change your cookie settings through your browser.
                            
                            I agree
                        
                        Politics
                    
                    
    16:58, 30-Sep-2026
                    
                
CGTN
, Updated 18:14, 30-Sep-2026
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Sultan of Brunei Haji Hassanal Bolkiah Mu'izzaddin Waddaulah on Wednesday exchanged congratulations on the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.
Xi noted that the traditional friendship between China and Brunei has a long history and remained strong over time.
In the process of working together towards modernization, the two countries have set an example of mutual respect, equality and common development between large and small countries, Xi added.
Over the 35 years since the establishment of diplomatic ties, China and Brunei have steadily deepened political mutual trust, achieved fruitful results in cooperation across various fields, and strengthened people-to-people exchanges, he said.
Xi said that last year, Hassanal paid a state visit to China, during which the two sides reached important consensus on building a China-Brunei community with a shared future, ushering bilateral relations into a new stage of historical development.
Xi emphasized that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Brunei relations and is willing to work with Hassanal to take the 35th anniversary of diplomatic ties as an opportunity to carry forward traditional friendship, enhance the alignment of development strategies, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, and advance the building of the China-Brunei community with a shared future in a more substantive and in-depth manner, so as to better benefit the two peoples and contribute more to regional prosperity and stability.
Hassanal stated that over the past 35 years since establishing diplomatic relations, Brunei and China have consistently trusted, respected, and understood each other.
In 2025, the two countries reached an important consensus on building a community with a shared future, he added.
He looks forward to taking the 35th anniversary of Brunei-China diplomatic relations as an opportunity to further strengthen bilateral ties, deepen cooperation and exchanges in areas such as economy, trade, investment, defense, and culture, and jointly achieve prosperity and progress for both countries, thereby better benefiting their peoples.

A view of the International Criminal Court in The Hague, the Netherlands, September 23, 2026. /VCG
UN Secretary-General AntÃ³nio Guterres and foreign ministers of eight countries on Friday criticized the US announcement of sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC).
"The secretary-general is deeply alarmed by the expected impact of today's sanctions on the International Criminal Court as a whole, and in particular, its continued ability to perform its important mandates, including in relation to the situations referred to it by the Security Council and states parties to the Rome Statute," said Stephane Dujarric, the spokesman for Guterres.
"Today's decision marks a serious blow to our collective pursuit of international criminal justice, of which the ICC is a key pillar. Accountability for international crimes and delivery of justice to victims are central to our global commitment to peace, security, human rights and fundamental freedoms," said the spokesman.
He said the secretary-general reiterated his unwavering support for the independence of the ICC and its officials, adding that Guterres called on all states to uphold their commitments under international law and to support efforts aimed at ensuring accountability for the most serious crimes of concern to the international community.
Also on Friday, foreign ministers of eight countries, Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom, issued a joint statement, expressing regret over and strong opposition to the US announcement of sanctions against the ICC.
"We, the undersigned States Parties to the Rome Statute of the ICC, reaffirm our continued and unwavering support for the independence, impartiality, and integrity of the ICC," said the statement.
The eight nations pledged to engage in constructive and inclusive dialogue with non-States Parties as they prepare for the Assembly of States Parties in December 2026.
Earlier on Friday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced sanctions against the ICC, saying the measures would ban transactions with the court, cut off its resources and cripple its ability to operate.

China's Foreign Ministry on Friday condemned Japanese right-wing forces for using manipulated historical data to distort the history of World War II through AI models.

"The covert moves of Japanese right-wing forces greatly hurt the sentiments of Japan's war victims and constitute a blatant affront to human conscience. The international community must stay on high alert and push back those moves," Mao said.

items.title: Finland halts Google data center work over environmental assessment
items.summary: A Finnish supervisory authority on Tuesday ordered environmentally significant preparatory work at two planned Google data center sites in northern Finland to be halted until legally required environmental impact assessments are completed.

    12:09, 07-Oct-2026

An aerial view shows the site where Google's data center is set to be built in Muhos, Finland, September 29, 2026. /VCG
A Finnish supervisory authority on Tuesday ordered environmentally significant preparatory work at two planned Google data center sites in northern Finland to be halted until legally required environmental impact assessments are completed.
The Finnish Licensing and Supervision Authority (LVV) said Tuike Finland Oy, the company responsible for the projects, must immediately suspend such work at the sites in the northern Finnish municipality of Muhos and the city of Kajaani and no later than October 23.
The order covers activities including tree removal, topsoil stripping, road and storage-area construction, and changes to drainage. Environmental impact assessments for both projects are still underway and are expected to be completed later this year.
Google said it would comply with the authorities' instructions. "We are examining the observations by the Finnish authorities carefully and will act in line with the instructions by Finnish authorities," Sondre Ronander, Google's head of communications for Finland and Norway, told Finnish national broadcaster Yle.
The company had earlier said it acted on the basis of Finnish forestry legislation. Finnish authorities have stressed, however, that environmental impact assessment requirements are governed by separate legislation.
Finnish Minister of Climate and the Environment Sari Multala told Finnish media that all companies operating in Finland, domestic or international, must comply with Finnish law. She said responsibility extended through the subcontracting chain, with the international company ultimately bearing responsibility.
The two projects are part of Google's 13-billion-euro (about $14.64 billion) investment plan for Finland, formally announced on September 9. The plan includes new data centers in Muhos, Kajaani and Vaala, a municipality in central-northern Finland, as well as an expansion of its existing facility in the city of Hamina in southern Finland.
Preparatory work at the Muhos and Kajaani sites began earlier this year, with tree clearing starting in March and other earthmoving and infrastructure work following later.
Google has described the investment as its largest single investment in Europe.

items.title: U.S. failure to appoint Australian ambassador "diplomatic insult": former deputy PM
items.summary: Former Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer has accused the U.S. of hitting Australia with a "diplomatic insult."
items.body_text:
CANBERRA, Jan. 3 (Xinhua) -- Former Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer has accused the U.S. of hitting Australia with a "diplomatic insult."
Fischer, who served as Deputy Prime Minister from 1996 to 1999 under Australia's longest-serving Prime Minister John Howard, on Wednesday said the U.S. administration's failure to appoint an ambassador to Canberra for 18 months indicated Australia was now of "low priority."
John Berry, the former U.S. Ambassador to Australia, resigned in September 2016, leaving the post vacant ever since.
"This is now bordering on a diplomatic insult," Fischer told Fairfax Media on Wednesday. "We've been downgraded, despite all the nice noises. We are a low priority.
Fischer identified U.S. President Donald Trump's opposition to a refugee deal negotiated between his predecessor Barack Obama and Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull as a likely reason for the current administration's failure to appoint an ambassador.
It has long been speculated that Admiral Harry Harris, head of the U.S. Pacific Command, is the likely next ambassador but there has been no confirmation from the White House.
Simon Jackman, head of the United States Studies Centre at the University of Sydney, disagreed with Fischer, saying the delay showed the Trump administration was taking the appointment "extremely seriously."

items.title: US FCC plan to bar Chinese testing labs could disrupt global electronics supply chains, raise industry costs: analysts
items.body_text:
US FCC plan to bar Chinese testing labs could disrupt global electronics supply chains, raise industry costs: analysts
The seal of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) prior to an open commission meeting at the agency's headquarters in Washington, DC, US, on Wednesday, Feb. 18, 2026. Photo: VCG
A US plan to bar Chinese laboratories from testing electronic devices for the American market could disrupt a key link in the global electronics supply chain, potentially forcing manufacturers to move testing operations overseas and raising costs for an industry heavily reliant on China's manufacturing and testing capabilities, Chinese analysts said on Thursday.
The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Wednesday that it will vote on October 29 on a proposal to bar laboratories and certification bodies in countries including China that do not offer reciprocal treatment to US-based labs from conducting FCC-required testing, Reuters reported.
The proposed restrictions, covering devices such as smartphones, computers and cameras destined for the US market, are scheduled to take effect in December 2028 if approved.
The proposal would widen restrictions introduced in 2025, when the FCC barred laboratories owned or controlled by the Chinese government from testing electronics for the US market, affecting several dozen facilities. The agency said this year, however, that a substantial majority of China-based labs continued to conduct such testing, according to Reuters.
He Weiwen, a senior fellow at the Center for China and Globalization, told the Global Times on Thursday that the proposed ban marks a further expansion of the FCC's technology restrictions on China, extending beyond telecom operators and equipment to testing and certification services.
"The move reflects an attempt to suppress China's role in the telecommunications sector, driven by concerns over the competitive disadvantage of the US relative to China in these areas," the expert said, describing the measure as a non-market, protectionist approach to technological competition.
According to the Reuters report, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said that 82 percent of electronic devices covered by the agency's testing figures were tested in China in 2025, while fewer than 4 percent were tested in US-based laboratories.
Under the proposal, manufacturers relying on China-based labs for FCC testing would need to shift to facilities in the US or other eligible economies. In a proposed rule published in the US Federal Register in May, the FCC sought public comment on ways to mitigate transition costs, as well as possible additional fees and oversight requirements.
The concentration of testing in China reflects the close integration of electronics manufacturing and compliance testing, an arrangement that global manufacturers have benefited from for years, with nearby laboratories helping reduce logistics costs and shorten development cycles, according to international testing firm Element.
Element also warned that shifting testing to other approved laboratories could lead to longer lead times and higher costs as demand puts pressure on available capacity. Manufacturers could also face greater scheduling difficulties and reduced access to specialized testing expertise, particularly for less common types of testing.
He Weiwen cautioned that placing national security considerations above objective technological principles could hinder technological progress and harm economic efficiency.
The proposal is the latest in a series of FCC restrictions affecting Chinese technology. The agency blocked approval of new models of Chinese-made drones in December 2025 and foreign-made consumer routers in March 2026. It also expanded equipment restrictions involving Huawei and ZTE in June and moved in July to bar devices containing key components from Chinese firms under the pretext of so-called national security risks.

items.title: South Africa freedom day memorial gathering reveals its pursuit of dignity and inclusive governance in post apartheid era
items.body_text:
IN-DEPTH / IN-DEPTH
South Africa freedom day memorial gathering reveals its pursuit of dignity and inclusive governance in post apartheid era
Politics finds its rhythm
 Editor's Note: 
In an era of profound global shifts and increasingly complex regional dynamics, a proper understanding of the world must be rooted in "grounded experience" and localized insights. Global Times English edition, in collaboration with the Academy of International and Regional Communication Studies, Communication University of China, is proud to launch "Local Insights," an English-language column dedicated to original, field-based observations.
We invite Chinese scholars and professionals who are studying, conducting exchanges, or working outside China, as well as international students and friends living and studying in China who are familiar with the social contexts of their home countries or third countries, to begin from first-hand field experience and engage with social, cultural, and contemporary issues beyond China. In the fifth article of this column, drawing on her onâtheâground experience as a Chinese exchange scholar, the author observes a South Africa Freedom Day memorial gathering, revealing how local politics unfolds through collective singing, dancing, and grassroots participation, while also reflecting on the gap between political liberation and economic justice.
As a PhD student, I am currently on an exchange program at Nelson Mandela University in South Africa, with support from the China Scholarship Council. Since arriving here, I have developed a habit of stepping beyond campus whenever possible. Community meetings, municipal events and public gatherings have become a vital way for me to engage with local life. This time, a local friend recommended that I attend a memorial event in Kariega, organized by the Congress of South African Trade Unions (COSATU) in honor of its former president, Phumzile John Gomomo. Beyond that, I had little sense of what kind of gathering I was about to enter.
It was on the way that I noticed the streets were unusually vibrant. Groups of people were dressed in colorful attire, with bright Xhosa headscarves and garments bearing political symbols. My friend then reminded me that it was April 27, which is Freedom Day in South Africa. On this day in 1994, South Africa held its first non-racial election, formally ending apartheid and inaugurating democratic rule. Over the past three decades, Freedom Day commemorates political liberation, while also inviting recurring reflection on whether the promise of freedom has been fully realized. In that sense, Freedom Day marks an important moment for observing contemporary South African politics and social sentiment.
The aerial view of Johannesburg, South Africa Photo: VCG
From street to hall: Entering Freedom Day
The event was scheduled to begin at 10 am, and we arrived shortly before the hour. Yet there were not many people present. Banners of COSATU, the South African Communist Party (SACP), and the African National Congress (ANC) had already been displayed inside the hall, quietly framing the political context of the gathering. Although my understanding was still limited, I could already sense that their presence mattered. COSATU, SACP and ANC represent key forces in South Africa's political landscape, historically linked through the "Tripartite Alliance" formed during the anti-apartheid struggle and sustained in various forms since 1994. I could see that this was not simply a local gathering, but one embedded within a much longer political tradition.
What struck me first was how different the atmosphere was from what I had expected of a political gathering. There was no sense of urgency or visible tension. My friend introduced me around, and we greeted each other through handshakes, embraces and brief conversations, with a familiarity that suggested long-standing connections. items.title: China to introduce new train timetable from July 1, including high-speed train service between Beijing and Urumqi
items.body_text:
China to introduce new train timetable from July 1, including high-speed train service between Beijing and Urumqi
Passengers are pictured at the Beijing Tongzhou Railway Station in the Beijing Municipal Administrative Center in Beijing, capital of China, May 29, 2026. From 2016 to 2026, the Beijing Municipal Administrative Center marks a decade of planning and development. Over the past ten years, it has undergone a remarkable transformation into a vibrant modern area. Photo: Xinhua
China's national railway network will implement a new train-running timetable starting July 1, which will strengthen connectivity between the country's northwestern provinces and the central, southern, and southwestern regions, while also introducing high-speed train service for the first time between Urumqi, Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, and Beijing, the China State Railway Group announced on Wednesday.
Tickets under the new timetable went on sale on Wednesday.
The upgraded network is expected to further enhance railway transportation capacity and operational efficiency. Under the new timetable, China's national railways will operate 12,174 scheduled passenger trains, marking an increase of 106 trains compared with the current schedule.
For example, the railway authorities have arranged 58 high-speed trains from Xi'an in Northwest China's Shaanxi to destinations including Nanyang of Central China's Henan Province, Hankou of Central China's Hubei Province and Chongqing city in Southwest China.
Wan Yaqiong, director of the ticket sales workshop at Xi'an Station under China Railway Xi'an Group, said that the new timetable will introduce direct services from Xi'an to Hankou, with the fastest round-trip travel time controlled within seven hours, according to a report by the China Central Television (CCTV) News on Wednesday.
Additionally, high-speed trains will operate from Yan'an city in Shaanxi to Shaoshan city in Central China's Hunan, establishing a direct high-speed rail link between the two major "red tourism" destinations - historical sites with a modern revolutionary legacy, the CCTV News report noted.
After the timetable adjustment, high-speed trains will run for the first time between Urumqi station and Beijing West station. At the same time, the T-series trains operating between Urumqi and Chongqing West will be upgraded to Z-series direct express trains, shortening the travel time between the two places by more than two hours.
The railway authorities will increase the number of high-speed services during morning and evening rush hours on certain high-speed rail lines in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, the Yangtze River Delta, and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, providing greater convenience for commuters.
Global Times

items.title: 学习手记 | “环境就是民生”
items.summary: 6月5日是世界环境日，也是我国环境保护法确立的环境日。 22年前的这一天，在时任浙江省委书记习近平部署推动下，以农村人居环境整治为重点的“千万工程”启动。 当时，习近平同志担任浙江省委书记刚半年多，工作千头万绪。他何以将农村人居环境整治作为重点工作？ 在基层调研时，习近平同志发现，在浙江经济快速发展的同时，广大农村却面临“成长的烦恼”，村庄面貌不如人意。 全省3.4万个村庄中，人居环境较好的仅4000个。有人形容：“走过一村又一村，村村都是垃圾村。”还有农民这样描述：“起早贪黑赚钞票，垃圾堆里数钞票，躺在医院花钞票。”可以说，人居环境整治是当时浙江农村群众的一个迫切期盼。 “千万工程”聚焦乡亲们走什么村道、怎么处理畜禽粪便等小问题，却直接关系农民获得感、幸福感，是实打实的民生大事。 老百姓的生活环境如何，习近平同志念兹在兹： 上世纪70年代，在陕北冯家坪公社赵家河大队驻点时，他撸起袖管，一石一瓦盖起村里第一个男女分开的厕所； 到正定工作，不仅大力推进“人拉猪吃”的“连茅圈”改造工作，还拿着大扫帚走上街头搞卫生，推动成立全县第一支专职卫生清洁队； 任福州市委书记，亲自为建造垃圾处理场选址

items.title: 刘国中在安徽调研时强调 全力以赴夺取夏粮丰收 全面打牢秋粮生产基础
items.summary: 新华社合肥6月5日电 中共中央政治局委员、国务院副总理刘国中3日至5日到安徽调研“三夏”农业生产工作。他强调，要深入学习贯彻习近平总书记关于国家粮食安全的重要论述，按照党中央、国务院部署，扛稳政治责任，毫不放松抓好夏收夏种夏管，全力以赴夺取夏粮丰收，全面打牢秋粮生产基础，确保完成全年粮食生产目标任务。 刘国中先后来到宿州市、淮南市、六安市，深入小麦机收和夏播现场、农机跨区作业服务点、农事服务中心、粮食仓储中心、地方农科院等，实地察看夏收夏种、农机作业服务保障、粮食烘干收储等工作，详细了解农作物新品种选育、大面积单产提升、农资保供稳价、高标准农田建设等情况。 刘国中强调，“三夏”工作抓得好不好，事关全年粮食生产目标任务能否顺利实现。当前正值“三夏”农业生产关键时期，要抓住有利天气抢晴收获，组织好农机跨区作业，强化服务保障和安全管理，确保夏收高效进行。要抓实抓牢机收减损、烘干晾晒等各项措施，最大程度减少粮食损失。要精心做好夏粮收购工作，引导各类企业积极入市，保障粮食市场平稳运行。要压茬推进夏播，加强农资供应和农事服务，强化技术集成及推广应用，落实落细合理密植、精量播种等大面积单产提升措施，

items.title: 韩正会见中美高级别二轨对话美方代表团
items.summary: 新华社北京6月5日电 6月5日，国家副主席韩正在北京会见中美高级别二轨对话美方代表团。 韩正表示，中美关系是当今世界最重要的双边关系之一。当前，中美关系处于关键历史节点。中美相互尊重、和平共处、合作共赢，不仅有利于两国，也有利于世界和平与发展。希望中美高级别二轨对话能不断汇聚两国有识之士的真知灼见，增进美国各界对中国的了解和理解，共同推动中美关系稳定、健康、可持续发展。 美方表示，美中高级别二轨对话有助于双方更好理解对方，为两国关系发展提供更多有益思路。中国经济发展令人钦佩，双方应加强贸易、投资等领域对话合作。

items.title: 全国人大常委会启动节约能源法执法检查
items.summary: 新华社北京6月5日电 为推动节约能源法全面有效实施，促进更高水平、更高质量做好节能工作，全国人大常委会5日启动节约能源法执法检查。 节约能源法自1998年1月1日实施，并于2007年、2016年、2018年进行了修改。 记者5日从全国人大常委会节约能源法执法检查组第一次全体会议上了解到，为全面深入了解法律实施情况，此次执法检查采取实地检查与委托检查相结合的方式，检查组将赴天津、江苏、湖南、广东、广西、四川等省（区、市）开展实地检查，并委托北京、河北、山西、吉林、上海、重庆等省（市）人大常委会对本行政区域内节约能源法实施情况进行检查。检查组将采取实地检查、听取汇报、组织座谈、典型调研、专题研究、抽查暗访等多种方式，全面准确了解法律实施情况，对带有普遍性的问题深入调查研究。 检查组将重点检查8方面内容：落实节能管理制度情况，推进重点领域节能工作情况，重点用能单位节能管理情况，推动节能技术进步情况，实施节能激励措施情况，与法律配套的行政法规、部门规章以及地方性法规的制定情况，法律实施中存在的其他问题，对节约能源法修改的意见和建议。

items.summary: 在树下院落、乡间凉亭，一场场热气腾腾的“凉亭夜话”，正悄然改变着河南省三门峡市卢氏县基层治理的面貌。从群众自发到如今党委引领下的制度化实践，“凉亭夜话”不仅成为群众表达心声的平台，也构建起基层治理的创新模式，让“小议事”撬动“大治理”。 “凉亭夜话”源于卢氏县木桐乡群众的自发行动。农闲时，村民围坐凉亭、树下，或为化解纠纷说和相劝，或为某一项目献计献策。卢氏县党委因势利导，对此进行规范化、制度化，并在全县推广。 “凉亭夜话”以开放空间为议事场景，每月至少组织一次群众议事会，激发群众参与热情。同时，明确“五议三不议”原则，划定议事边界。通过建立民情收集机制，形成“民情清单”“议事清单”，配套“四公”议事制度和闭环工作机制，加强督促督办。 2024年，“凉亭夜话”决议落实率高达92%，持续激发干部群众谋发展、干事业、促振兴的内生动力。木桐乡年投资59亿元的钼矿项目落地，创办了创业技能培训中心，打造了“灵神粉条”网红品牌，办起了位于豫陕交界地带的烤鱼店，各项产业红红火火，名列全县“十快乡镇”。全县农村党支部领办专业合作社170余家，涌现出一批集体经济收入超百万元的村。（记者 崔志坚 通讯员 刘

items.title: 北京发布14项举措保障新就业群体权益
items.summary: 本报北京6月4日电 （记者王洲）6月3日，北京市司法局、市市场监管局、市总工会联合发布14项具体举措，构建政策协同、法律服务和维权保障三位一体的制度框架保障新就业群体权益。在公共法律服务方面，北京市司法局组织市、区两级公共法律服务中心、乡镇（街道）工作站为新就业形态劳动者提供法律咨询、法律查询服务以及律师、公证、司法鉴定等法律便利服务，村（居）法律顾问也将常住新就业形态劳动者纳入服务范围；设立“城市蜂鸟”法律援助项目，为在交通事故中不负主要责任、无法认定法律援助条件的网约配送员提供公益法律服务。 同时，北京市市场监管部门将发挥网约配送行业党委作用，及时收集、反映、协调解决网约配送员的问题困难和集中诉求，协同开展“清朗网络平台算法典型问题治理”专项行动，推动平台企业落实算法安全主体责任。市总工会将规范召开企业职工代表大会，落实劳动者四项重大权益保障，开通工会法律服务绿色通道，常态化开展工会特色交通安全、职业健康专项教育。 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 14 版）

items.title: 北京出台举措优化入境旅游服务

items.title: “阿大葱油饼”焕新记（干部状态新观察·走进一线探作风）
items.summary: “阿大葱油饼”店铺前排起长队。 受访者供图"> “阿大葱油饼”店铺前排起长队。受访者供图 下午两点，午餐时间已过，上海市静安区石门二路上，“吴根存阿大葱油饼”的招牌下还排着长长的队伍。 “阿大”吴根存在上海颇有名气。他做了30多年的葱油饼，一度是上海街头小吃中的“顶流”。直到3年前老店歇业，“阿大葱油饼”才渐渐淡出人们的视线。 年近七旬的“阿大”坐到店门口休息，厨房里忙碌的，是他的儿子吴志勇。 “想把老爸树起来的品牌再做起来，把葱油饼的手艺传承下去。”摘下帽子、口罩，脱掉围裙，吴志勇满头大汗。曾是外企员工的他，有这个念头已经许久。在上海市区多处考察后，今年4月，一家人选中了石门二路这家门面“老店新开”。 “‘阿大葱油饼’回来了！”随着刚出炉的葱油饼照片、视频在网上热传，新店门前迅速热闹了起来。顾客络绎不绝，店里只得贴出提示：每人限购5只。 生意红火令人欣喜，可没成想，紧接着就收到不少投诉。 4月底，周边商户、居民接连反映：店里的油烟乱排，影响正常经营、生活；马路上排队的顾客有时太多，堵住人行道，阻碍交通。 “街道干部来找我时，我是有点蒙的。”吴志勇说，葱油饼要好吃，需要烤和炸，自然产生

items.title: 优化口岸营商环境没有最好，只有更好（快评）
items.summary: 出台高效举措、优化服务体验、强化硬件设施、搭建高效平台……近年来，海关等职能部门和地方政府密切合作，推出一系列精准有力的政策措施，为激发经营主体活力和助力外贸高质量发展注入强劲动能。 口岸营商环境直接关系到国际贸易的便利程度。优化口岸营商环境，意味着在简化流程、提高效率、降低成本上下功夫。无论是通关时间的缩短，还是报关手续的简化，都显著降低了企业的运营成本，加快了货物的流转速度。 优化口岸营商环境没有最好，只有更好。随着全球贸易格局不断变化，口岸营商环境的优化仍将是一个持续的过程。各地各部门应持续提升政策供给质量，更大程度释放政策效应，推动口岸营商环境向着更加高效、透明、公平、便利的方向发展，有力助推贸易强国建设。 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 08 版）

items.title: 将适老化理念融入“诗与远方”（专家点评）
items.summary: 自驾出行、列车出游和旅居康养成为越来越多老年人的选择。 银发旅游蓬勃发展，推动了旅游产业升级。无论是城镇还是乡村，都在努力完善旅游基础设施和公共文化服务。为了更好满足老年游客的需求，还应开发更多适合老年人的旅游线路和产品，并加强博物馆、美术馆、酒店等场所的适老化改造。从硬件到服务，全社会应共同发力，将适老化理念融入方方面面，助力老有所游、老有所乐。 值得关注的是，老年人也可能因信息不对称而遭遇消费陷阱，还可能因为行程安排不当而水土不服。文化和旅游部门要联合市场监管等部门，从社交平台的旅游广告和招徕资质审查开始，重点规范交通、餐饮、住宿、购物、自费项目、医疗保障和应急救援等服务标准，加强对强买强卖、诱导消费、价格歧视等行为的综合监管和专项执法，让老年人畅享“诗与远方”。 （作者为中国旅游研究院院长） 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 04 版）

items.title: 习近平总书记关切事｜我们的名字叫“长江”——三个沿江村庄的变迁故事

items.summary: 6月4日上午，国家主席习近平在北京中南海会见白俄罗斯总统卢卡申科。 新华社记者 黄敬文摄"> 6月4日上午，国家主席习近平在北京中南海会见白俄罗斯总统卢卡申科。 新华社记者 黄敬文摄 新华社北京6月4日电 6月4日上午，国家主席习近平在中南海会见白俄罗斯总统卢卡申科。 习近平再次祝贺卢卡申科当选连任总统。习近平指出，中国和白俄罗斯是真朋友、好伙伴。双方一直以诚相待、以信相交。两国传统友好历久弥坚，政治互信牢不可破，各领域合作全面推进。中方始终从战略高度和长远角度看待和发展中白关系，愿同白方一道，推动两国关系和互利合作行稳致远。双方要进一步加强在联合国、上海合作组织等多边框架内协调和配合，共同反对霸权霸道霸凌，捍卫国际公平正义。 卢卡申科表示，这是我第15次访问中国，每一次都真切感受到中方的深情厚谊。白方感谢中方长期以来大力支持和帮助，对中国高度信任，将坚定不移发展对华关系，积极推进对华合作。在国际事务中，中国坚定维护多边主义，反对单边主义和制裁施压，为世界树立了榜样。白方深表钦佩，愿与中方共同捍卫国际公平正义。 王毅参加会见。 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 01 版）

items.title: 习近平向韩国当选总统李在明致贺电
items.summary: 新华社北京6月4日电 6月4日，国家主席习近平致电李在明，祝贺他当选韩国总统。 习近平指出，中韩互为重要近邻和合作伙伴。建交33年来，双方超越意识形态和社会制度差异，携手并进、相互成就，实现两国关系平稳健康发展，不仅增进了两国人民福祉，也为促进地区和平稳定和发展繁荣作出积极贡献。 习近平强调，我高度重视中韩关系发展。当前，世界百年变局加速演进，国际和地区形势中的不确定因素增多。作为全球和地区重要国家，中方愿同韩方一道，坚守建交初心，坚定睦邻友好方向，坚持互利共赢目标，共同推动中韩战略合作伙伴关系不断向前发展，更好造福两国人民。 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 01 版）

items.title: 公证档案管理办法修订 推进公证电子档案信息化建设
items.summary: 记者6月4日从司法部获悉，司法部、国家档案局近日印发新修订的《公证档案管理办法》，进一步推进公证电子档案信息化建设，优化公证档案保管期限，完善公证档案利用规则等。 公证档案是记录公证活动过程的基本载体，是国家档案的重要组成部分，是公证执业监督和质量管理的主要依据。办法完善公证档案管理部门职责任务，明确国务院司法行政机关负责制定全国统一的公证档案工作制度，并与国家档案主管部门对全国公证档案工作进行监督、指导和检查。 在推进公证档案电子化与文书材料归档数字化转型方面，办法设专章明确公证档案信息化建设的整体性要求和原则性规定，规定公证电子档案与传统载体公证档案具有同等效力，倡导推进公证档案数字化，并对已经数字化的档案备查提出要求。让静态数据转化为服务动能，更好促进减证便民。 此外，办法依据新修订的档案法及其实施条例，规定大幅缩短公证档案保管期限，将永久、60年和20年的保管期限，相应调整为永久、30年和10年，并制作《公证档案保管期限表》，以附件形式附后。办法明确公证档案保管责任，规定公证机构可以将公证档案的保管期限通过书面告知、办公场所公示等方式告知当事人。规范公证档案销毁条件和程序，明确

items.title: 法治力量护航民营经济高质量发展（代表之声）
items.summary: 《中华人民共和国民营经济促进法》颁布施行，令民营企业界广为振奋。这部法律的出台，承载着民营经济人士多年的期盼，回应了经营实践中的痛点、难点问题，必将开启民营经济发展的崭新篇章。 改革开放40多年来，民营经济从小到大、从弱到强，不断发展壮大。我父辈那样老一代民营企业家视法治建设为企业发展根基，呼吁加强法治保障，对民营经济领域法治建设有着深切期盼。上世纪90年代，许多民营企业家为制定乡镇企业法建言献策。从当年的乡镇企业法，到如今的民营经济促进法，映照了我国从推进农村工业化到构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制的深刻变革。 作为一名来自民营企业的全国人大代表，我有幸参与了民营经济促进法的立法过程。去年在草案征求意见阶段提交了意见，今年全国两会期间又提交了相关代表建议，并列席十四届全国人大常委会第十五次会议，见证了新法的审议和表决。让我印象特别深刻的是，立法过程中，立法机关充分听取民营企业家的意见，相关部门负责同志也专程到我们的驻地，就法律条款进行详细解读和沟通，充分体现了党和国家对民营经济的重视、对民营企业诉求的尊重。 党的十八大以来，党中央出台一系列重大举措，促进民营经济持续、健康、高质量发展。

items.title: “阿大葱油饼”焕新记（干部状态新观察·走进一线探作风）

items.title: “填一表、跑一次” 辽宁沈阳推出“公民信息连锁变更一件事”
items.summary: 平日里，你有过变更身份信息多次跑的经历吗？如何让更改身份信息快速又准确，来看看沈阳推出的“公民信息连锁变更一件事”。 2024年10月17日，沈阳市“公民信息连锁变更一件事”正式上线。沈阳居民在申请变更姓名、出生日期、民族、性别、居民身份证号码等基本信息时，可以在线下基层派出所或线上的沈阳政务服务网，通过填写一张表单，提交一次变更申请，进行业务办理。审批通过后，公安内部立即启动跨层级、跨警种联动，外部与社保、医保、公积金等部门跨部门联动，开展“串并联”审批。全部完成后，同步发放新的身份证、驾驶证、机动车登记证、机动车行驶证、保安员证、爆破作业人员许可证、社会保障卡，同步变更医保和公积金账户等信息，证照全部邮寄到家。截至目前，全市已经办理相关业务160余件。 沈阳市民邵某是“公民信息连锁变更一件事”的首位体验者，通过沈阳政务服务网“公民信息连锁变更一件事”板块申请变更姓名后，邵某的身份证、驾驶证、机动车行驶证、机动车登记证书，医保、公积金和姓名同步更改，一次申请全部办理完成。 据介绍，“公民信息连锁变更一件事”改革的实施离不开办事流程优化以及多部门数据共享与协同合作。沈阳市营商环境建设局

items.title: 中央网信办等：开展军队文职人员考试培训专项整治
items.summary: 关于开展军队文职人员考试培训专项整治的通告 近年来，一些教育培训机构以军队文职人员考试培训为名违法违规经营，出现无证经营、虚假宣传、借机敛财等乱象，损害了考生权益，严重影响军队形象声誉和考试公平性。为维护人民军队良好形象、考生切身利益和市场经营秩序，现就有关问题通告如下： 一、严禁仿冒军队文职人员考试主管部门官方微信、微博、网站等行为；不得在互联网上擅自解读、曲解军队文职人员管理、军队文职人员考试有关政策或者擅自发布关于军队文职人员考试的不当宣传、不良炒作、欺骗误导考生和社会公众等信息。 二、各类学校不得违规组织军队文职人员考试培训活动，未经批准不得向军队文职人员考试培训机构提供场地，不得为军队文职人员考试培训机构招揽生源提供便利，学校教师和其他工作人员不得违规到军队文职人员考试培训机构兼职、代课，不得参与编写有关培训材料。各级教育行政部门要按照属地管理原则，配合有关部门开展军队文职人员考试培训专项整治工作。 三、军队文职人员考试培训类广告不得对培训效果作出保证性承诺，不得明示或者暗示有关考试机构或者其工作人员、考试命题人员参加培训；禁止不明码标价、价格欺诈行为。 中央网络安全和信息化

items.title: Two Chinese Books Shortlisted for US National Translation Awards
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019103/Two Chinese Books Shortlisted for US National Translation Awards
items.summary: This week’s shortlist announcement included two works of prose originally written in Chinese. A separate Chinese anthology was also longlisted for the poetry prize last month.
items.body_text:
Two Chinese Books Shortlisted for US National Translation Awards
Two books translated into English from Chinese have been shortlisted for the 2026 U.S. National Translation Awards, which recognize excellence in both original and translated literary works.
The shortlist, announced Tuesday by the American Literary Translators Association, includes two originally written in Chinese: Chinese author Shuang Xuetao’s short story collection “Hunter,” translated by Jeremy Tiang, and Hong Kong writer Hon Lai Chu’s “Mending Bodies,” translated by Jacqueline Leung, among a total of 11 poetry and prose works translated from nine languages.
“The Ruins,” an anthology by Chinese poet Ye Hui and translated by Li Dong, was longlisted among 23 works across prose and poetry on Sept. 3 but did not make the shortlist. Ye is known for his spare, understated poems that draw on everyday life and nature and explore questions of time, memory, and existence.
Established in 1998, the awards rank among the world’s top professional accolades for literary translation. Winning translators in both categories — poetry and prose — each receive a $4,000 prize. Translations of Chinese works have previously been listed for the prize, including works by contemporary writers Xu Zechen and Yan Lianke, as well as Qing dynasty (1644–1911) novelist and playwright Li Yu.
Shuang Xuetao, author of “Hunter,” one of the two shortlisted Chinese works, was born in 1983 in Shenyang, capital of the northeastern Liaoning province. He is widely considered a leading figure in the “Dongbei Renaissance,” a cultural movement emerging from northeast China, or Dongbei. Known for his use of local dialect, Shuang often portrays the lives of ordinary people in the region, long dismissed as a cultural backwater and rust belt. Several of his works have been adapted into films.
“Hunter” features 11 standalone stories, some of which were originally written in Dongbei dialect: from provincial ambulance drivers searching for a hospital in the middle of the night, to a legendary knife fighter working in a factory. In a note about their selection published alongside the announcement, the competition’s judges wrote that Shuang’s stories “paint a portrait of a region marked by gritty pragmatism, dark humor, and magical realism.”
The work was translated by Shuang’s long-term collaborator Jeremy Tiang — a novelist in his own right. The judges wrote that Tiang “expertly translated Shuang’s often inventive, utterly unique description; his English texts are layered and witty.”
The second book nominated for the prize, “Mending Bodies” by Hong Kong writer Hon Lai Chu, is a work of speculative fiction and follows a young woman adjusting to life after surgically binding her body to a partner, in a future where people are encouraged to do so. Hon has previously drawn praise for her surreal, introspective fiction, which often explores the fragility of the body, memory, and human relationships.
According to the judges, Jacqueline Leung, the book’s Hong Kong-based translator, “flawlessly translates the between-the-lines subtleties of the languages.”
“The shortlisting of these works carries substantial significance for the overseas circulation of Sinophone literature and its greater visibility within global professional literary circuits, representing, in a sense, a multifaceted retelling of Chinese stories across fiction and poetry,” Shao Dong, an assistant professor of creative writing at Hong Kong Metropolitan University, told Sixth Tone.
The overall award winners will be announced on Oct. 23 as part of the American Literary Translators Association’s annual conference.
Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.
(Header image: Covers of “Hunter,” “Mending Bodies,” and “The Ruins,” by Shuang Xuetao, Hon Lai Chu, and Ye Hui, respectively. Reedited by Sixth Tone)

items.title: ‘Healing’ Chickens vs. Hungry Thieves: Art Students’ Project Ends in Tears
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019087/‘Healing’ Chickens vs. Hungry Thieves: Art Students’ Project Ends in Tears
items.summary: Students at a Chinese fine arts university had aimed to promote sustainability by raising chickens — but then a nighttime raid drew unwanted attention and a ban.
items.body_text:
‘Healing’ Chickens vs. Hungry Thieves: Art Students’ Project Ends in Tears
The thieves came in the dead of night in late August — seven ghostly figures illuminated only by the glow of their flashlights and burning cigarettes. When they left, tucked under their arms were 10 chickens and two geese.
The next day, watching footage of the theft recorded by a security camera, Xu Lingni’s heart sank. It was the end of a dream.
The poultry had been kept overnight in a hilltop coop at the bucolic Huxi campus of the Sichuan Fine Arts Institute (SCFAI), in the southwestern megacity of Chongqing, and belonged to the Happy Chick Feeding Cooperative, a student-led club aimed at rebuilding the bonds between humans and nature.
The group had intended to use the project to promote interest across campus and beyond in food-waste conversion, community-supported agriculture, plastics consumption, and other sustainability issues.
For Xu, the club’s leader, those plans vanished along with those 12 birds. Yet worse was to come.
After a brief investigation, the Chongqing police discovered that several workers hired by SCFAI for a summer construction project had taken the poultry and eaten them. Their crew manager agreed to pay 7,000 yuan ($1,040) to compensate for the financial loss and the students’ emotional distress.
However, the theft drew widespread attention and sparked fresh criticism over raising animals on campus. Facing mounting pressure, the school’s leadership decided to ban the practice. The cooperative was over.
Hatching a plan
The Happy Chick Feeding Cooperative was a key part of the Healing Garden Project, which inhabits a patch of land on campus once piled high with construction waste. Seven years ago, Jin Lipeng, an associate professor in SCFAI’s School of Experimental Art, led students in repurposing the debris to pave paths and build planting beds. He envisioned an area that could restore nature and nurture people.
At the time, the campus cafeteria was sending hundreds of kilograms of food scraps — often mixed with unsorted plastic waste — to an incinerator dozens of kilometers away. Jin and his students began to use these leftovers as compost, converting roughly 40 tons of food waste into fertilizer over the years.
The idea for the cooperative stemmed from a graduate student’s thesis project in spring 2025 that looked at permaculture and the role of foraging chickens in loosening soil, eating pests, clearing weeds, and providing eggs. To test a theory, the student purchased five chickens of a local breed with red combs and black skin. They were allowed to roam freely through campus and returned at night to their hilltop coop.
Xu, an undergraduate majoring in sculpture, was already involved in the garden project and began informally caring for the chickens, buying them grain and taking them to the veterinarian.
In summer last year, as temperatures soared above 40 degrees Celsius, one bird died of heatstroke, and three others disappeared. Fearing that the sole survivor would get lonely, Xu bought a new one from the market. Then one of the escapees returned.
A few days later, Xu found six new adolescent chickens in the coop. A school janitor, who had bought them to raise for their meat, agreed to sell the birds to the students. These were soon joined by a common chicken brought from a roadside stall, a Plymouth Rock chicken, a new hatchling, and a wuhei black-boned chicken. (Two birds died before the theft — one from hypothermia, the other from a wild animal attack. The wuhei chicken was the only one left behind by the thieves; its dark plumage likely made it hard to spot at night.)
As the flock grew, the birds began producing more eggs than the students could eat. Jin, whose research area includes labor issues, proposed creating the cooperative as a student club and asked Xu to lead it. items.title: China’s DeepZang AI Aims to Improve Tibetan Translation
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019100/China’s DeepZang AI Aims to Improve Tibetan Translation
items.summary: Released in March, the model, which can convert speech and writing between Tibetan, Mandarin Chinese, and English, will undergo a series of linguistic upgrades.
items.body_text:
China’s DeepZang AI Aims to Improve Tibetan Translation
DeepZang, China’s first Tibetan-language large language model, is being upgraded to better adapt to Tibetan dialects, enable real-time translation between Tibetan and Mandarin Chinese, and support offline use.
At a Monday seminar in Hohhot, capital of northern China’s Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, the model’s developer unveiled a series of upgrades scheduled between October and December. The seminar featured representatives from companies, research institutions, and universities.
DeepZang, developed by local technology company Choknor, was launched in March in Lhasa, capital of the southwestern Xizang Autonomous Region. Its app supports AI-powered conversations, translation, and speech transcription in Tibetan, Mandarin Chinese, and English.
At the model’s launch, organizations including the Xizang branches of China Mobile and the People’s Insurance Company of China, as well as Sichuan Minzu Publishing House, signed agreements with Choknor to promote its adoption.
According to Choknor, DeepZang has attracted nearly 400,000 users across Xizang, the northwestern Qinghai and Gansu provinces, and southwestern Sichuan province, where most of China’s Tibetan speakers reside.
The company has said the model has cut the time needed for some Tibetan-Chinese translation tasks involving two or three people from 40 minutes to just over 10 minutes for one person. It also reported that the model has been used in such varied settings as helping non-Tibetan-speaking doctors communicate with local patients, generating Tibetan-language contracts for yak sales, and assisting grassroots officials in drafting Tibetan work reports.
The model has been trained on nearly 70 million pairs of standardized Tibetan and Chinese texts, along with more than 30,500 hours of Tibetan speech covering its three major dialect groups — Ü-Tsang, Kham, and Amdo. The team collected the data from libraries, medical institutions, and monasteries, among other settings.
At Monday’s seminar, Choknor unveiled plans to develop offline language packages for Tibetan, Chinese, and English, allowing the app to function with limited or no internet access. The company also plans to pilot 50 simultaneous interpretation devices among at least 300 participants in Lhasa this December.
Tenzin Norbu, Choknor’s founder, said the company aims to bring DeepZang into “pastoral tents, tourist service counters, and grassroots hospitals,” enabling Tibetan speakers to “enjoy the benefits of artificial intelligence on an equal footing.”
Choknor said on Sunday that beyond fostering exchanges and integration among ethnic groups, DeepZang could help ensure the accuracy of Tibetan-language information and contribute to social stability and long-term security.
Founded in 2016, Choknor specializes in Tibetan-Chinese bilingual speech technology, scanning and translation tools, and optical character recognition. Its products include smart computer mice, scanning and translation pens, and an AI-powered Tibetan subtitling system.

items.title: NATO ‘Theory of Victory’ plan not directed against Russia — chairman of military committee
items.summary: The word ‘victory’ in this context means, first and foremost, just one thing: war will never begin because those who threaten us are convinced not to start it, Giuseppe Cavo Dragone said
items.body_text:
ROME, October 10. /TASS/. NATO’s new "Theory of Victory" plan is intended to ensure that "war never begins," Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, chairman of the NATO Military Committee, assured said in an interview with La Repubblica newspaper, responding to a question about criticism that the plan was a "provocation against Russia."
"The word ‘victory’ in this context means, first and foremost, just one thing: war will never begin because those who threaten us are convinced not to start it. That is precisely why we must demonstrate that our collective deterrence system is reliable and suited to current conditions," he said.
"Defense planning is not a provocation; it is the duty of any responsible military organization. [It is based] on the principle that deterrence is effective only when the adversary knows that an attack has no chance of success," Dragone explained. In his view, the best victory is one that does not have to be fought for.
NATO's military command has drawn up a new defense plan for the alliance's eastern flank, focusing on drones and artificial intelligence. Dubbed the "Theory of Victory," it will be presented to NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe Alexus Grynkewich on October 12. The plan aims to clarify responses to a "possible invasion of NATO territory" and emphasizes countering hybrid threats and deterrence through combat readiness.
Russia’s leadership has repeatedly rejected speculation that the country may attack NATO states by 2030. Russian President Vladimir Putin said last year that Moscow was ready to "formalize an agreement on mutual non-aggression with Western countries in order to address existing concerns in this regard." Later, at a TASS-organized meeting with the heads of leading global news agencies, the Russian leader stressed that claims of Moscow allegedly preparing to attack Europe were not merely nonsense, but a provocation and disinformation aimed at deceiving their own populations.

A major energy deal reached on Friday to export Russian diesel to the US and global markets, potentially easing an international fuel shortage, is an “immediate win” for both US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, Craig Pasta Jardula, host of the daily call-in show “Drive Time,” has told RT.

One of the biggest concerns in the US is oil prices, so this will boost market confidence at a time when markets have become increasingly unstable,” Jardula said.
Diesel prices affect agriculture, home heating, and trucking costs, and are near record highs, posing a risk for Trump’s fellow Republicans ahead of elections on November 3 that will determine whether they retain control of Congress. US diesel futures fell almost 5% following news of the deal and were trading at $4.64 a gallon.
Following the news, the US Treasury also issued a temporary sanctions waiver covering Russian diesel shipments until April 7, 2027.
The Ukraine conflict dominated much of the discussion between the presidents, with Putin briefing Trump on the situation along the front lines and Moscow’s response to Ukrainian “terrorist strikes” on energy infrastructure and civilian targets deep inside its territory.
Putin said Kiev had effectively derailed plans to resume trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the US, which the leaders had discussed holding after Russia’s State Duma elections. Kremlin foreign policy aide Yury Ushakov said Ukrainian drone attacks on polling stations and election officials had fundamentally changed the situation.
Moscow will now reconsider when negotiations can resume, according to the Kremlin aide.

Pentagon to livestream firing-squad execution of US Army psychiatrist who killed 13: Inside the scrutinized plan
US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth’s plan to livestream the firing-squad execution of former Army psychiatrist Nidal Hasan, who killed 13 people at the Fort Hood base in 2009, is set to become an unprecedented event in the nation’s history.
Approved by US President Donald Trump, the plan has drawn bipartisan criticism and condemnation from human rights advocates and religious leaders, who say it risks turning an execution into a public spectacle.
What happened at Fort Hood
The fatal shooting occurred on November 5, 2009, at Fort Hood’s Soldier Readiness Processing Center in Texas, where troops prepared for overseas deployment. US Army Major Nidal Malik Hasan, a 39-year-old military psychiatrist, opened fire with two semiautomatic pistols, killing 12 service members and one civilian Defense Department employee, and wounding 32 more.
Military police injured Hasan by returned fire, leaving the shooter paralyzed from the waist down before taking him into custody. A US Senate report designated the spree killing as the deadliest terrorist attack on US soil since September 11, 2001.
The man behind the Fort Hood shooting
Born in the US in 1970 to Palestinian immigrant parents, Hasan trained as a doctor before becoming an Army psychiatrist. Before the shooting, he served at Walter Reed Army Medical Center in Maryland, where he worked with service members, including those returning from combat zones. By 2009, he had attained the rank of major and was preparing for a transfer to Afghanistan.
Was the shooting part of a wider plot?
Hasan said he had acted in the name of jihad, and witnesses reported that he shouted “Allahu akbar” (“God is greatest”) during the shooting. Authorities examined the attack in the context of Islamic extremism, while the FBI said in the days immediately after the shooting that it had found no evidence of accomplices or a wider terrorist plot. Investigators continued examining the circumstances that led Hasan to carry out the attack.
In the years before the attack, Hasan exchanged emails with Anwar al-Awlaki, a radical cleric linked to al-Qaeda. The FBI reviewed some of their correspondence but initially concluded that the available information did not indicate Hasan was involved in terrorist activity. A subsequent review found serious failures in how the FBI and the US Department of Defense had assessed and shared information about him, concluding that the agencies had enough information to identify signs of his radicalization but had failed to act on it.
From conviction to execution date
In August 2013, a military court found Hasan guilty of 13 counts of premeditated murder and 32 counts of attempted premeditated murder. Later that month, a panel of 13 senior military officers unanimously sentenced him to death, ordering his dismissal from the Army and forfeiture of all pay and allowances. Hasan has since been held on military death row at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas.
Earlier this week, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Hasan would be executed by a firing squad of soldiers at Fort Hood on December, 3, at 1 PM – the same time the 2009 shooting began. Hegseth added that the execution would be livestreamed “because people need to understand there’s serious consequences for these types of things.”
Livestream plan draws bipartisan backlash
The plan has drawn criticism from lawmakers across party lines, religious leaders and the United Nations’ human rights office, which warned on Friday that broadcasting the execution would amount to “breach the absolute prohibition of torture.”
Republican Senator Thom Tillis called the proposal “beyond disgusting,” while Democratic Senator Chris Murphy likened public executions to those carried out by terrorist groups. items.title: ‘Goebbels is applauding’: Israel attacks Nobel committee for honoring Gaza genocide investigator
items.summary: West Jerusalem has been angered by the awarding of the Nobel Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, claiming that it legitimizes “anti-Israeli hatred” Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
‘Goebbels is applauding’: Israel attacks Nobel committee for honoring Gaza genocide investigator
Israel is angry that the Nobel Peace Prize committee has honored Navanethem ‘Navi’ Pillay, who chaired a UN commission accusing it of genocide in Gaza. Nazi propagandist Joseph Goebbels would have welcomed the decision, the Israelis said.
The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory concluded in September 2025 that Israel was “responsible for the commission of four genocidal acts in Gaza with the specific intent to destroy Palestinians in Gaza.” Israel vigorously disputed the findings of Pillay’s team.
A year earlier, the International Criminal Court (ICC) issued an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity committed in Gaza, including intentional targeting of civilians and using starvation as a method of warfare.
Wednesday marked three years since Israel launched its military operation in Gaza, with more than 74,000 people, including at least 21,000 children, being killed and over 175,000 wounded in airstrikes and a ground offensive in the Palestinian enclave, according to data from the local Health Ministry.
The UN says that some 1.98 million or 90% of the enclave’s population was displaced due to Israeli military attacks since October 7, 2023, with most of Gaza’s water and sanitation network damaged or destroyed.
Israel sent its forces into Gaza in retaliation for an incursion by Palestinian armed group Hamas, in which some 1,200 people lost their lives and 250 others were taken hostage.
The Norwegian Nobel Committee announced on Friday that the 125th Nobel Peace Prize would go to Pillay for “her efforts to promote peace and international law.” The 85-year-old South African lawyer, who was an ICC judge between 2003 and 2008, “has been instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted,” it said.
The Israeli Foreign Ministry said in a post on X later in the day that honoring Pillay was a “grotesque weaponization of an award to legitimize anti-Israel hatred and prejudice.” The jurist was responsible for a “relentless, politically motivated demonization of Israel,” it claimed.
The ministry called the accusations of genocide against Israel “the biggest lie of the 21st century,” saying that “Joseph Goebbels is certainly applauding from hell” the decision by the Nobel committee.
Goebbels was a loyal follower of Adolf Hitler and Nazi Germany’s propaganda minister between 1933 and 1945, who advocated the extermination of Jews.
The office of the Israeli prime minister suggested that the Nobel committee “has lost its moral compass” by giving the prize “to a bigot who built her career around inventing and propagating blood libels against the one and only Jewish state.”
Pillay, who currently sits on the International Court of Justice (ICJ), denied that she held any bias against Israel.
After being told by journalists that she had been awarded the prize, the jurist recalled that she was surprised when people complemented her on her courage for calling out Israeli actions in Gaza as genocide.
“Why would you need courage to speak the truth? You interpret the law. You look at all the facts, so it’s an impartial decision,” she insisted.

items.title: Germany Sticks to Russia Sanctions After Trump Diesel Announcement
items.summary: Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to the global market to ease fuel prices. Kyiv's allies are not supportive.
items.body_text:
Germany said on Saturday it would maintain sanctions against Russia over its war on Ukraine following United States President Donald Trump's announcement that his administration had temporarily lifted U.S. sanctions on Russian fuel.
"The federal government has taken note of the U.S. decision relating to Russian diesel deliveries," government spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said in a statement.
He said Germany's position remained clear: "The federal government remains committed to the decisions on sanctions against Russia and is working with its European partners on further sanctions."
He said Germany's support for Ukraine was unchanged and diplomatic efforts to reach a solution would continue.
Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices. He said his administration temporarily lifted U.S. sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its war on Ukraine.
Prices for diesel, used for agriculture, heating homes and trucking, have risen to near record levels, posing a risk for Trump's fellow Republicans ahead of the November 3 congressional elections that will determine whether they maintain thin control of Congress.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who visited Kyiv last weekend, has said repeatedly that Germany, Ukraine's largest European donor, would not reduce its support for the Kyiv government.

items.title: Rosatom Says it Wins Tribunal Ruling in Finnish Nuclear Plant Dispute
items.summary: Rosatom said the International Chamber of Commerce agreed that a Finnish firm wrongly terminated the contract for a new nuclear power plant.
items.body_text:
Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom said on Saturday that an International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) tribunal had ruled in its favour in a long-running dispute with Finnish utility Fennovoima over the cancelled Hanhikivi-1 nuclear power project.
Rosatom said the tribunal found that Fennovoima had unlawfully terminated the contract for the construction of the planned plant in northern Finland in 2022.
The parties have been locked in legal disputes since Fennovoima scrapped the 7 billion euro ($7.8 billion) project in May 2022, citing significant delays and political risks shortly after Russia launched its conflict in Ukraine.
Rosatom said the tribunal found that the project was making good progress when it was terminated.
"Today's victory is important, but not final. We will continue to prove that we are right regarding the Finnish project in courts of various instances," Rosatom Director General Alexey Likhachev said in a statement.
Fennovoima did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The contract to build the 1.2 gigawatt plant was signed in 2013 with Fennovoima, a consortium in which Finnish stakeholders including Fortum, Outokumpu and SSAB originally controlled two thirds through a joint venture, and the Russian side held one third.
After the project's termination, Fennovoima wound down its operations and is primarily engaged in legal proceedings.

items.title: Putin Downplayed Immediate Ukraine Talks Resumption in Phone Call With Trump, Kremlin Says
items.summary: The Kremlin also said Putin and Trump discussed major economic initiatives during the phone call, including potential supplies of Russian fuel.
items.body_text:
Russian President Vladimir Putin told U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday that Kyiv had undermined the possibility of an immediate resumption of trilateral Ukraine peace talks after it had hit Moscow with drones during last month's election, the Kremlin said.
Trump has so far unsuccessfully tried to broker a peace deal to end the war in Ukraine, which started with Russia's invasion in February 2022.
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Thursday that Russia's war in Ukraine is at a dangerous stalemate and the United States will keep working toward a settlement to end the conflict.
Putin had said that Moscow had been ready to resume negotiations with Kyiv after last month's Russian parliamentary elections, but Ukraine launched attacks on Moscow and hit polling stations, putting the peace process in jeopardy, according to him.
"By launching a massive drone attack on Moscow, other cities and polling stations, as well as on specific individuals involved in organizing the election, on the main voting day, the Kyiv regime effectively disrupted the possibility of an immediate resumption of the negotiation process," Kremlin foreign policy aide Yury Ushakov said about the call with Trump.
"And now, as the president said, we will consider when those negotiations can be resumed," he added, referring to trilateral negotiations involving the U.S., Russia and Ukraine.
Ushakov also said Putin and Trump discussed major economic initiatives during the phone call, including potential supplies of Russian fuel.
Trump said earlier on Friday after the call with Putin that Russia had agreed to immediately supply diesel to U.S. and global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections next month, although analysts said the amounts would likely not reduce prices greatly.
