items.title: ‘We’re being used as a front,’ Zelensky says of Trump’s diesel deal with Putin
items.summary: Russia and the U.S. have agreed on a deal to supply Russian diesel fuel to the U.S. and global markets. President Donald Trump announced the agreement on the evening of October 9 after a phone call with Vladimir Putin. Trump called the talks “highly successful.” Putin confirmed that Russia is ready to supply oil and petroleum products to the U.S. and global markets.
items.body_text:
Russia and the U.S. have agreed on a deal to supply Russian diesel fuel to the U.S. and global markets. President Donald Trump announced the agreement on the evening of October 9 after a phone call with Vladimir Putin. Trump called the talks “highly successful.” Putin confirmed that Russia is ready to supply oil and petroleum products to the U.S. and global markets.
The U.S. said it is easing sanctions on Russian diesel. The Treasury Department has already issued a temporary license allowing sales of Russian diesel on the global market through April 7, 2027, despite U.S. sanctions. Washington previously eased sanctions on Russian oil temporarily because of a market crisis caused by the U.S. and Israeli war with Iran.
Russia has also begun lifting restrictions on diesel exports, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said. Sanctions and domestic export bans restrict exports of Russian oil and petroleum products worldwide. A ban on diesel and marine fuel exports by producers, for example, remains in effect through the end of October. Russia imposed it amid Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries and a domestic fuel crisis caused by Ukrainian attacks over the summer.
Trump said the two sides agreed on the “immediate” delivery of more than 300,000 metric tons of Russian diesel. Russia will supply another 500,000 metric tons in November, followed by an additional million metric tons. Novak said Russia is ready to supply additional diesel to the U.S. market as early as October. Exports are also expected to rise in November and December as refineries resume operations after repairs.
Ukraine criticized the diesel deal between Moscow and Washington. President Volodymyr Zelensky wrote on social media that any easing of sanctions on Russia without agreements on de-escalation shows “obvious weakness.” “Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world. Russia will ‘repay’ the diesel with further terror and perfidy. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged. Russian authorities asked the U.S. to lift sanctions as part of talks on an “energy truce,” sources told The Kyiv Independent on the eve of the diesel deal. items.body_text:
Trump says he’s reached a deal with Putin to supply Russian diesel to U.S. and global markets. Zelensky calls it ‘an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged.’
U.S. President Donald Trump said he had reached a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to supply Russian diesel fuel to U.S. and global markets. Trump said they reached the agreement during “highly successful” talks by phone.
Russia agreed to supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel fuel to U.S. and global markets as soon as possible, Trump said. It will supply another 500,000 metric tons in November and 1 million metric tons “immediately thereafter.”
“Based on the condition of their Diesel Refineries,” Moscow could also supply another 3 million metric tons of diesel “within a short period of time,” Trump said.
Trump’s announcement came as the U.S. Treasury Department issued a temporary license allowing Russian diesel fuel to be supplied to the global market until April 7, 2027.
“Thanks to our total control of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!” Trump said.
In a response on social media, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the diesel deal “an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged”:
Exports of Russian oil and petroleum products to countries around the world are restricted by sanctions and Russia’s own export bans. For example, a ban on producers exporting diesel fuel, marine fuel, and gas oil remains in effect until the end of October.
Sources told Interfax on October 6 that Russian authorities were considering partially lifting the ban on diesel exports for some producers that month.
Ukraine has also been striking Russian oil refineries. These attacks caused a fuel crisis in Russia during the summer of 2026. Donald Trump has repeatedly urged Zelensky to stop attacking Russian oil facilities. According to Trump, the strikes are causing a global fuel shortage and driving up prices.

items.title: Ukrainian drone alert disrupts Russian government flights returning from Putin’s Turkmenistan trip
items.summary: Several aircraft from Russia’s Rossiya Special Flight Detachment, which transports the country’s leaders and senior officials, circled over Moscow on the evening of October 9 because of the threat of a Ukrainian drone attack.
items.body_text:
Ukrainian drone alert disrupts Russian government flights returning from Putin’s Turkmenistan trip
Several aircraft from Russia’s Rossiya Special Flight Detachment, which transports the country’s leaders and senior officials, circled over Moscow on the evening of October 9 because of the threat of a Ukrainian drone attack.
Five of the detachment’s aircraft were unable to land immediately. At least three were returning from Turkmenistan, where Russian President Vladimir Putin had attended a Commonwealth of Independent States summit, several Russian news outlets and Telegram channels reported (1, 2, 3). All three were Il-96s, the type used to transport the president, Agentstvo reported.
According to Flightradar24, two Il-96s with registration numbers RA-96020 and RA-96022 circled over Moscow and the surrounding region. They departed Turkmenbashi Airport at 2 p.m. and 2:15 p.m. and landed at Moscow’s Vnukovo Airport at 6:06 p.m. and 6:21 p.m., respectively.
A third Il-96, with registration number RA-96025, departed Turkmenbashi at 3:52 p.m. and flew over Moscow even though it was scheduled to land at Vnukovo. It was eventually diverted to St. Petersburg’s Pulkovo Airport and later departed for Moscow.
Restrictions were imposed at all Moscow airports around 3:40 p.m. and fully lifted by 6:40 p.m. According to estimates from Ostorozhno, Novosti, more than 200 flights were delayed and more than 100 canceled amid the restrictions.
It is unclear which aircraft Putin was aboard. At 1:52 p.m., TASS reported that the president had ended his visit to Turkmenistan and boarded one of the Rossiya detachment’s aircraft, which was preparing to depart Turkmenbashi. Agentstvo suggested that Putin may have been aboard RA-96025. He had flown to Turkmenistan on that aircraft on October 8.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky had threatened to “close the skies” over Russia in early September. Putin called the statement “a signal of intent to commit state terrorism.” In response to Ukraine’s threats, Russia’s Transport Ministry said the country’s aviation services would prevent “significant disruptions” to civil aviation.

items.title: Russian attacks kill 11 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the U.S.-Russia diesel deal a “weak decision” that would help Moscow prolong the war, as Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia killed three children among the dead
items.body_text:
Russian strikes killed at least 11 people in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, officials said on Saturday (October 10, 2026), a day after U.S. President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel that Kyiv warned would help bankroll Moscow’s war in Ukraine.
Three children were among the 11 people killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Mykhailo Semikin, head of the regional military administration, said on Saturday. At least 16 people were wounded in the attack, according to Ivan Fedorov, co-chair of the region’s defence council.
Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war, while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4.5 years since Moscow’s full-scale invasion. Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 60 people over the past four days.
The latest attacks came a day after Mr. Trump said he had struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a sharp reversal of years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine, and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections.
Mr. Trump said on social media on Friday (October 9, 2026) that he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call in which he had been expected to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia. Instead, Mr. Trump announced that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tonnes in November 2026, and 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter.” Russia would deliver an additional 3 million tonnes “within a short period of time” after that, he wrote.
Mr. Trump’s announcement was in stark contrast to a sweeping Russia sanctions law he signed last month, which aimed to clamp down on the oil and gas revenues that fuel Russia’s war against Ukraine.
In a lengthy post online reacting to the deal, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia would repay it “with further terror and perfidy.” He described it as an investment in the war, allowing it to be prolonged. “It plays into Russia’s hands — allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world,” he said.
According to a statement released by the Ukrainian Embassy in Washington, Mr. Zelenskyy called it “a weak decision, unfortunately, a weak decision by strong partners.”
Mr. Trump announced the deal as his envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner were meeting Ukrainian officials in Miami to discuss a proposal to end the war. “I believe our team is simply being used as a smoke screen. And that is certainly not fair. It is certainly not how partners should treat each other,” Mr. Zelenskyy said.
Published - October 10, 2026 04:24 pm IST

Elon Musk on Saturday (October 10, 2026) stepped up his attack against industrialist Mukesh Ambani, sharing screenshots of media reports alleging that a Reliance-funded firm helped boost BJP campaigns on social media and that a Reliance-linked company made large political donations to the ruling party.

The latest post comes amid Mr. Musk's scathing criticism of Mukesh Ambani over a persistent delay in the launch of Starlink satellite broadband services in India.
Reliance has not publicly responded to Mr. Musk's allegations, while the government has maintained that the country's authorisation framework for telecom and satellite services is "fair and non-discriminatory" and that any suggestion that it was being applied selectively was "baseless and misconceived."
A few hours before he made the post, Mr. Musk on X addressed Mukesh Ambani as "Prime Minister Ambani" and accused him of protecting a monopoly. Mr. Musk wondered if Mr. Ambani would consider allowing his satellite internet service to compete with his entity in the country.
On Friday (October 9, 2026), Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia asserted that India does not permit monopolies in any sector, and that despite the buzz around one particular company, three players have received satcom licences and can start operations after meeting the security requirements and milestones.
Mr. Musk has alleged that powerful business interests are seeking to block his service to preserve their dominance in the Indian market. He said his Starlink was being blocked by certain oligarchs seeking to "maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people."
"Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realising that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?" he wrote.
Mr. Musk also said many areas of India have no internet access, and the absence denies children education and small businesses the opportunity to sell their goods to a global market.
Starlink would change their lives for the better, the technocrat asserted.
Within minutes of that post late Friday evening (October 9, 2026), Mr. Musk wrote another, saying Starlink has proven to be essential in saving lives during natural disasters throughout the world, when all other communication systems failed. "So you would also be helping save men, women and children throughout India," he added.
Mr. Scindia has said India doesn't allow monopoly in any sector.
"Let me set the record straight. For us, the Department of Telecommunications, we are technology-agnostic... Our job is to be able to provide the bouquet of services to every single customer. It is for the customer to choose in a free market which service he or she prefers, and within that service bouquet, which company's service he or she prefers," the Union minister said at a briefing at the India Mobile Congress here.
Mr. Scindia said three entities - Mr. Musk's Starlink, Reliance Jio's satellite venture Jio Satcom, Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb - have already secured licences, while Amazon's Project Kuiper has expressed interest and will need to follow the established procedure.
While there is a lot of conversation about one particular company, three have got satcom licences, he said.

items.title: Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro and HCL among IT firms suspended from U.S. green card programme
items.summary: The Department of Labour is also suspending Microsoft and Adobe from the PERM programme
items.body_text:
The U.S. on Thursday (October 8, 2026) suspended IT firms Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe from the Permanent Labour Certification Programme, which allows companies to apply for green cards for H-1B visa workers.
The announcement was made by U.S. Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling, with Vice-President J.D. Vance, the head of the U.S. Anti-Fraud Task Force, by his side.
“I am hereby suspending from the Permanent Labour Certification Programme some of the largest IT outsourcing firms in the world, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, and Capgemini,” Mr. Sonderling said.
He said the Department of Labour is also suspending Microsoft and Adobe from the program.
“We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labour certification applications involving these companies. Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost three million foreign workers. They’ve received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labour certifications,” Mr. Sonderling said.
“That’s hundreds of thousands of jobs that were taken from American workers,” Mr. Sonderling said.

items.title: जंतर-मंतर नहीं पहुंच पाए प्रदर्शनकारी, लीडर्स हिरासत में:38 हजार सुरक्षाकर्मी, 10 फीट ऊंचे बैरिकेड्स; पुलिस ने प्रदर्शन कैसे रोका, 7 पॉइंट्स में
items.summary: दिल्ली पुलिस की सख्ती की वजह से शाम 5 बजे तक कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी के प्रदर्शनकारी जंतर-मंतर तक नहीं पहुंच पाए। पुलिस ने सीजेपी की लीडरशिप अभिजीत दीपके, सौरव दास और आशुतोष रांका को सुबह ही एयरपोर्ट पर हिरासत में ले लिया। पार्टी ने सुबह 10 बजे जंतर-मंतर पर प्रदर्शन बुलाया था। समर्थकों ने यहां पहुंचने की कोशिश भी की, लेकिन कई जगह 3 से 5 लेयर की बैरिकडिंग की वजह से आगे नहीं बढ़ने दिया। अब तक 3500 लोगों को कस्टडी में लिया गया। इस दौरान ममता बनर्जी, अरविंद केजरीवाल को भी हिरासत में लिया गया। पुलिस से झड़प
items.body_text:
- Hindi News
- National
- Jantar Mantar Protest LIVE | CJP CEC Gyanesh Kumar SIR Row Violence Photos Update; Abhijeet Dipke Rahul Gandhi Vs Delhi Police BJP Congress
LIVEजंतर-मंतर नहीं पहुंच पाए प्रदर्शनकारी, लीडर्स हिरासत में:38 हजार सुरक्षाकर्मी, 10 फीट ऊंचे बैरिकेड्स; पुलिस ने प्रदर्शन कैसे रोका, 7 पॉइंट्स में
- कॉपी लिंक
दिल्ली पुलिस की सख्ती की वजह से शाम 5 बजे तक कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी के प्रदर्शनकारी जंतर-मंतर तक नहीं पहुंच पाए। पुलिस ने सीजेपी की लीडरशिप अभिजीत दीपके, सौरव दास और आशुतोष रांका को सुबह ही एयरपोर्ट पर हिरासत में ले लिया।
पार्टी ने सुबह 10 बजे जंतर-मंतर पर प्रदर्शन बुलाया था। समर्थकों ने यहां पहुंचने की कोशिश भी की, लेकिन कई जगह 3 से 5 लेयर की बैरिकडिंग की वजह से आगे नहीं बढ़ने दिया। अब तक 3500 लोगों को कस्टडी में लिया गया। इस दौरान ममता बनर्जी, अरविंद केजरीवाल को भी हिरासत में लिया गया।
पुलिस से झड़प की एक या दो घटनाएं सामने आईं। प्रदर्शनकारियों ने बैरिकेडिंग भी तोड़ी। आकाशवाणी भवन के पास पत्थर फेंके, जिससे 2 पुलिसकर्मी घायल हो गए।
CJP ने मतदाता सूची में गड़बड़ियों और SIR के विरोध में मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग को लेकर जंतर-मंतर पर प्रदर्शन का आह्वान किया था।
प्रदर्शन के पहले और बाद की 3 तस्वीरें…
पुलिस ने 'कॉकरोच' का प्रदर्शन कैसे रोका, 7 पॉइंट्स में
1. 38 हजार जवान तैनात: 8 से 12 अक्टूबर तक CAPF की 221 कंपनियां यानी करीब 23 हजार जवान बुलाए गए। इनके अलावा दिल्ली पुलिस के कम से कम 15 हजार कर्मियों की तैनाती की योजना बनाई गई।
2. दिल्ली आने वाली ट्रेनें रद्द, बसों की बुकिंग की जांच: शनिवार को सुबह 4 बजे से दोपहर 2 बजे तक आने वाली 250 ट्रेनें रद्द की गईं। बसों की बुकिंग की जांच शुरू की गई, ताकि पता चल सके कि कौन वाहन किराए पर ले रहा है और कितने लोग दिल्ली आने वाले हैं।
3. छात्रों को रोकने की अपील: यूनिवर्सिटी-कॉलेज प्रमुखों और PG मालिकों से संपर्क कर छात्रों को प्रदर्शन में शामिल होने से रोकने की अपील की गई।
4. मेट्रो स्टेशन बंद, बैरिकेडिंग: 10 अक्टूबर को 45 मेट्रो स्टेशनों पर एंट्री और एग्जिट बंद रखने की व्यवस्था की गई। जंतर-मंतर से पहले ही 10 फीट ऊंचे बैरिकेड लगाए गए। आंसू गैस की गाड़ियां भी तैनात की गईं।
5. दिल्ली के बॉर्डर पर सख्ती: दूसरे राज्यों से आने वाले रास्तों पर जांच बढ़ाई गई। यूपी से लगी पूर्वी दिल्ली और शाहदरा सीमा के साथ राजस्थान से आने वाले रूट पर भी नजर रखी गई। कीलें और बैरिकेड लगाए गए।
6. बॉडीकैम से रिकॉर्डिंग, अस्थायी हिरासत केंद्र की तैयारी: झड़पों की रिकॉर्डिंग के लिए फ्रंटलाइन पर तैनात पुलिसकर्मियों को 150 बॉडीकैम दिए गए। प्रदर्शनकारियों को रखने के लिए स्टेडियम में अस्थायी हिरासत केंद्र बनाए गए।
7. दीपके फ्लाइट से ही हिरासत में, रास्ते में ही कार्यकर्ताओं को रोका: अभिजीत दीपके, आशुतोष रांका और सौरव दास को फ्लाइट से ही हिरासत में लिया गया। CJP कार्यकर्ताओं को जंतर-मंतर पहुंचने से पहले ही पकड़ा गया।

विजुअल गाइडअभिजीत दीपके की गिरफ्तारी का अनकट VIDEO:महिला पुलिस फ्लाइट में घुसी; CJP लीडर बोले- हम डरते नहीं, हाथ पकड़कर निकाला
- कॉपी लिंक
कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी के फाउंडर अभिजीत दीपके को मुंबई से दिल्ली पहुंची फ्लाइट के अंदर से ही हिरासत में ले लिया गया। उनके साथ CJP नेता सौरव दास और आशुतोष रांका को भी पुलिस अपने साथ ले गई। वे मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के खिलाफ जंतर-मंतर पर होने वाले प्रदर्शन में शामिल होने दिल्ली पहुंचे थे।
फ्लाइट के अंदर से एक वीडियो सामने आया है। इसमें महिला पुलिसकर्मी दीपके और CJP के दूसरे नेताओं को हिरासत में लेते दिख रही हैं।
दो मिनट के वीडियो में क्या-क्या हुआ…
वीडियो में दीपके कहते सुनाई देते हैं, “आप देख सकते हैं कि देश किस दिशा में जा रहा है। हमें फ्लाइट में ही हिरासत में लिया जा रहा है। ऐसा तो कभी इंदिरा गांधी ने भी नहीं किया था। यह तानाशाही है, लेकिन हम इनसे डरते नहीं हैं।”
दीपके पुलिसकर्मियों की ओर इशारा करते हुए कहते हैं, “आओ, हमें गिरफ्तार कर लो। हम गिरफ्तार होने ही आए हैं। मैं आपसे डरता नहीं हूं। हम गिरफ्तारी के लिए तैयार हैं।”
इस पर एक पुलिसकर्मी जवाब देती हैं, “नहीं, यह गिरफ्तारी नहीं है। सर, कृपया कॉपरेट करें।”
इसके बाद दीपके और फ्लाइट में बैठे उनके साथियों ने ‘भारत माता की जय’ के नारे लगाए। दीपके ने ‘इंकलाब जिंदाबाद’ के नारे भी लगाए।
फ्लाइट में महिला पुलिसकर्मी आगे खड़ी थीं। दीपके ने उनसे कहा, “आप लोग फ्लाइट में कैसे आ गए?” वहीं, पुलिसकर्मी उनसे बाहर आने के लिए कहती रहीं।
आशुतोष और दीपके ने पुलिस से पुरुष पुलिसकर्मियों को आगे करने के लिए कहा। इस पर महिला पुलिसकर्मी उनसे बाहर आने का अनुरोध करती रहीं।
आशुतोष और सौरभ दास के बाद महिला पुलिसकर्मियों ने दीपके को बाहर ले जाने की कोशिश की। इस दौरान दीपके ने हाथ जोड़कर कहा, “मुझे अपना फोन तो लेने दीजिए। मैं अपना बैग ले लूं। मैं गिरफ्तार होने ही आया हूं।”
इसके बाद पुलिस दीपके और उनके साथियों को फ्लाइट से बाहर ले गई। इस दौरान दीपके कहते सुनाई दिए, “कौन-सी जेल में डालोगे? राजस्थान की? NSA या UAPA, जो लगाना है लगाओ।”

124 पूर्व ब्यूरोक्रेट्स बोले- चुनाव प्रक्रिया पर भरोसा रखें:हमने वोट धांधली का भी दौर देखा है: 2 दिन पहले 42 पूर्व जजों ने लेटर लिखा था
- कॉपी लिंक
पूर्व विदेश सचिव कंवल सिब्बल समेत 124 पूर्व नौकरशाहों ने भारत की चुनावी प्रक्रिया के समर्थन में देश की जनता के नाम लेटर लिखा है।
पूर्व राजदूतों और रिटायर्ड IAS अधिकारियों ने लिखा, “हम यह पत्र इसलिए लिख रहे हैं, क्योंकि आजकल हमारे चुनावों के लिए बिना किसी सबूत के ‘धांधली’ शब्द का इस्तेमाल किया जा रहा है। इस शब्द को बार-बार दोहराने से लोकतंत्र में लोगों का वह भरोसा कमजोर होता है।”
यह पत्र ऐसे समय आया है, जब चुनाव आयोग और मतदाता सूची के SIR को लेकर राजनीतिक विवाद चल रहा है। विपक्ष के साथ कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी ने प्रदर्शन कर रही है। 8 अक्टूबर को ज्ञानेश कुमार के सपोर्ट में 42 पूर्व जजों ने लेटर लिखा था।
बूथ कैप्चरिंग से फर्जी वोटिंग तक का जिक्र
लेटर में पूर्व अधिकारियों ने चुनावों में गड़बड़ी के पुराने तरीकों का जिक्र किया। उन्होंने वह दौर देखा है, जब बूथ पर हथियार लेकर पहुंचना, बाहुबलियों के जरिए मतदाताओं को प्रभावित करना, फर्जी वोट डालना, बैलेट बॉक्स चुराना और लोगों को मतदान से रोकना जैसी घटनाएं होती थीं। पत्र में कहा गया कि बूथ कैप्चरिंग की समस्या इतनी व्यापक थी कि संसद ने 1989 में इसे अपराध घोषित किया।
सुप्रीम कोर्ट के जजों के बयान भी चर्चा में
- 4 अक्टूबर: जस्टिस उज्जल भुइयां ने कहा- वोटिंग से रोकने वाली प्रक्रिया मनमानी: सुप्रीम कोर्ट के सिटिंग जज जस्टिस उज्जल भुइयां ने 4 अक्टूबर को NALSAR यूनिवर्सिटी में कहा था कि लाखों भारतीय नागरिकों को वोट देने के अधिकार से वंचित करने वाली कोई भी प्रक्रिया मूल रूप से मनमानी है।
- 5 अक्टूबर- पूर्व CJI गवई बोले- विचाराधीन मामले पर बयान मर्यादा के खिलाफ: पूर्व जस्टिस गवई ने कहा कि किसी लंबित मामले पर सुप्रीम कोर्ट के मौजूदा जज को सार्वजनिक टिप्पणी नहीं करनी चाहिए। यह न्यायिक मर्यादा के खिलाफ है। दिल्ली हाईकोर्ट के दो रिटायर्ड जजों ने भी ऐसा बयान देने से पहले हजार बार सोचना चाहिए था।
- 8 अक्टूबर- पूर्व सुप्रीम कोर्ट जज वी. गोपाला गौड़ा बोले- SIR पर फैसला वापस लिया जाए: पूर्व जज वी. गोपाला गौड़ा ने कहा- ‘SIR पर आया फैसला वापस लिया जाना चाहिए। यह गैरकानूनी, असंवैधानिक और अलोकतांत्रिक है। सुप्रीम कोर्ट को इलेक्शन कमीशन से सभी रिकॉर्ड मंगाने चाहिए। इससे पता चलेगा कि SIR का फैसला पूरे आयोग ने बहुमत वाले चुनाव आयुक्तों की सहमति और मंजूरी से लिया था या नहीं।'
2000 नागरिक SIR रोकने लेटर लिख चुके
इससे पहले सितंबर में 2,000 से ज्यादा नागरिकों ने एक ओपन लेटर में कोर्ट से SIR रोकने की अपील की थी। उन्होंने इसकी वैधता और प्रक्रिया की स्वतंत्र जांच होने तक अभियान रोकने की मांग की थी।
CJI सूर्यकांत को लिखे लेटर में साइन करने वालों ने वोटर लिस्ट के मैनेजमेंट और ECINet प्लेटफॉर्म से जुड़ी गड़बड़ियों की कोर्ट की निगरानी में जांच की मांग की थी।
लेटर पर दस्तखत करने वालों में पूर्व नौसेना प्रमुख एडमिरल विष्णु भागवत, पूर्व आईएएस अधिकारी अदिति मेहता, वरिष्ठ वकील प्रशांत भूषण, इतिहासकार आदित्य मुखर्जी और अभिनेता प्रकाश राज सहित शिक्षाविद, वकील, पत्रकार और सामाजिक कार्यकर्ता शामिल थे।
SIR और चुनाव पैनल से जुड़ी याचिकाएं लंबित
SIR प्रक्रिया से जुड़ी याचिकाएं सुप्रीम कोर्ट में लंबित हैं। इसके अलावा चुनाव पैनल से जुड़े नए कानून की वैधता पर भी सुनवाई बाकी है। इस नए कानून में मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त के चयन पैनल से CJI को बाहर रखा गया है।
हालांकि सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने 5 अक्टूबर की सुनवाई में उन्हें निलंबित करने का अंतरिम आदेश देने से तो इनकार किया, लेकिन चुनाव आयोग को नोटिस जारी कर जवाब मांगा है। कोर्ट ने कहा कि अगर फैसले बिना सहमति के लिए पाए गए, तो उन्हें वापस लिया जा सकता है। पढ़ें पूरी खबर…
----------

items.body_text:
CJP Delhi Protest Live: 3,000 detained, defiant CJP tells protesters to march on to Jantar Mantar
CJP Delhi protest Live: Party posts video of police detaining its members
The detentions continue in Delhi, with the police detaining key members of the Cockroach Janta Party, which has called for a protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar.
CJP’S TEAM FORCEFULLY DETAINED! Delhi Police is pushing, dragging and detaining people for peacefully protesting! Is peacefully raising your voice a crime now? https://t.co/EfUle4X9iG
— Cockroach Janta Party - CJP (@Cockroachisback) October 10, 2026
CJP protest Live: Institutions must remain accountable, says Karnataka CM
Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar said young people raising concerns deserved to be heard, “not silenced”. He called for institutional accountability and the protection of every citizen’s right to speak, question and peacefully dissent.
Youth of India, we're with you: Rahul Gandhi's message as cops crack down on CJP protest
Rahul Gandhi attacked Narendra Modi, Amit Shah and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as Opposition protests intensified in Delhi over the electoral roll revision exercise. The remarks came amid mass detentions and fresh Opposition claims that peaceful dissent and voting rights are under threat. Read more here.
CJP protest Live: What Imran Khan said before being detained

items.body_text:
No trains, no internet for UPI: Rail passengers in Delhi face CJP protest pain
The public announcement system at the New Delhi Railway Station was busy announcing one train cancellation after another. The suspension of mobile internet meant no UPI and no news updates. Railway passengers were caught in the crossfire as the Cockroach Janta Party's planned protest and the security clampdown left them stranded far from home without a Plan B.
The heat was unforgiving in the national capital, the trains were cancelled, and even a lemon soda came with an unexpected problem. At New Delhi Railway Station on Saturday, 23-year-old Abhinav had one more thing to worry about after finding out that he had forgotten his wallet. With internet services suspended, completing a UPI payment for the drink he had already consumed became a struggle.
"I forgot to carry my wallet and now, with no mobile internet, payments through mobile are also not possible," Abhinav told India Today Digital.
The Varanasi-bound commuter said he realised he had left his wallet behind only after buying the drink. And just when he thought he could wait for his train, another announcement dashed his hopes. The train he was supposed to board had been cancelled, leaving him waiting at the station until after 2 pm.
For Abhinav, and hundreds of other rail commuters in the national capital, it was a total disruption.
The disruptions at New Delhi Railway Station and Hazrat Nijamuddin Railway Station were part of a wider security clampdown in the national capital amid the proposed demonstration by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP). The CJP is protesting, seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged issues related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise of voter rolls.
Across the station, announcements in Hindi continued to echo through the speakers. "Varanasi ke liye jaane waali train radhh ki jayi hai (The train to Varanasi has been cancelled)." Another announcement followed, informing passengers that the Pune Express had also been cancelled.
These were not isolated announcements. More than 170 trains had been cancelled for the day, a railway official at New Delhi Railway Station, speaking on condition of anonymity, told India Today Digital.
Abhinav said he had no prior information that the train would be cancelled, and that is why he landed up at the station in New Delhi. With mobile internet suspended in the station area, it wasn't possible for him to keep updated on the train schedule.
WHEN POLITICAL PROTEST BY CJP DISRUPTED TRAIN JOURNEY
With authorities invoking Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), central Delhi was placed under extensive restrictions. Barricades appeared at major intersections and across roads leading to sensitive areas, with police personnel deployed in large numbers to prevent crowds from gathering.
In New Delhi, the sight of barricades guarded by groups of police personnel became routine. Several routes were diverted or restricted on security grounds, adding to the difficulties of people trying to move through the capital.
My team member Anand Singh, who was reporting from Jantar Mantar and Connaught Place told me that there were more security personnel than civilians. Police personnel were checking ID documents of people who were trying to reach the New Delhi Railway Station and allowing them to move on only when they were convinced they were genuine travellers.

items.title: NIA files case over flydubai attack in which Omani co-pilot stabbed Indian captain
items.summary: NIA files case over flydubai attack in which Omani copilot stabbed Indian captain
items.body_text:
NIA files case over flydubai attack in which Omani co-pilot stabbed Indian captain Smit Machchhar
The Centre has directed the NIA to investigate an attack on Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar aboard FlyDubai Flight 1073 on September 30. The Omani first officer reportedly stabbed him during an apparent hijack or crash attempt.
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has been directed by the Central Government to register a case and investigate an attack on Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flyDubai flight, after the aircraft reportedly made a sharp dive and turned back into Saudi airspace following an altercation inside the cockpit.
According to information cited by the Central Government, flyDubai Flight 1073, piloted by Indian national Captain Smit Machchhar and the Omani first officer, departed from Dubai on September 30 at 7:05 am Gulf Standard Time (GST), carrying 174 passengers and six crew members.
The aircraft was flying near the Jordan-Saudi Arabia border when it reportedly made a rapid dive and turned back towards Saudi airspace.
FIRST OFFICER ACCUSED OF ATTACKING CAPTAIN
The government said passengers reported that the Omani first officer stabbed Captain Machchhar during the flight in what appeared to be an attempt to hijack the aircraft or cause it to crash.
The first officer was reportedly overpowered and restrained by passengers and crew members following the attack.
Captain Machchhar sustained deep cuts to his head and hands, according to the information cited in the government order.
Following the incident, other flyDubai pilots who were on board took control of the aircraft and landed it safely at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Airport in Tabuk, northwestern Saudi Arabia, at around 10:45 am GST.
The first officer was subsequently arrested by Saudi authorities, according to the government.
NIA TO INVESTIGATE POSSIBLE LARGER CONSPIRACY
The Central Government said the incident disclosed the commission of offences against an Indian national under Section 3 of the Anti-Hijacking Act, 2016, and Section 16 read with Section 15(1)(a) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.
The offences mentioned in the order are scheduled offences under the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008.
The government said the case involved an attack on an Indian pilot and an apparent attempt to hijack or crash flyDubai Flight 1073. It said the incident had grave national and international ramifications and required a detailed investigation to uncover any larger conspiracy.
The Central Government, therefore, directed the NIA to register a case and investigate the matter under the provisions of the NIA Act.
The direction was issued under sub-sections 5 and 8 of Section 6 read with Section 8 of the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008.
The NIA investigation is expected to examine the circumstances surrounding the attack, the events inside the aircraft and whether the incident was part of any wider conspiracy.
The government order, however, does not provide further details about the motive of the first officer or the circumstances leading up to the reported attack.

items.title: 'Kya aap Emergency dekh sakte hain?' CJP reacts as politicians, journalists, lawyers detained
items.summary: CJP mocked PM Modi over Delhi protest detentions as police detained protesters, activists, journalists and lawyers ahead of its "Chalo Delhi" march.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: X/@Cockroachisback, ANI. CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke detained by the Police at Delhi Airport.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) took a dig at Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday, calling the police action against protesters an "emergency"-like situation. Police detained protesters, activists, journalists and lawyers ahead of the party’s ‘Delhi Chalo’ march. Hundreds of people were stopped across Delhi as organisers planned to gather at Jantar Mantar and demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over disputed voter-roll revisions.
"Kya aap Emergency dekh sakte hain, fraands?" the CJP asked in a satirical response to the detentions. The remark invoked India's 1975-77 Emergency, when civil liberties were severely curtailed and opposition leaders were jailed under then-Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
- Protestors Detained - Politicians Detained - Journalists Detained - Lawyers Detained https://t.co/LViLfBLEPx
— Cockroach Janta Party - CJP (@Cockroachisback) October 10, 2026
Police have detained about 200 more protesters in Connaught Place while attempting to reach Jantar Mantar, News Agency ANI reported earlier, quoting Delhi Police sources. Earlier, police had reported detaining roughly 500 people travelling in groups towards the demonstration.
Police also said nearly 50 people with criminal antecedents were taken into preventive custody, separate from those identified as protesters. The New Delhi district was divided into 20 operational zones, with temporary detention centres established for each. Stadiums were also designated for holding detainees.
Police said the march had not received permission. Authorities cited public order concerns and said the organisers' application was filed too close to the protest date. Prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita were in force. Roadblocks, metro closures and restrictions on mobile internet disrupted movement in central Delhi.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, who travelled from Mumbai, was detained after his flight landed at Delhi airport. Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were also held. In a video shared on Instagram, Dipke alleged that officers had boarded the aircraft before passengers disembarked.
"Not even Indira Gandhi did this during the Emergency," he said, accusing the authorities of treating peaceful protesters like criminals. "We are not afraid of you," he added.
CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh also alleged that police surrounded her car outside her home and tried to detain her without producing written authorisation. She said officers told her they had "orders from above" but did not explain who had issued them.
Four reporters covering the demonstration had been detained. Lawyers protesting near the Supreme Court were also taken into custody, according to a statement by the Supreme Court Bar Association president. Police had not immediately responded to those specific allegations.
Content creator Dhruv Rathee was detained at his Gurugram residence. The CJP accused the government of trying to silence young people who questioned it.
The latest march is part of a campaign against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. CJP and opposition parties say legitimate voters have been removed and accuse the Election Commission of favouring the BJP. The commission and the BJP deny the allegations. The commission says the exercise is intended to identify deceased, duplicate and ineligible voters and that wrongful deletions can be corrected.
The youth-led CJP began as an online satirical movement in May and later organised protests over examination irregularities. It has since joined student organisations and opposition parties in demanding greater scrutiny of electoral rolls and accountability from the Election Commission.

items.title: EC-SIR row protest escalates: Internet suspended, 1,500+ detained; AISA Chief Neha Bora held
items.summary: Delhi Police detained student leader Neha Bora and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke amid Saturday's protests demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: ANI, X/@neha_aisa. All India Students' Association president Neha Bora.
Delhi Police detained student leader Neha Bora and several protesters on Saturday as demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar spread to other parts of the capital. Meanwhile, Delhi airport authorities detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two colleagues. Police said the protest had not received permission.
Earlier, Bora, the national president of the All India Students' Association (AISA), called on supporters to gather elsewhere after police blocked access to Jantar Mantar. "Dilli Haat becomes our Jantar Mantar! Gyanesh Kumar must go!" she wrote on X.
Dilli Haat becomes our Jantar Mantar! Gyanesh Kumar must go! https://t.co/T33Q8uz4iB
— Neha (@neha_aisa) October 10, 2026
Earlier today, at Indira Gandhi International Airport, police officers boarded a flight from Mumbai and detained CJP founder Dipke along with senior leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Videos shared by the group showed officers confronting the activists before escorting them away.
NCP (SP) spokesperson Anish Gawande, who was travelling on the same flight, said he did not know where the three had been taken.
"We were all on the same flight. The three of them were sitting right in front of me. Police officers entered the aircraft, inconvenienced all other passengers and picked him up from the aircraft. We do not even know whether he (Dipke) has been brought out of the airport or is still there," he told reporters.
Gawande said protesters were still attempting to reach Jantar Mantar and urged police to exercise restraint.
"The plan will be revealed to you very soon. Currently, young people are making their way to Jantar Mantar. We hope that the Police will not use excessive violence or force. We hope that the Police will treat young people of this country as equal citizens, rather than criminals who deserve to be punished," he said.
Police deployed thousands of personnel and set up barricades and vehicle checkpoints around central Delhi. Authorities restricted access to dozens of Metro stations, disrupted some rail services and suspended mobile internet in parts of the city.
Delhi Police said the organisers had submitted their application too late to meet the required notice period. Officers also cited prohibitory orders and public-order concerns.
By early afternoon, more than 1,500 people had reportedly been detained across Delhi. The Times of India also reported stone-throwing near Akashwani Bhawan and injuries to two police personnel. The circumstances of the confrontation were still being established.
The CJP, meanwhile, asked supporters to avoid violence and not breach police barricades. In Mumbai, police also detained activist Tushar Gandhi ahead of a solidarity demonstration. Tushar Gandhi is a prominent Mumbai-based social activist, author, and the great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi. He is the son of journalist Arun Manilal Gandhi and currently serves as the president of the Mahatma Gandhi Foundation.
The protest, organised by CJP alongside student groups, seeks Kumar's resignation and challenges the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Opposition parties allege that the exercise has wrongly removed eligible voters and benefited the ruling BJP. The commission and the BJP reject allegations of deliberate manipulation.
As part of the Election Commission of India's (ECI) ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR), roughly 130 million names were removed, including entries for people who had relocated, passed away, or could not be traced. The Commission says that eligible voters who were wrongly excluded can apply to be reinstated.
The agitation follows several days of demonstrations by INDIA bloc leaders in Delhi.

items.title: 'Driven by foreign forces': BJP chief Nitin Nabin accuses Rahul Gandhi and CJP of plot to destabilise India
items.summary: BJP national president Nitin Nabin has accused Rahul Gandhi, the INDIA bloc and the Cockroach Janta Party of attempting to destabilise India at the behest of foreign forces. His allegations came amid protests in Delhi demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over the revision of electoral rolls.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: AI edit/author. LoP Rahul Gandhi, BJP Chief Nitin Nabin, AAP Chief Arvind Kejriwal and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke.
BJP president Nitin Nabin on Saturday accused Rahul Gandhi and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) of attempting to destabilise India, alleging that their protests were driven by political motives and foreign forces. His remarks came as CJP supporters and INDIA bloc leaders challenged the Election Commission over voter roll revisions and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Speaking at a press conference in New Delhi, he described what he called an attempt to create a "highly dangerous and serious situation" in the country. He singled out the opposition alliance and CJP, a youth-led movement, and sought to link the latter to Aam Aadmi Party leader Arvind Kejriwal.
"Who is doing this? Two anarchic groups: one led by Rahul Gandhi of the 'INDI Alliance,' and the other led by Arvind Kejriwal's associates, CJP," he said.
The BJP chief accused the groups of refusing to accept electoral defeats and competing to cause unrest. "These are people that the public has rejected... instead of accepting that verdict or learning from it, you have hatched a plot to destabilise the country," he said.
He further alleged that they were pursuing their political agendas "at the behest of foreign forces".
#WATCH | Delhi: BJP National President Nitin Nabin says, "Today, an attempt is being made to create a highly dangerous and serious situation in the country. Efforts are underway to destabilize the nation—where 1.4 billion people are living in peace and harmony, contributing collectively to India's development. Who is doing this? Two anarchic groups: one led by Rahul Gandhi of the 'INDI Alliance,' and the other led by Arvind Kejriwal's associates, CJP. I want to state clearly to both these groups that the people of India see right through your motives. Your 'anarchist competition', vying to see who can create more instability in the country, will not succeed. These are people that the public has rejected... instead of accepting that verdict or learning from it, you have hatched a plot to destabilize the country. I want to say that you are undertaking these efforts, driven by your political agendas, at the behest of foreign forces..." He adds, "Despite persistent global crises, the country is forging ahead on a path of continuous progress. Yet, this fact rankles you. You cannot digest India's growth, progress, and advancement. You cannot bear to see India moving forward as a self-reliant and empowered nation, and you are attempting to destabilize it at the behest of foreign forces. Let me state clearly: Indian democracy possesses immense strength, and the patriots of this nation will unite to thwart your designs."

items.title: Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports
items.summary: The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
items.body_text:
Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
- World News
- 4 min read
Washington: President Donald Trump said Tuesday he was delaying 50% U.S. tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports after the two countries reached a last-minute deal hours before the sanctions were to go into effect.
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
“I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for three days, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalisation of documents, have a DEAL!” Trump posted on Truth Social less than two hours before the 12:01 a.m. Wednesday deadline.
If they had gone into effect as scheduled at 12:01 a.m. Wednesday, Trump’s import taxes would have hit Canadian products ranging from hockey sticks to tongue depressors.
Advertisement
But the political impact would likely have been bigger than the economic one. Canada had threatened to retaliate against any new tariffs with levies of its own, aggravating a trade fight between countries that sold each other $880 billion worth of goods and services last year.
Canadian officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment Tuesday night.
Advertisement
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Trump had spoken twice by phone in the past two days about the ongoing negotiations, including a call Tuesday afternoon, Carney’s office said, underscoring the last-minute push for a deal.
Both countries had reason to step back from the brink. Nearly 72% of Canada’s goods exports last year went to the United States. And the Trump administration would be taking a risk by imposing a hefty new tariff — paid by U.S. importers who try to pass along the cost to consumers via higher prices — ahead of November’s midterm elections. U.S. voters are already frustrated with the high cost of living.
“I don’t think either side really wants these tariffs to come into effect,’’ Ryan Majerus, a partner at King & Spalding and a former U.S. trade official, said before the delay was announced. “There’s a pretty strong push on both sides to find an off-ramp here.’’
Trump’s approach to dealing with Canada marks an extraordinary departure from the traditionally cooperative relationship between the two countries. Trump has hit Canadian goods with tariffs — in a push to bring manufacturing back to the U.S. — and has repeatedly made inflammatory comments about turning Canada into America’s 51st state.
Trump has made tariffs the centrepiece of his second-term economic agenda. Last year, he imposed double-digit import taxes on almost every country, justifying them by declaring the longstanding U.S. trade deficit a national emergency. The Supreme Court in February ruled that he’d overstepped his authority, striking down those tariffs and setting the stage for the federal government to pay refunds to importers.
So Trump has looked for other legal authority to impose tariffs.
To hit Canada, he reached back to the Great Depression, invoking Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to threaten 50% tariffs on products that account for about 5% of Canadian exports to the United States.
Nearly a century ago, with the U.S. and world economies in collapse, Congress passed the 1930 tariff law, imposing taxes on imports from around the world. Known as the Smoot-Hawley tariffs, named for their congressional sponsors, they are notorious among economists and historians for limiting world commerce and making the Great Depression worse.
Section 338 tariffs have never been used before.
Section 338 authorises the president to impose tariffs of up to 50% on imports from count

'Allegations Lack Seriousness': Turkiye Denies Israel's Claims Over Syria Airstrikes
"These air strikes should stop, and we stand against them," Dujarric said at a UN press briefing on Tuesday. As per Al Jazeera, Egypt's Foreign Ministry also condemned the Israeli strikes, calling them a "dangerous escalation that threatens security and stability in the region".
- World News
- 3 min read
Ankara: Turkiye on Wednesday rejected Israel's claim that its airstrikes on Syria's Abu al-Duhur military airport were linked to a planned Turkish troop deployment, saying the allegations "lack seriousness" and seek to legitimise strikes on Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
In a post on X, the Turkish Presidential Communications Directorate said, “The allegations put forward by the Israeli Prime Ministry, which lack seriousness, aim to legitimize Israel's unlawful airstrikes targeting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria.” It added, "The accusations raised stem from Netanyahu's intent to continue his expansionist and destabilizing policies in the region ahead of elections in Israel."
Turkiye said it supports the establishment of lasting peace in the region, adding that "the sole path to this lies in Netanyahu abandoning his aggressive and coercive policies and demonstrating respect for international law". "Turkey will steadfastly continue its cooperation with the Syrian Government on legitimate grounds to establish peace, stability, and prosperity in Syria, and will never allow Syria to be destabilized," it said.
The remarks came after Israel carried out airstrikes on the Abu al-Duhur military airport in Syria's eastern Idlib province. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said that Syria was allowing Turkish troops to deploy at an airbase near Aleppo. Meanwhile, on Tuesday (local time), UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres' spokesperson Stephane Dujarric called the strikes "yet another very worrying violation" of Syria's territorial integrity and airspace.
Advertisement
"These air strikes should stop, and we stand against them," Dujarric said at a UN press briefing on Tuesday. As per Al Jazeera, Egypt's Foreign Ministry also condemned the Israeli strikes, calling them a "dangerous escalation that threatens security and stability in the region".
In a statement, the ministry said Egypt "fully rejects" Israel's continued violations of Syrian sovereignty and warned that the strikes could further destabilise Syria at a critical time when the country requires support to restore stability and pursue political solutions. Cairo called on the international community to "assume its responsibilities" by putting an end to repeated Israeli violations and adopting firm measures to deter actions that could fuel a broader regional conflict.
Advertisement
Earlier on Tuesday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said Israel and Syria had agreed to maintain a security "status quo". In a post on X, Netanyahu's office said, "Israel and Syria agreed to a status quo in security matters, which Syria was on the verge of breaching by permitting Turkish troops to deploy at an airbase near Aleppo," the statement said.
"Israel will not tolerate threats to its security, and would welcome a return to the status quo," it added. Meanwhile, US Special Presidential Envoy for Syria and Iraq Tom Barrack expressed concern over the Israeli airstrikes, calling them an "unnecessary escalation". "We are deeply concerned that the confirmed Israeli airstrikes on Abu al-Duhur Airbase constitute an unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability," Barrack said.
The airbase was targeted in four airstrikes, marking the first reported attack on the facility since the fall of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's government in December 2024.

items.title: ‘India Is No Longer A Democracy’: Priyanka Gandhi Alleges ‘Dictatorship’; Rahul Backs Youth Protests
items.summary: ‘India Is No Longer A Democracy’: Priyanka Gandhi Alleges ‘Dictatorship’; Rahul Backs Youth Protests
items.body_text:
Rahul Gandhi stated he has been fighting Narendra Modi, the RSS, and people associated with them for over a decade. He claims to understand their tactics
‘India Is No Longer A Democracy’: Priyanka Gandhi Alleges ‘Dictatorship’; Rahul Backs Youth Protests
Rahul Gandhi targeted PM Modi and RSS, urging arrests of all Opposition leaders and young protesters. Priyanka Gandhi alleged “dictatorship” over Delhi protest detentions.
- Rahul Gandhi criticises Modi, RSS, challenging government over arrests.
- CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke detained from aircraft, sparking outrage.
- BJP counters Rahul Gandhi, citing Indira Gandhi's Emergency actions.
Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) in a video shared on social media, saying he has been fighting them and their associates for over a decade.
Gandhi said he understood his opponents “inside out” and was familiar with their tactics.
“I have been fighting Narendra Modi, the RSS and people associated with them for over a decade now. I understand my opponents as well as anyone understands their rivals. I know them inside out and am familiar with their every move,” he said.
Rahul Gandhi Calls Modi, Shah, Bhagwat, Others ‘Cowards’
In the video, Gandhi described what he called the defining characteristic of his political opponents as “cowardice”. He named Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and National Security Advisor Ajit Doval, alleging that they were “slowly getting cornered”.
 I’ve been fighting Narendra Modi and the RSS for over a decade now. I understand them like you would understand your opponent - inside out, like the back of my hand. The core characteristic of these people is cowardice. Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Mohan Bhagwat, Gyanesh Kumar and Ajit Doval, the villains of this story, are slowly finding the space closing around them. We are closing that space. Mr. Modi, do whatever you want. Call out all the police: 10,000, 20,000, 50,000, whatever you want. Arrest all the leaders. Arrest all the young people. Arrest us all. We are surrounding you, and we are not going to back down. Mark my words: we already have the information we need. We are going to defend our Constitution. We are going to protect the voice of the Indian people. And we are going to ensure that what was done to India over the last 10-15 years will never, ever be done again. Youth of India, I am proud of you. Keep protesting. We are standing with you. We are going to ensure that this regime and the people who have attacked our Constitution are defeated. मैं नरेंद्र मोदी, RSS और इनसे जुड़े लोगों के ख़िलाफ़ एक दशक से भी ज़्यादा समय से लड़ रहा हूँ। मैं अपने विरोधियों को उतनी अच्छी तरह समझता हूँ, जितना कोई भी अपने प्रतिद्वंद्वी को समझता है। मैं इन्हें अंदर तक जानता हूँ, इनकी हर चाल से वाक़िफ़ हूँ। इन लोगों की सबसे बड़ी पहचान है - कायरता। नरेंद्र मोदी, अमित शाह, मोहन भागवत, ज्ञानेश कुमार, अजीत डोभाल - इस कहानी के खलनायक - अब धीरे-धीरे घिरते जा रहे हैं। इनके चारों तरफ़ से दायरा सिमट रहा है। जो करना है, कर लीजिए। जितनी पुलिस बुलानी है, बुला लीजिए - 10 हज़ार, 20 हज़ार, 50 हज़ार, जितनी चाहें बुला लीजिए। सारे नेताओं को गिरफ़्तार कर लीजिए। सारे युवाओं को गिरफ़्तार कर लीजिए। हम सबको गिरफ़्तार कर लीजिए। घबराइये मत - हम आपको चारों तरफ़ से घेर रहे हैं, और हम पीछे हटने वाले नहीं हैं। मेरी बात याद रखिए - हमें जो जानकारी चाहिए, वह हमारे पास पहले से है। हम अपने संविधान की रक्षा करेंगे। हम हिंदुस्तान की जनता की आवाज़ की हिफ़ाज़त करेंगे। और हम यह सुनिश्चित करेंगे कि पिछले 10-15 सालों में हिंदुस्तान के साथ जो हुआ है, वह दोबारा कभी, किसी भी सूरत में न हो। हिंदुस्तान के युवाओं, मुझे आप पर गर्व है। अपना विरोध जारी रखिए। हम आपके साथ खड़े हैं। हम यह सुनिश्चित करेंगे कि इस सरकार और हमारे संविधान पर हमला करने वालों को शिकस्त मिले।

items.title: ‘Undeclared Emergency’: Sonam Wangchuk Backs CJP Protest, Warns Of Hunger Strike If Leaders Not Released
items.summary: ‘Undeclared Emergency’: Sonam Wangchuk Backs CJP Protest, Warns Of Hunger Strike
items.body_text:
Wangchuk stated he had important work in Ladakh, including winter preparations and projects for water security and GLOF risks. He also mentioned not anticipating the scale of detentions.
‘Undeclared Emergency’: Sonam Wangchuk Backs CJP Protest, Warns Of Hunger Strike If Leaders Not Released
Addressing his absence from Saturday's protest, Wangchuk said he had not anticipated the scale of the detentions when he appealed for unity and peace a day earlier.
- Sonam Wangchuk condemns detentions, calling situation
- He threatened hunger strike if protesters are not released soon.
- CJP protest against irregularities disallowed, leading to leaders' detentions.
- Wangchuk earlier cited Ladakh work, urging peaceful protest.
Activist Sonam Wangchuk has voiced support for the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) protest in Delhi, describing the situation in India as an “undeclared Emergency” after several protesters and leaders, including CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, were detained on October 10.
Wangchuk, who did not attend the protest at Jantar Mantar, warned that he would consider launching a hunger strike or a foot march if those detained were not released by the following day. His remarks came a day after he explained his decision to stay in Ladakh, citing important work at home.
"India in a state of undeclared Emergency," Wangchuk said in a post on X, criticising the mass detentions.
"I will be compelled to consider an Anshan Fast (hunger strike) or Padyatra March (foot march) if they are not released by tomorrow," he added.
The CJP and Opposition leaders had sought to protest in New Delhi over alleged electoral irregularities and what they described as “collusion” between the Election Commission and the ruling BJP. They were, however, disallowed from holding the demonstration at Jantar Mantar.
Wangchuk Says Situation Changed After His Earlier Appeal
Addressing his absence from Saturday's protest, Wangchuk said he had not anticipated the scale of the detentions when he appealed for unity and peace a day earlier.
 INDIA IN A STATE OF UNDECLARED EMERGENCY... Yesterday when I posted a message appealing for unity & peace in today's protest I had never imagined that the biggest democracy in the world would be under an undeclared EMERGENCY. I was happy there were so many leaders to lead the movement, but I now learn that they have all been arrested. I hope those arrested will be released soon. I will be compelled to consider an Anshan Fast or Padyatra March if they are not released by tomorrow. #JantarMantar #protest #CJP #CEC #sonamwangchuk
— Sonam Wangchuk (@Wangchuk66) October 10, 2026
"Yesterday when I posted a message appealing for unity & peace in today's protest I had never imagined that the biggest democracy in the world would be under an undeclared Emergency," he said.
On Friday, Wangchuk had shared a modified version of a famous couplet by Urdu poet Faiz Ahmed Faiz to explain his decision not to participate in the demonstration.
"Aur Bhi Gham Hain Zamaane Main Siyaast Ke Siva... Rahaten aur bhi hain wasl ki raahat ke siva," he wrote.
The couplet conveys the idea that there are other sorrows in the world beyond politics and other comforts beyond union with a beloved. The original verse uses “mohabbet” (love) rather than “siyaast” (politics), while the original word for sorrow is “dukh”, not “gham”.

Wangchuk Urges Peaceful Protest, Calls For Unity
In his Friday post, Wangchuk said he was continuing his work in Ladakh despite what he described as government efforts to hinder and damage it.
"Despite all efforts of the government to hinder & damage our work we continue to work for national security... making preparations as another winter comes. This includes making artificial glaciers for water security & experiments for GLOF or glacial lake flood security... to difuse the 200+ ticking water bombs in high Himalayas," he wrote.

items.title: CJP Protest Live Updates: Actor Imran Khan Detained In Mumbai; Rahul Gandhi Says, ‘Arrest Us All’
items.summary: CJP Protest Live: Dipke Leaves For Delhi Ahead Of Jantar Mantar Protest Today
items.body_text:
CJP Protest Live Updates: Actor Imran Khan Detained In Mumbai; Rahul Gandhi Says, ‘Arrest Us All’
CJP Protest Delhi Live Updates: Delhi Police have denied permission for the Cockroach Janta Party's proposed October 10 protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar.
LIVE
Background
CJP Delhi Protest Live Update: Authorities in Delhi have stepped up security measures ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) proposed protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, October 10. The measures include prohibitory orders, denial of permission for the demonstration and a request to restrict access to 57 metro stations.
The Delhi Police have imposed Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) in the New Delhi district, restricting the assembly of more than five people. Police have also denied permission for the protest called by the CJP and some student organisations.
Joint Commissioner of Police, New Delhi Range, Nupur Prasad, said on Friday that the application seeking permission was received on October 7, just three days before the planned demonstration. According to police guidelines, applications must be submitted at least 10 days in advance.
Delhi Police Seek Restrictions At 57 Metro Stations
The Delhi Police have also asked the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) to shut 57 metro stations from 9 pm on Friday until Saturday, citing the possibility of an "unruly mob movement towards sensitive locations".
In a letter sent on Thursday, Joint Commissioner of Police (Transport Range) Rajneesh Gupta said the frequency of metro trains passing through these stations could also be reduced on October 10, depending on the situation. The proposed restrictions are linked to the planned CJP protest at Jantar Mantar.
The stations listed in the request include Janpath, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Barakhamba Road, Supreme Court, Indraprastha, Kashmere Gate, Chandni Chowk, INA, Hauz Khas, Azadpur, Jamia Millia Islamia, Shaheen Bagh, Welcome and Rohini West.
CJP Protest Targets CEC Over SIR Allegations
The CJP has called the demonstration against Kumar over allegations of voter-list tampering during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The allegations also concern claims that the CEC bypassed his two colleagues to make changes involving Form 6, which is used to register as a voter.
The police cited the late submission of the application and alleged violations of rules during a previous demonstration as reasons for denying permission. Section 163 of the BNSS empowers authorities to issue orders to prevent potential disturbances and maintain public order.
The proposed metro restrictions are a request to the DMRC; the information provided does not confirm whether the corporation has agreed to implement them.
‘Delhi Is Officially Pyongyang’: Mahua Moitra Questions Mamata Banerjee’s Detention
Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra questioned the detention of West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee during a protest in Delhi, asking why the TMC leader and three party MPs were allegedly stopped from staging a sit-in outside the party office.
In a post on X, Moitra argued that the gathering did not exceed the limit under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).
“Why [@MamataOfficial] been detained? How is it illegal for Ex-Chief Minister and 3 MPs (not exceeding BNSS 163 limit) to sit at bus stop outside party office,” Moitra wrote.
Taking aim at the authorities, she added, “Delhi is officially Pyongyang.”
Moitra also vowed that the protest would continue, writing, “This will continue tomorrow & tomorrow & tomorrow. Kar le jo karna hai Modi Shah.”
‘Mamata Trying To Create Jungle Raj In Delhi’: BJP MP Khagen Murmu On CJP Protest
BJP MP Khagen Murmu on Saturday accused the Opposition of spreading misinformation by joining hands with the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) during its protest in Delhi.

  दिल्ली में बड़ी संख्या में प्रदर्शनकारियों को पुलिस ने हिरासत में लिया है (Photo: PTI)  
Delhi CJP Protest Live Update: शनिवार को दिल्ली में CJP का जंतर मंतर प्रदर्शन पुलिस की सख्त घेराबंदी के कारण कई छोटे प्रदर्शनों में बंट गया. पार्टी मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग कर रही है और उन पर SIR और फॉर्म 6 में गड़बड़ी के आरोप लगा रही है. मेट्रो, ट्रेन और मोबाइल इंटरनेट पर रोक रही और करीब 25,000 जवान तैनात थे. शाम 5 बजे तक कम से कम 3,000 लोग हिरासत में लिए गए, जिनमें नेता और संगठनों के प्रमुख भी थे. पुलिस ने बल प्रयोग नहीं किया. सोमवार को INDIA गठबंधन का प्रदर्शन होगा. उधर दिल्ली में भी अरविंद केजरीवाल, ममता बनर्जी जैसे कई नेताओं को हिरासत में लिया गया है.
CJP प्रोटेस्ट को लेकर देश की राजधानी दिल्ली और अन्य जगहों पर क्या कुछ चल रहा है, जानने के लिए Live Update यहां देखते रहें.
 6:43 PM (10 मिनट पहले) 
अहमदाबाद के एलिसब्रिज में एमजे लाइब्रेरी के पास GenZ ने विरोध प्रदर्शन किया. प्रदर्शनकारियों ने मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त (CEC) ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे और स्पेशल इंटेंसिव रिवीजन (SIR) को लेकर विरोध जताया. प्रदर्शन को देखते हुए पूरे इलाके में भारी संख्या में पुलिस बल तैनात किया गया. इस दौरान पुलिस ने विरोध प्रदर्शन करने पहुंचीं महिलाओं समेत प्रदर्शनकारियों को हिरासत में ले लिया.
 6:14 PM (38 मिनट पहले) 
दिल्ली की मुख्यमंत्री रेखा गुप्ता ने राहुल गांधी और अरविंद केजरीवाल पर निशाना साधा है. उन्होंने आरोप लगाया कि जनता की ओर से नकारे जा चुके राहुल गांधी और केजरीवाल अपनी B-Team CJP के साथ मिलकर दिल्ली को अखाड़ा बनाने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं.
 6:13 PM (40 मिनट पहले) 
दिल्ली मेट्रो रेल कॉर्पोरेशन (DMRC) ने बताया है कि सुरक्षा कारणों से शुक्रवार रात 9 बजे से बंद किए गए 45 मेट्रो स्टेशन आज, 10 अक्टूबर को रात 10 बजे तक बंद रहेंगे. DMRC के मुताबिक, सुरक्षा एजेंसियां स्थिति की समीक्षा करेंगी. इसके बाद जरूरत के अनुसार आगे का अपडेट जारी किया जाएगा.
 6:05 PM (47 मिनट पहले) 
कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP) ने दावा किया है कि उसके राष्ट्रीय प्रवक्ता सिद्धांत भारद्वाज और उनकी टीम को प्रदर्शन करने के दौरान हिरासत में ले लिया गया. CJP ने दिल्ली पुलिस पर निशाना साधते हुए आरोप लगाया कि पुलिस उन सभी लोगों के खिलाफ कार्रवाई कर रही है, जो देश के लिए आवाज उठा रहे हैं.
 5:59 PM (54 मिनट पहले) 
मुंबई के अगस्त क्रांति मैदान से अभिनेता इमरान खान को हिरासत में लिया गया है. यह जगह CJP के प्रदर्शन के समर्थन में प्रस्तावित विरोध प्रदर्शन का केंद्र थी.
 5:58 PM (55 मिनट पहले) 
दिल्ली की साकेत कोर्ट ने कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP) की लीगल अफेयर्स हेड रत्ना सिंह की अर्जी खारिज कर दी है. रत्ना सिंह की ओर से यह अर्जी उनके घर पर कथित तौर पर हिरासत में लिए जाने को लेकर पुलिसकर्मियों के खिलाफ FIR दर्ज करने की मांग के साथ दाखिल की गई थी.
अर्जी में उन्हें तुरंत रिहा करने का निर्देश देने की मांग भी की गई थी. हालांकि, पुलिस ने उन्हें शाम को ही रिहा कर दिया. इसके बाद कोर्ट ने अर्जी खारिज कर दी.
 5:23 PM (एक घंटा पहले) 
सोनम वांगचुक ने दिल्ली में CJP प्रोटेस्ट के दौरान नेताओं की गिरफ्तारी पर सवाल उठाए हैं. उन्होंने भारत को अघोषित आपातकाल की स्थिति में बताया और कहा कि उन्होंने एक दिन पहले शांति और एकजुटता की अपील की थी. आंदोलन का नेतृत्व करने वाले कई नेता आगे आए थे, लेकिन अब सभी गिरफ्तार हो चुके हैं. पूरी खबर यहां क्लिक कर पढ़ें - 'कल तक रिहा नहीं किया तो अनशन करूंगा...', प्रदर्शनकारियों को लेकर सोनम वांगचुक का सरकार को अल्टीमेटम
 5:05 PM (एक घंटा पहले) 
दिल्ली में पुलिस की सख्ती के बावजूद सेंट्रल दिल्ली में प्रदर्शनकारी जुटे. जिन्हें पुलिस ने हिरासत में लिया. बसों की मदद से उन्हें डिटेंशन सेंटर ले जाया गया. इस बीच एक वीडियो वायरल हो रहा है. जिसमें नजर आ रहा है कि युवक बस के खुली गेट से उतर रहे हैं. तीन-चार युवक तो उतर गए. लेकिन, बाद में फिर पुलिस ने गेट बंद किया.
 4:58 PM (एक घंटा पहले) 
कांग्रेस नेता राहुल गांधी ने प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी, RSS और बीजेपी के कई वरिष्ठ नेताओं पर निशाना साधा है. उन्होंने कहा कि वह एक दशक से भी ज्यादा समय से नरेंद्र मोदी और RSS के खिलाफ लड़ रहे हैं और अपने विरोधियों को अच्छी तरह समझते हैं. राहुल गांधी ने आरोप लगाया कि इन नेताओं की सबसे बड़ी पहचान कायरता है. उन्होंने प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी, गृह मंत्री अमित शाह, RSS प्रमुख मोहन भागवत, मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार और राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा सलाहकार अजीत डोभाल का न

items.summary: सोनम वांगचुक ने दिल्ली में CJP प्रोटेस्ट के दौरान नेताओं की गिरफ्तारी पर सवाल उठाए हैं. उन्होंने भारत को अघोषित आपातकाल की स्थिति में बताया और कहा कि उन्होंने एक दिन पहले शांति और एकजुटता की अपील की थी. आंदोलन का नेतृत्व करने वाले कई नेता आगे आए थे, लेकिन अब सभी गिरफ्तार हो चुके हैं.

लद्दाख के पर्यावरण कार्यकर्ता सोनम वांगचुक ने दिल्ली में हो रहे CJP प्रोटेस्ट के दौरान नेताओं की गिरफ्तारी पर सवाल उठाए हैं. उन्होंने भारत को 'अघोषित आपातकाल' की स्थिति में बताया है और गिरफ्तार नेताओं को जल्द रिहा करने की मांग की है. वांगचुक ने साफ कहा है कि अगर इन नेताओं को कल तक रिहा नहीं किया गया, तो वह अनशन या पदयात्रा शुरू करने पर विचार करेंगे. इन नेताओं में अभिजीत दिपके, सौरभ दास और आशुतोष रांका समेत कॉकरोच पार्टी के कई लोग शामिल हैं.
सोनम वांगचुक ने सोशल मीडिया पर एक बयान जारी करते हुए अपनी बात रखी. उन्होंने बताया कि एक दिन पहले ही उन्होंने आज के प्रदर्शन को लेकर एकजुटता और शांति बनाए रखने की अपील की थी. उस वक्त उन्होंने सोचा भी नहीं था कि दुनिया के सबसे बड़े लोकतंत्र में ऐसी स्थिति बन जाएगी, जिसे वह अघोषित आपातकाल मान रहे हैं. अघोषित आपातकाल का मतलब ऐसे हालात से है, जिसमें आपातकाल का एलान नहीं हुआ हो, लेकिन लोगों को लगे कि हालात वैसे ही हैं.
वांगचुक के मुताबिक, उन्हें इस बात की खुशी थी कि आंदोलन का नेतृत्व करने के लिए कई नेता आगे आए हैं. लेकिन अब उन्हें पता चला है कि उन सभी नेताओं को गिरफ्तार कर लिया गया है. वांगचुक ने इसी बात पर सवाल उठाए हैं. उन्होंने उम्मीद जताई है कि गिरफ्तार किए गए सभी नेताओं को जल्द रिहा कर दिया जाएगा.
वांगचुक ने यह भी साफ किया है कि अगर कल तक नेताओं की रिहाई नहीं होती, तो उन्हें अनशन या पदयात्रा शुरू करने पर विचार करना पड़ेगा. यानी वह खुद अनशन या पदयात्रा के जरिए अपना विरोध दर्ज कराने पर सोच सकते हैं. अनशन का मतलब खाना छोड़कर विरोध करना है, जबकि पदयात्रा में लोग पैदल चलकर अपनी बात रखते हैं. वांगचुक ने अपने संदेश में शांति और एकजुटता पर जोर दिया है.
दिल्ली में 10 अक्टूबर को प्रस्तावित CJP प्रोटेस्ट को लेकर सुरक्षा व्यवस्था कड़ी की गई है. इस बीच प्रदर्शन और उससे जुड़ी राजनीतिक गतिविधियों के दौरान नेताओं की हिरासत का मुद्दा भी चर्चा में है. वांगचुक का बयान ऐसे समय आया है, जब प्रदर्शनकारियों की गिरफ्तारी और विरोध करने के अधिकार को लेकर सवाल उठाए जा रहे हैं. उनके बयान से इस पूरी राजनीतिक बहस में आंदोलन को लेकर एक नया घटनाक्रम सामने आया है.

कांग्रेस नेता राहुल गांधी ने दिल्ली में CJP के प्रदर्शन के बीच केंद्र सरकार और राष्ट्रीय स्वयंसेवक संघ (RSS) पर निशाना साधा है. उन्होंने सोशल मीडिया पर पोस्ट कर प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी, गृह मंत्री अमित शाह, RSS प्रमुख मोहन भागवत, ज्ञानेश कुमार और अजीत डोभाल का नाम लेते हुए कहा कि ये लोग धीरे-धीरे घिरते जा रहे हैं. राहुल गांधी ने कहा कि चाहे जितनी पुलिस बुला ली जाए या जितने नेताओं और युवाओं को गिरफ्तार कर लिया जाए, वे पीछे हटने वाले नहीं हैं.
राहुल गांधी ने अपनी पोस्ट में लिखा, 'मैं नरेंद्र मोदी, RSS और इनसे जुड़े लोगों के खिलाफ एक दशक से भी ज्यादा समय से लड़ रहा हूं. मैं अपने विरोधियों को उतनी अच्छी तरह समझता हूं, जितना कोई भी अपने प्रतिद्वंद्वी को समझता है. मैं इन्हें अंदर तक जानता हूं और इनकी हर चाल से वाकिफ हूं.' उन्होंने आगे लिखा, 'इन लोगों की सबसे बड़ी पहचान है- कायरता.'
राहुल गांधी ने प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी, अमित शाह, मोहन भागवत, ज्ञानेश कुमार और अजीत डोभाल का जिक्र करते हुए कहा, 'इस कहानी के खलनायक अब धीरे-धीरे घिरते जा रहे हैं. इनके चारों तरफ से दायरा सिमट रहा है.' उन्होंने आगे कहा, 'जो करना है, कर लीजिए. जितनी पुलिस बुलानी है, बुला लीजिए- 10 हजार, 20 हजार, 50 हजार, जितनी चाहें बुला लीजिए. सारे नेताओं को गिरफ्तार कर लीजिए. सारे युवाओं को गिरफ्तार कर लीजिए. हम सबको गिरफ्तार कर लीजिए.'
हम पीछे हटने वाले नहीं हैं
राहुल गांधी ने कहा, 'घबराइये मत- हम आपको चारों तरफ से घेर रहे हैं और हम पीछे हटने वाले नहीं हैं. मेरी बात याद रखिए- हमें जो जानकारी चाहिए, वह हमारे पास पहले से है.' उन्होंने संविधान की रक्षा और देश की जनता की आवाज की हिफाजत करने की बात भी कही. राहुल गांधी ने लिखा, 'हम अपने संविधान की रक्षा करेंगे. हम हिंदुस्तान की जनता की आवाज की हिफाजत करेंगे. हम यह सुनिश्चित करेंगे कि पिछले 10-15 सालों में हिंदुस्तान के साथ जो हुआ है, वह दोबारा कभी, किसी भी सूरत में न हो.' कांग्रेस नेता ने युवाओं से अपना विरोध जारी रखने की अपील करते हुए लिखा, 'हिंदुस्तान के युवाओं, मुझे आप पर गर्व है. अपना विरोध जारी रखिए. हम आपके साथ खड़े हैं.' उन्होंने अपनी पोस्ट के अंत में कहा, 'हम यह सुनिश्चित करेंगे कि इस सरकार और हमारे संविधान पर हमला करने वालों को शिकस्त मिले.'
3000 लोगों को हिरासत में लिया गया
दिल्ली में CJP के प्रदर्शन के बीच शनिवार सुबह से करीब 3,000 लोगों को एहतियातन हिरासत में लिए जाने की बात सामने आई है. इसी दौरान आम आदमी पार्टी के संयोजक अरविंद केजरीवाल को दिल्ली के लोदी एस्टेट के बाहर से हिरासत में लिए जाने की खबर सामने आई. वहीं, पूर्व सांसद साकेत गोखले ने दावा किया कि पश्चिम बंगाल की मुख्यमंत्री ममता बनर्जी और तृणमूल कांग्रेस के पांच अन्य नेताओं को भी दिल्ली में उनके आवास के बाहर से हिरासत में लिया गया. गोखले के मुताबिक, दिल्ली पुलिस और CRPF ने उन्हें एक कैदी वाहन में बैठाकर किसी अज्ञात स्थान पर ले जाया.
