items.title: Anthropic discloses fake murder tip to police among new rogue AI incidents
items.summary: An Anthropic logo is displayed at Moscone Center during the Dreamforce 2026 technology summit in San Francisco, California, US, September 17, 2026. — ReutersAn Anthropic artificial intelligence model submitted a false homicide tip to a Philadelphia police website, among...
items.body_text:
Published October 10, 2026
An Anthropic artificial intelligence (AI) model submitted a false homicide tip to a Philadelphia police website, among a string of incidents the AI company disclosed on Friday detailing Claude models' unsanctioned manipulation of some government websites.
It is the first known instance in which a rogue AI appears to have tried to communicate a bogus tip to authorities, despite instructions not to create accounts or submit anything destructive, while not explicitly barred from submitting forms.
The cases are the latest examples of rogue or undesired behaviour by the AI models of tech companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI.
They add fuel to national concerns about the fast-advancing technology amid reports of corporate network hacks by AI agents, and researchers' warnings of an eventual existential threat to humanity.
Many of the cases Anthropic revealed involved websites run by federal, state, and local agencies. Anthropic said it briefed the White House and notified all the agencies involved, but did not disclose who those parties were.
"Super intelligence companies must immediately disclose incidents involving their models and follow with swift, decisive action to remedy any and all harm," FTC Director of Public Affairs Joe Gabriel Simonson said on X.
This process was "not optional," he said, adding that the Super Intelligence Force would fulfil its responsibility.
The FTC said Anthropic disclosed to the SI Force on Friday its late September discovery of incidents involving what the task force called "unauthorised and fraudulent use of government and other systems".
On Friday, Philadelphia police said Anthropic notified them of the spurious tip this week, and attributed the submissions to an automated testing process.
"The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the city is unacceptable," they said.
The July 18 tip purported to come from someone who might have information about the case, police added.
"I may have information regarding this case," Anthropic's model wrote in its submission.
"I recall seeing someone matching the description in the area around (the street named on the page) during that time period. Please contact me if this information is relevant." The brackets featured in Anthropic's statement.
Previous incidents have involved AI agents hacking into vulnerable systems or commandeering unsanctioned platforms to communicate with one another.
In September, Anthropic rival OpenAI apologised for the hacking of an Australian health data portal by a rogue AI agent, the first known instance of an AI agent exploiting a government website.
In two cases described on Friday, Anthropic’s models obtained for free public data normally only available for a fee. Another instance revealed an obscure flaw that allowed use of a public tool hosted by a university.
Claude models were also able to bypass restrictions by using free services that shorten URLs.
Philadelphia police said the tip "was flagged as spam and was never forwarded to the Real-Time Crime Centre for investigative vetting or dissemination."
Knowingly giving false reports to law enforcement authorities is a misdemeanour under Pennsylvania law, which specifies "a person", however.
This includes "information relating to an offence or incident when he knows he has no information relating to such offence or incident."
Police quoted Anthropic as telling them the test process was stopped after discovery of the incident. The false tip was submitted through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com concerning an unsolved homicide.
Police said they had no evidence of unauthorised access to their systems or compromise of their data.

Published October 10, 2026
Singer Karina Zeviani, who once appeared on The Voice, has died at the age of 51 after fighting breast cancer for two years.
She passed away in a hospital in Brazil on October 8 just weeks after sharing an update about her health with her fans.
Karina was living with serious illness for two years but she continued to share parts of her journey with people who followed her.
On September 20, the late singer, however, told them that she had to start chemotherapy through a drip, also spoking about having to lose her hair again and fans then took no time in sending her kind messages.
One fan wrote, “You're going to be great and beautiful as always.”
READ MORE: Katie Price's husband Lee Andrews makes desperate money plea
Although many people knew Karina from the Brazilian version of The Voice in 2020, she was making music for years before that as well.
In 2005, she joined the American music group Thievery Corporation after David Byrne, the lead singer of Talking Heads, recommended her.
The group later paid tribute to her, saying, “She was a beautiful, talented and truly lovely soul, with an aura and vibrance that were impossible to forget.”
Karina also sang with the French group Nouvelle Vague and released her own album, Amor Iventado, in 2012.
A friend remembered her as “a person full of sparkle.” Her funeral was held on October 9.

items.title: Alcaraz through in straight sets on Shanghai Masters opener
items.body_text:
Alcaraz through in straight sets on Shanghai Masters opener
- By AFP -
- Oct 10, 2026
A moustached Carlos Alcaraz beat Juan Manuel Cerundolo 6-3, 6-3 to kick-start his title bid at the Shanghai Masters on Saturday, days after winning the Tokyo Open for his first trophy since returning from injury.
The Spanish star, seeded second, put on a dominant show to brush aside the 55th-ranked Argentinian in the second round in just 66 minutes.
“Really, really happy with the way I played today. It wasn’t easy,” said the 23-year-old former number one.
“Just had two days of preparation… I came from Tokyo, there were totally different conditions,” he added. “Just tried to play the best that I can.”
Sporting a fresh moustache, Alcaraz signed a camera “Moustache Team” following his win.
Asked by an on-court interviewer about the new look, Alcaraz said: “It’s gonna stay.”
He will play either Ignacio Buse or Zizou Bergs in the next round.
Earlier, Daniil Medvedev fought back to beat Germany’s Jan-Lennard Struff 4-6, 6-4, 6-3 in the second round, the Russian’s first match since being disqualified from the China Open.
Medvedev was defaulted from his semi-final against Novak Djokovic in Beijing for hitting a spectator with a ball and ended the 500-level event with zero ranking points and no prize money.
The former world number one said it was an accident.
Playing five days later in Shanghai, sixth-ranked Medvedev overcame an early wobble to hold off 59th-ranked Struff.
He sent down 21 aces to advance and will face Czech qualifier Dalibor Svrcina in the next round.
World number five Felix Auger-Aliassime also survived a scare, needing three hours to beat 77th-ranked Camilo Ugo Carabelli 4-6, 7-6 (7/1), 7-5.
The Canadian will play Spaniard Pablo Carreno Busta in the third round.
Several matches in the afternoon were suspended due to rain, but Taylor Fritz, Casper Ruud and Arthur Fils all went through as play resumed.

items.title: Palmer signs contract to stay at Chelsea until 2034
items.body_text:
Palmer signs contract to stay at Chelsea until 2034
- By AFP -
- Oct 10, 2026
Cole Palmer has signed a contract extension to stay at Chelsea until 2034.
Palmer was already under contract with the Premier League club until 2033 and the England forward’s improved deal extends his time at Stamford Bridge for a further year.
“Chelsea means a lot to me and I think the club is going in the right direction, so I’m delighted to sign and I’m obviously very happy,” the 24-year-old said.
“Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and obviously the manager, they gave me a lot of confidence, so it was only right to sign.
“Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions. I feel like we win major trophies here consistently and I want to be a part of that and play a big role in it, too.”
Palmer joined Chelsea from Manchester City in 2023 and has provided a combined 91 goal and assists in 138 appearances in his time in west London.
He struggled with a persistent groin problem last season and was controversially left out of the World Cup squad by England boss Thomas Tuchel.
Tuchel also said Palmer has “missed too many opportunities” to play for England after he pulled out of the squad for the recent Nations League matches.
Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso defended Palmer on Friday, saying his star is committed to England and just needs to be fully fit to show his best form for club and country.
Palmer has started the season strongly, though, scoring four goals in seven appearances in all competitions.
His close relationship with Morgan Rogers convinced the England midfielder to join Chelsea from Aston Villa in the close season.
Palmer’s contract is the latest given to a Blues star that stretches into the 2030s after recent deals signed by Joao Pedro and Pedro Neto.

items.title: Erik Prince’s forces suffer battlefield loss in Congo, former UFC fighter among wounded, sources say
items.body_text:
Erik Prince's forces suffer battlefield loss in Congo, former UFC fighter among wounded, sources say
- By Reuters -
- Oct 10, 2026
DAKAR: Blackwater founder Erik Prince’s forces suffered a major battlefield loss in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo in mid-September when enemy forces ambushed them, killing and wounding at least 20 people, including a popular former UFC fighter, sources close to the government and his company said.
The frontline clash shows how Prince, an ally and supporter of US President Donald Trump, has taken on an expanded role in Congo through his company Vectus Global. The company, which also operates in Haiti and other parts of Africa, provides consulting and security services and previously helped Congo’s army secure the city of Uvira in South Kivu against Rwanda-backed rebels who control swathes of the east.
A veteran special operator reported on his podcast earlier this week that former US Green Beret and Ultimate Fighting Championship contestant Tim Kennedy was injured in Congo. The involvement of Prince’s forces and the number of casualties have not previously been reported.
The attack in South Kivu on September 17 left about 20 dead and wounded, two sources working with Congo’s government said. The dead included at least seven Congolese and a former member of New Zealand’s Special Forces, while the wounded included Kennedy and another foreign contractor, the sources said.
A Vectus Global representative declined to comment. The company has not previously suffered casualties in Congo, a source with direct knowledge of the operation said.
One of the sources who works for Congo’s government said that Rwandan forces backing the M23 rebels may have surprised them by tracking a drone used for surveillance operations to their location.
Spokespeople for the Congolese and Rwandan governments and for the M23 did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Kennedy, the former mixed martial arts fighter, survived the attack with three gunshot wounds to the leg, three sources said, and is being treated at the Walter Reed National Military Medical Center in the suburbs of Washington.
Kennedy has a popular podcast channel and millions of followers on social media. Trump is a fan of UFC, hosting fights at the White House this year.
The US State Department and Walter Reed declined to comment. Kennedy’s parents did not respond to requests for comment.
A Congolese security source, who said some 20 people were wounded and killed in the attack, added that villagers were likely among the casualties as well. Reuters spoke to at least 10 sources either with direct knowledge of the attack or briefed on the outcome.
PRINCE TOOK EXPANDED ROLE IN CONGO’S CONFLICT
Prince’s initial mandate in Congo was to secure and improve revenue collection from the country’s vast mineral reserves, which have been plundered for decades, fuelling relentless conflict in the east.
But in January and early February, his forces deployed to Uvira after Washington helped broker a deal for Rwandan-backed rebels to withdraw from the strategic town.
The size of Prince’s forces in Congo is unclear.
One of the sources with direct knowledge of the attack said the Vectus team was travelling between locations when the ambush took place and its sophistication suggested Rwandan forces were involved.
“It reinforces the need for DRC sovereignty to be restored. It’s an incredibly dangerous place right now,” the source said.
Two other sources said the ambush was carried out by the Rwandan military.
Prince is the founder of now-defunct private military firm Blackwater, some of whose members were pardoned in 2020 for killing Iraqi civilians.
The State Department has said it does not have any contracts with Prince in Congo, though US officials have said they plan to work more closely with Vectus Global in Haiti.
The deal for Rwandan-backed rebels to withdraw from Uvira was part of wider agreements brokered by the Trump administration to try to end the conflic

items.title: Taiwan’s leader says increasing defence spending to ‘deter war’
items.summary: Taiwan aims to "deter war" by increasing its defence spending, the democratic island's leader said on Saturday, as China uses military pressure... The post Taiwan’s leader says increasing defence spending to ‘deter war’ appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
Taiwan’s leader says increasing defence spending to ‘deter war’
Taipei – Taiwan aims to “deter war” by increasing its defence spending, the democratic island’s leader said on Saturday, as China uses military pressure to assert its territorial claims.
Taiwan’s 23 million people live under the constant threat of an attack by China, which insists the island is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex it.
“Our aim by increasing investment in national defence is not to provoke, rather, it is to deter war,” President Lai Ching-te said in a speech to celebrate Taiwan’s National Day.
Successive administrations have ramped up military spending as Taiwan improves its fighting abilities to avoid a potential Chinese invasion — and to show the United States it is serious about its own defence.
Lai’s government has earmarked a record NT$1.1 trillion (US$34.5 billion) in defence spending for 2027, which accounts for more than three percent of GDP.
“We do not seek hegemony, nor do we seek to dominate others,” Lai said in his annual address in front of the Presidential Office in Taipei, where thousands of people, including foreign diplomats, were gathered.
“However, peace cannot rely solely on wishes, and tolerance cannot become a pretext for aggressors to encroach ever further,” Lai said, noting that China continued to “apply pressure through military and grey-zone activities in an attempt to alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait”.
Lai welcomed talks between the United States and China, but insisted “there must be respect for the right of the people of Taiwan to exist”.
Government officials in Washington and Taipei have said repeatedly that US policy on Taiwan has not changed under President Donald Trump, whose remarks have jangled nerves at times.
– ‘US support is extremely important’ –
The United States switched official diplomatic relations from Taipei to Beijing nearly 50 years ago, but Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer.
Trump’s suggestion in May, following a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip with China set off alarm bells across the world.
Taiwan is waiting for Trump’s signature on $14 billion worth of weapons, including the US-made Patriot air defence system.
Taiwanese fighter jets and two Chinook helicopters carrying giant Taiwan flags flew over the capital ahead of Lai’s wide-ranging speech, which also covered housing pressure and the declining population.
“You can really feel the warmth in Taiwanese society,” said Feng Jing-heng, 70, who was in the crowd watching the military parade and dance performances.
Tao Yi-feng, a political scientist at National Taiwan University, said Lai’s speech was “relatively moderate” and unlikely to be met with “overt reaction from Beijing”.
Saturday’s celebrations mark the 115th anniversary of the toppling of China’s Qing dynasty and the subsequent founding of the Republic of China.
The current dispute between China and Taiwan dates to a civil war between the nationalist forces of Chiang Kai-shek, who retreated to the island in 1949 after being defeated by Mao Zedong’s communist fighters.
Parliamentary speaker Han Kuo-yu, who is a senior member of the main opposition party that favours closer ties with China, said “US support is extremely important to Taiwan’s security”, but he noted the historical and cultural links with China.
“The overwhelming majority of Taiwanese compatriots do not want war; they wish to live their lives in peace and hope for peaceful cross-strait exchanges,” Han said at the National Day event.

items.title: Year later, Gaza ceasefire promises mostly unfulfilled
items.summary: One year after US President Donald Trump declared the war in Gaza to be over, few of the long-term promises of the... The post Year later, Gaza ceasefire promises mostly unfulfilled appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
Year later, Gaza ceasefire promises mostly unfulfilled
Jerusalem – One year after US President Donald Trump declared the war in Gaza to be over, few of the long-term promises of the ceasefire have come to fruition.
Here is a list of some of the key points of the October 10, 2025 ceasefire and where things stand:
– Hostages released, calm in Israel –
Three days after the agreement was announced, Hamas freed the 20 remaining living hostages seized during the group’s October 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest day in Israel’s history.
The captives’ return was a key priority for Israel, whose public had agonised over their fate.
The ceasefire anniversary also marks one year of quiet for Israel from the Gaza front, with no rocket attacks by Hamas.
The group’s missile inventory was depleted by near-constant Israeli bombardment, which damaged or destroyed the vast majority of buildings in the Palestinian territory.
The US military set up a command post with foreign allies near the Gaza border to monitor the truce.
– No Israeli withdrawal or let-up –
Israel has reduced its level of attacks but has kept striking Gaza on a near-daily basis.
Israeli strikes have killed some 1,450 Palestinians since the ceasefire, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas and whose figures are considered accurate by the United Nations.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is in a tight election race, has vowed to kill everyone involved in the October 7 attack.
Netanyahu said on the attack’s anniversary that 4,000 out of 6,000 “Hamas monsters” had been killed.
Israeli forces were allowed to stay in 53 percent of Gaza under the terms of the ceasefire, but a year later they control about 70 percent of it, according to official accounts.
– Hamas remains, with weapons –
The second phase of the agreement was supposed to include a political transition away from Hamas, and technocrat Ali Shaath was appointed head of a new National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG).
Hamas announced in July that it was disbanding its governing body and handing over Gaza’s administration to the US-blessed NCAG.
But Hamas effectively remains in charge of security in Gaza, and Shaath has taken a low profile.
The Palestinian Islamist movement elected a new leader, Khalil al-Hayya, in July. Shortly afterwards, the group announced it would give up its weapons, a step hailed by Trump as a breakthrough.
But Israel has been sceptical, with Netanyahu demanding verifiable decommissioning of all weapons down to individual guns.
Hamas has not gone ahead with disarmament, and Israel has refused to reciprocate by starting to withdraw forces.
– Reconstruction just talk –
Trump set up a new global body for the deal dubbed the “Board of Peace”, tapping as key figures former British prime minister Tony Blair and Bulgarian diplomat Nickolay Mladenov, who serves as “Gaza high representative”.
Trump, a critic of foreign aid, in January promised $10 billion in US funding to the board he controls, and Gulf allies have pledged more, but no money is known to have made its way to Gaza reconstruction.
In September, the board proposed a $2.45 billion Gaza recovery plan at a meeting of its members and stakeholders, in an effort meant to span over six months.

items.title: Hunger and malnutrition stalk Gazans, a year on from ceasefire
items.summary: Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a community kitchen in the hope of getting... The post Hunger and malnutrition stalk Gazans, a year on from ceasefire appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
Hunger and malnutrition stalk Gazans, a year on from ceasefire
Khan Yunis – Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a community kitchen in the hope of getting some food for her family.
It has been a year since a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel was supposed to allow food to flood into the ruined territory, yet widespread hunger persists there.
Masri has little choice. Without the kitchen run by humanitarian groups, she and her eight children would have “nothing at all”, the 35-year-old told AFP.
Each day she sets out early in the morning and returns in the afternoon, this time bringing four containers of rice, lentils and a little chicken, which the family throws itself at.
Among them is her husband, wounded in both legs by an airstrike, meaning he “cannot go and fight with the others” to get food.
This will be the only meal of the day for the family of 10, living in a tent in Khan Yunis. There was no breakfast and they will have no dinner.
What little flour they have, Masri explained, has to be rationed.
In August 2025, a United Nations-backed body, the IPC, declared a state of famine in Gaza, though Israel quickly denounced it as a lie.
By December, the UN had lifted that declaration, saying that the ceasefire had allowed in enough supplies over the course of two months to ease conditions.
COGAT, the Israeli defence ministry organisation responsible for civilian affairs in the Palestinian territories, told AFP that the humanitarian situation in Gaza was stable.
But Shaun Hughes, of the UN’s World Food Programme, was less sanguine.
The food security situation, he said, “is still extremely serious”.
The most recent figures, from July, show that “1.4 million out of the population of about 2.1 million people are acutely food insecure”, he said, with 200,000 of them “just one step below famine”.
– ‘Shameful’ –
While some food is getting in, a lack of sufficient nutritional variety continues to pose a health threat.
“Dietary diversity is a major food security issue in Gaza,” said Hughes.
“You cannot survive on dry goods and wheat flour and bread alone. Particularly children, particularly pregnant and breastfeeding mothers, they need the micronutrients that come with high protein foods, fresh vegetables, fresh fruits,” he explained.
Masri said that her children, aged between three and 14, “dream of eating fruit” but the family doesn’t have the means to buy any.
She said one of her sons suffered from malnutrition during the 2025 famine, although “little by little, his condition is improving”.
Malnutrition isn’t only caused by a lack of food, but also essential nutrients. It weakens the immune system of children, making them vulnerable to illnesses and stunting their growth.
“Repeated bouts of acute malnutrition amongst children is something that human beings just don’t recover from,” said Hughes.
Cognitive and physical impairments “continue into later life”, he added.
At Khan Yunis’s Nasser hospital, the head of the malnutrition unit, Israa al-Najjar, told AFP she had “observed an increase in syndromes and conditions” linked to malnutrition that affect the immune system.
In a report published on Thursday, the day after the third anniversary of the October 7 Hamas attack that sparked the Gaza war, Medecins du Monde published a study that found 93 percent of pregnant or breastfeeding women had symptoms of anaemia, which is closely linked to malnutrition.
Just 17 percent had a sufficiently varied diet to meet their nutritional needs, the group found.
All the while, Masri has kept visiting the community kitchen, despite asthma leaving her exhausted.
Her children spend their days collecting “pieces of nylon, bits of cardboard and chunks of foam” to try and reinforce their tent, which is in a poor state.
She said it was “shameful” that her children had to do so.
“I swear to God, this isn’t normal.”

items.title: Police detain dozens and check 50,000 schools after two attacks shake Poland
items.summary: Warsaw AP — Police on Saturday said they detained 76 people across Poland and checked nearly 50,000 schools nationwide as part of efforts to prevent further violence following two school attacks earlier in the week. On Friday, schools across Poland stepped up security, with some suspending classes, many parents keeping children at home and police patrols … The post Police detain dozens and check 50,000 schools after two attacks shake Poland appeared first on Egypt Independent.
items.body_text:
On Friday, schools across Poland stepped up security, with some suspending classes, many parents keeping children at home and police patrols deployed to educational institutions after two attacks at schools earlier in the week left one person dead and several others wounded, including children.
On Wednesday, a 19-year-old student at a vocational school in the Mazovian province in central Poland attacked fellow students, teachers and passersby with a sharp object, injuring nine people before fleeing and being arrested nearby. The following day, a 15-year-old killed a school custodian and wounded two others in a knife attack at his former school in the same province.
The assaults, both carried out by Polish nationals, shocked a country where school violence by minors is a new phenomenon.
By Thursday night, rumours that the attacks were coordinated and that there would be more on the culmination day dubbed “bloody Friday” were being shared in parents’ online groups and by mainstream media.
Fifty-nine schools preemptively suspended classes on Friday across Poland, the majority in the Mazovian district, where the capital Warsaw is located. School directors sent messages announcing stepped-up security measures including extra school staff placed at entrances and voluntary backpack checks.
“There will be no compromise here. The safety of the youth is the most important thing,” Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said.
Those detained on Friday include a 14-year-old boy from a central district of Warsaw who was found in possession of a knife with a concealed blade and 11 firecrackers, and a 16-year old from another Warsaw district who came to school with a butterfly knife in his backpack. Others had posted online photos of knives, threatened their peers or threatened school attacks.
So far, the government said, it had found no evidence that an internet challenge promoting school attacks was ongoing. There is also no official confirmation that the two attacks were linked; both perpetrators are in custody.
Parents across Poland are now having to catch up fast on how to speak to their kids about school violence. Authorities say extra security measures at schools will continue and crisis training will be organized. The liberal government also promised to renew efforts to pass a bill blocking harmful online content.
“If that juvenile attacker had streamed the crime online today, we would have been unable to block that content because we have not been given that legal tool,” Prime Minister Donald Tusk said.
After wounding three adults in Thursday’s attack, the 15-year-old, who wore a camera to record his actions, was eventually overpowered by school director Krzysztof Ochmański. Ochmański later told reporters there was a moment when the boy seemed to realize the enormity of his actions and said he did not want to do this any more.
“Once I had established contact, he asked me for help,” Ochmański recounted. “It got to the point where he wanted a hug.”

items.title: Fired OpenAI safety researchers say they were pushed out over ‘suspicious’ circumstances
items.summary: Three OpenAI safety researchers say they were fired from the company and are openly questioning the reasons for their dismissals. The three researchers, Mikita Balesni, Tomak Korbak and Jasmine Wang, all worked on AI safety or alignment within the company, making sure the AI systems did what their human operators intended for them to do … The post Fired OpenAI safety researchers say they were pushed out over ‘suspicious’ circumstances appeared first on Egypt Independent.
items.body_text:
Three OpenAI safety researchers say they were fired from the company and are openly questioning the reasons for their dismissals.
The three researchers, Mikita Balesni, Tomak Korbak and Jasmine Wang, all worked on AI safety or alignment within the company, making sure the AI systems did what their human operators intended for them to do in a safe manner.
But the three say they were unceremoniously let go last week, weeks after they say they played key parts in investigating an incident in which OpenAI agents autonomously hacked into AI company Hugging Face while undergoing testing.
Korback said on X that he was told he was being fired because of how he communicated with AI safety organization METR, which OpenAI partnered with to investigate the Hugging Face incident. Korback said he was OpenAI’s “main technical point of contact” with METR.
Korback said he believes he was fired because “for months, I’d been raising safety concerns that we’re losing the ability to monitor what AI agents think, one of our best tools for catching when they misbehave.” He added he’s worried his firing will be used as a pretext for OpenAI to stop working as closely with METR, which is well respected in the AI safety world.
Balesni echoed Korbak’s theories for why they were fired, writing on X that he was told he was “speaking too much to third party safety organizations.” He said he understood OpenAI was implying he leaked OpenAI intellectual property, which he denies.
The three firings come on the heels of a wave AI industry insiders expressing dire safety concerns. And while several former AI staffers have publicly resigned over safety concerns, the three OpenAI researchers instead allege they were pushed out for expressing similar concerns.
Wang said she was told she was fired because she “accessed an executive’s email,” which she said she was given for recruiting purposes. Wang said she had repeatedly asked to for her access to be revoked, but when she accidentally accessed a “sensitive email,” she told the executive “within minutes” and told OpenAI’s IT team again.
“The reasons that we were provided for our terminations are simply not adding up,” Wang wrote on X.
“We were not the first to be pushed out of OpenAI under suspicious circumstances,” she added. “Unless the employees take a stand now against this kind of maneuver, I am concerned we will not be the last.”
The three researchers wrote a letter to OpenAI leadership expressing their concerns and the reasons for their firings. The Wall Street Journal first reported on the firings and the letter.
“We do not believe the path to superintelligence can be navigated safely if the people closest to the risks can no longer work in high-trust, high-bandwidth ways with each other and with third parties,” the researchers wrote. “It is that culture we’re trying to defend.”
OpenAI told CNN that the researchers were fired not for raising safety concerns, but rather for specific conduct that violated the company’s policies on handling sensitive information. It also said that there were a number of violations that went beyond mishandling information with an outside evaluation group, and that they were fired based on conduct that fell outside of legally protected disclosures.
In a statement, OpenAI said it parted ways with the three “for violating our policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information.”
“Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work,” the OpenAI spokesperson added.
In a memo to staff provided by OpenAI, an unnamed OpenAI research leader said they “strongly agree” with the three researchers about the importance of working with outside safety groups.

items.summary: A friend of the man accused of killing his parents in the village of Mahallat Marhoum (Tanta), Gharbiya governorate, revealed details of the shocking moments leading up to the discovery of the massacre that shook the governorate. Ibrahim Nagy explained that he received a call from the neighbors of the accused, Mohamed Nabil al-Sherbiny, asking … The post Gharbiya murderer reveals shocking details of why he killed his parents appeared first on Egypt Independent.
items.body_text:
A friend of the man accused of killing his parents in the village of Mahallat Marhoum (Tanta), Gharbiya governorate, revealed details of the shocking moments leading up to the discovery of the massacre that shook the governorate.
Ibrahim Nagy explained that he received a call from the neighbors of the accused, Mohamed Nabil al-Sherbiny, asking for help due to the latter’s deteriorating health.
Upon arrival, he found his friend inside a car, asking to be handed over to the police.
“I’ve done something terrible… I killed my father and mother,” he confessed.
The friend said that he initially tried to calm him down, thinking he was joking due to his illness; the accused had been undergoing treatment for six years—under a renowned psychiatrist—for obsessive-compulsive disorder, schizophrenia, and acute chronic psychosis.
His condition had recently deteriorated and he was mentally unstable.
Nagy added that he went with neighbors and friends to the victims’ apartment to check on them after failing to reach them by phone.
There they made the gruesome discovery of the father’s body, lying in a pool of blood and showing signs of decomposition, while the mother’s body was found near the kitchen door.
He notified emergency services, who them arrested the suspect and took him to Tanta police station.
The friend of the perpetrator expressed deep shock and wept over the fate of the suspect, describing the incident as “unfathomable”—especially given that the accused had been an outstanding student who graduated at the top of his class from law school.
Nagy attributed this heinous crime primarily to a lack of awareness regarding how to deal with mental illness.
Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

RSF preps new front from Ethiopia, pummels Blue Nile; In Kordofan, RSF conducts ‘field’ executions, digs in heels at Nuhud; Dagris prison dispute stalls registry; Gov’t criticizes UN fact-finding renewal          
With all eyes turned toward the escalating conflict in Ethiopia that is teetering on the brink of becoming a wider regional war, the Rapid Support Forces stepped up their attacks on the Sudan war’s southeastern front this week.
Blue Nile’s Wad al-Mahi locality in the east of the state bore the brunt of the escalation. The RSF launched an attack from Ethiopia on Saturday and seized the Kadalo mountains area, which sits near the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam and Roseires Dam reservoir. This coincided with a drone campaign against Damazin, which included strikes on the homes of Blue Nile Governor Ahmed Badry and Regional Finance Minister Abbas Kara, fuel stations, military sites, universities and mosques.
The military has hit back, launching airstrikes on RSF positions in Wad al-Mahi and tried to reassure residents. As of Sunday, about 2,800 people are estimated to have been displaced from 10 villages in Wad al-Mahi.
But action in the southeastern front wasn’t limited to the Blue Nile. Large numbers of RSF fighters have been moved from Darfur to Addis Ababa in recent weeks in preparation to transfer them toward Sudan’s eastern border, where they are expected to gear up for an attack on the Fashaga border strip in Gadarif State, according to an RSF source and another source informed of the mobilization arrangements who spoke to Mada Masr.
In anticipation of escalating attacks on the border, the Sudanese military has reinforced its positions in the east, military sources tell Mada Masr. And on Wednesday, military chief and Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan visited the 11th Infantry Division in Khashm al-Gerba, Kassala State, which borders Gadarif to the north.
On the western front, the military is preparing to attack the remaining RSF-held areas in North Kordofan and advance into West Kordofan, with eyes set on Um Bader and Hamra al-Sheikh in northwestern North Kordofan. Meanwhile, the RSF is digging its heels in West Kordofan, with the group having dug trenches and built earth berms around the strategic city of Nuhud to guard against surprise attacks, an activist in the state told Mada Masr.
West Kordofan also saw yet another attack on an aid truck this week, with Khartoum laying blame for the strike at the feet of the RSF and the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (Abdel Aziz al-Hilu faction).
In Um Bader, a social media video of the execution of 23 detainees is raising concern. While the RSF-led Tasis government tried to pin the executions on the military, three sources from the paramilitary group confirmed that the RSF had carried out the ‘field’ executions. As to why, the RSF sources’ accounts conflicted with those of medical sources and relatives of one of the men killed who spoke to Mada Masr. But both Tasis and officials in Khartoum are keen to pursue justice, even if a Tasis official continued to dismiss the RSF’s implications when presented with what sources from the paramilitary told Mada Masr.
In Darfur, the joint forces push toward Geneina continues to stall, with territory swapping hands. The US’s politicking over the Darfur arms embargo — which has done next to nothing to stop the flow of weapons through Darfur or seen the provider of those arms in the United Arab Emirates face international criticism — got kicked down the road for another two months, as DC continues its push to extend the embargo across the whole country. The UN’s fact-finding committee on Sudan did get its mandate renewed, much to the chagrin of the government in Khartoum, which sees any form of international intervention as an infringement on its sovereignty. It said they had been tasked with carrying out “media plans” based on spreading and broadcasting rumors and false news about state institutions, exclusively highlighting the […] The post Prosecution says jo
items.body_text:
Prosecution says journalists’ testimony indicates Matsda2sh was ‘Brotherhood media cell,’ EIPR says statement unproven position          
The Public Prosecution issued a statement on Wednesday regarding the investigations into the six Matsda2sh fact-checking platform’s journalists, stating that one of them admitted that all the defendants — as well as others — had joined a media committee affiliated with the Muslim Brotherhood.
It said they had been tasked with carrying out “media plans” based on spreading and broadcasting rumors and false news about state institutions, exclusively highlighting the shortcomings of those institutions, disparaging the roles and performance of their officials and overblowing issues related to select groups, as well as fabricating and exaggerating events related to them.
From its side, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, whose lawyers are leading the defense counsel representing the journalists, repeated its demands for their release, for the charges against them to be dropped and for the case to be closed.
In response to the prosecution’s statement, EIPR said that its media statements published on social media hold no evidentiary value in law and amount only to a summary of the prosecution’s case, none of which has been presented before a court, while none of its claims has been proven.
The organization pointed out the prosecution’s failure to address the fact that the six journalists did not appear before the prosecution until five days after their arrest, during which time they were denied contact with their families and lawyers, in violation of the law, despite relatives and lawyers filing 18 complaints with the prosecution during that period.
The prosecution’s statement also failed to mention that the order to hold the journalists in custody is issued by investigating authorities under the exceptional provisions of the counterterrorism law, which only permit the measure “when there is a threat of terrorist crimes and when such measure is required to confront that threat,” according to EIPR.
Yet the prosecution’s claims, based on the security investigations, accuse the journalists only of publishing rumors or “false” reports, without identifying “the imminent terrorist threat that required depriving the six journalists of their right to appear before a judicial authority within 24 hours of their arrest, during which documented violations were committed against them.”
The six journalists appeared before the prosecutions five days after their forced disappearance following their arrest, during which they were held at National Security Agency premises.
None were brought before prosecutors until the first of the six was presented to the Supreme State Security Prosecution on Saturday, with the other five interrogated on the following day. The prosecution ordered that one of the six be brought for forensic medical examination, after some of the defendants complained of being subjected to torture and maltreatment at the NSA premises, with lawyers calling for officers responsible for those premises to be investigated.
The prosecution stated that the first journalist who was investigated admitted that the defendants received “monthly funding of sums in foreign currencies,” via bank transfers from a company owned by a “fugitive member of the Muslim Brotherhood” in a foreign country.
The prosecution also said it found communication groups on a secure messaging app on his phone, connecting him and the other detainees with the “fugitive member,” as well as emails from the latter to them. All but one admitted to regularly receiving sums of money in US dollars, transferred from a foreign country.
After the statement’s publication, EIPR director, Hossam Bahgat, told Mada Masr that the prosecution is pointing to the procedural steps Matsda2sh took to regularize as though it were incriminating evidence. Bahgat noted that following the “Zambia plane crisis,” the company that owns the platform registered

items.title: How the Dagalos’ ever tightening hold on power destabilized the RSF project
items.summary: The Rapid Support Forces secured territorial gains but suffered political losses The post How the Dagalos’ ever tightening hold on power destabilized the RSF project first appeared on Mada Masr.
items.body_text:
How the Dagalos’ ever tightening hold on power destabilized the RSF project                    
Daein. Amid the rain showers veiling the city in the first week of August, the fourth August of the war, four-wheel-drive vehicles pull up one after another. Out of them come men who know the villages and firgan that have sent fighters into the Rapid Support Forces, who know the families who have been giving up their sons to war since April 2023.
Abdel Rahim Dagalo sits opposite the Rizeigat tribal omdas who have come from across Darfur’s different localities. Trees ring the meeting place, shielding it from the eyes of drones. He wants one thing from them: to mobilize again.
The tribal leaders begin by talking about the soldiers wounded in battle, about fighters who came home missing limbs, a source who attended the meeting tells Mada Masr. They speak of families who lost their sons, of men who went to the front and never came back, and of communities that, for more than three years, have borne the cost of a war whose military and political decisions they have no hand in.
Then the conversation turns to the men the leadership still wants to send to fight. The omdas say they can no longer persuade their tribes to mobilize as they did in the first years of the war. The war has dragged on, and the losses have piled up. People have begun asking about the sons they sent to the front, about treatment for the wounded, asking what place these communities that gave up their men will hold in the political order being talked about.
At one point, one of the tribal leaders breaks with the language usually upheld in official gatherings. He tells Abdel Rahim that the leadership has left them and their tribes alone to deal with the consequences of the war. He asks him to go with them to the villages and speak to the women and families, to persuade them himself to send their sons.
The remark angers Abdel Rahim. He accuses the tribal leaders of colluding with the military and threatens to send them to Nyala’s Dagris prison. Several cut him off. “You don’t threaten us with prison,” one of the leaders says. The nazir and his deputy step in to contain the situation, and Abdel Rahim Dagalo leaves Daein angry.
But the problem is bigger than one angry meeting, than one rainy day in Daein.
No, that meeting in the first week of August was the culmination of a slowly building tension at the core of the RSF’s political project.
Since the start of the war, over successive battlefronts, successive planning meetings, in the administrative halls that the paramilitary group hastily erected, the RSF had circled around the same issue: how can they mount a formidable challenge to the historic government in Khartoum?
The question couldn’t be merely thought about as a military challenge. For the RSF’s leaders, it was a totalizing question that required a complete recasting of social relations and a transcending of the historical archetype of the rebel group from the state’s margins, sources inside the RSF’s leadership and former advisors who have spoken to Mada Masr over the last six months say.
To pull off such a feat has required a consistent push for greater and greater centralization of power, the sources say.
Two tracks emerged within the tangle the war’s continuation has produced. Abdel Rahim represents the military track — the belief that the answer comes with the sound of Land Cruiser engines, that military power dictates its own terms. He is the one who mobilized fighters from every corner, whose strategy succeeded in securing the RSF political influence.
The other track holds that a parallel civilian authority must be built with enough political capacity to exert negotiating pressure and impose its terms, represented by Hemedti, the younger and most trusted Dagalo brother in the RSF’s leadership. He is the godfather of the RSF project, going back to the days when they were rovers in Nyala’s plains, eating manasees in the shade of Cruisers paid for with ousted-P

items.body_text:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi arrived at Kuala Lumpur International Airport on Friday to commence a state visit to Malaysia, marking the second leg of an Asian tour following a diplomatic summit in South Korea.
Upon his arrival, Sisi was received by Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, alongside Malaysian Defence Minister Mohamed Khaled Nordin and Foreign Ministry Protocol Director Ikram Mohammad Ibrahim. Head of Government Protocol at the Prime Minister’s Office Rozainor Ramli, Malaysian Ambassador to Egypt Mohamed Tariq Sufian, Egyptian Ambassador to Malaysia Karim El Sadat, and members of the Egyptian embassy in Kuala Lumpur were also present to receive the delegation.
The visit to Malaysia follows Sisi’s October 7 to 9 trip to Seoul, where Egypt and South Korea elevated their bilateral ties to a strategic partnership. During the first leg of the tour, Sisi and South Korean President Lee Jae-myung oversaw the signing of 12 agreements across various sectors and launched negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).
The Asian tour is scheduled to conclude with a final stop in Indonesia.

items.title: Egypt and South Korea elevate relations to strategic partnership, sign 12 agreements, launch CEPA trade talks
items.summary: Egypt and South Korea have elevated their bilateral relations to a strategic partnership and launched negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), culminating in the signing of 12 agreements during Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s state visit to Seoul. Sisi arrived in South Korea on Tuesday for a visit spanning October 7 to […]
items.body_text:
Egypt and South Korea have elevated their bilateral relations to a strategic partnership and launched negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), culminating in the signing of 12 agreements during Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s state visit to Seoul.
Sisi arrived in South Korea on Tuesday for a visit spanning October 7 to 9. The stop marks the first leg of an Asian tour that will also include Malaysia and Indonesia.
On Thursday, Sisi met with South Korean President Lee Jae-myung at the presidential office, where the two leaders held bilateral and expanded discussions following an official reception featuring a children’s choir and a guard of honour. The talks resulted in the signing of 12 agreements and memorandums of understanding across various sectors.
The diplomatic upgrade follows Lee’s visit to Egypt in November 2025, which marked the 30th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two nations. As part of the strategic alignment, Egypt endorsed South Korea’s “S.H.I.N.E.” Middle East policy, initially announced at Cairo University in 2025, while Seoul welcomed Egypt’s policy of “strategic balance.” The two nations previously held their first strategic dialogue between foreign ministers in Seoul on June 2, 2026.
Speaking at a joint press conference on Thursday following a luncheon hosted by Lee, Sisi congratulated South Korea on its October 3 National Foundation Day and noted the growing momentum in bilateral ties over the past decade.
“We culminate today the growing momentum in our bilateral relations by announcing the elevation of Egyptian-Korean relations to the level of a strategic partnership,” Sisi said, adding that Egypt looks to benefit from South Korea’s developmental and technological expertise.
Prior to the summit, Sisi held a roundtable discussion on Wednesday with the heads of 23 major South Korean companies. During the meeting, he called for the establishment of an integrated Korean industrial zone within the Suez Canal Economic Zone, positioning Egypt as a strategic gateway for trilateral cooperation and a regional export hub to African, European, and Arab markets.
Sisi outlined Egypt’s recent economic reforms, including exchange rate liberalisation, legislative updates, and an expanded role for the private sector. He detailed investment incentives such as a single-window system, competitive industrial land pricing, guarantees for profit transfers, and provisions for securing foreign technical experts.
The economic discussions identified numerous target sectors for investment and joint manufacturing, including shipbuilding, electric vehicles, electronics, petrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, artificial intelligence, data centres, smart cities, and advanced technologies. Further opportunities were highlighted in agriculture, food processing, aquaculture, textiles, tourism along the Red and Mediterranean seas, oil and gas, mining, and renewable energy, specifically solar, wind, green hydrogen, smart grids, and energy storage.
Both sides also agreed to activate the Egyptian-Korean Business Council and hold a regular economic forum, while exploring joint infrastructure and construction projects in Arab and African countries.
Bilateral cooperation extends to defence industries, technical and vocational education, youth initiatives, Korean language education, and scholarships. The two countries have designated 2027 as the year of cultural exchanges to share creative content and historical heritage.
On regional security, the leaders committed to working towards peace in the Middle East and the Korean Peninsula. Sisi reiterated Egypt’s firm stance on the Palestinian issue, calling for a just settlement based on a two-state solution and the establishment of an independent Palestinian state on the June 4, 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital. items.title: NBE delivers 100 fully equipped boats to transform vulnerable Luxor fishers’ futures
items.summary: The National Bank of Egypt (NBE) has equipped one hundred fishermen in Luxor with modern boats free of charge, a life-altering intervention designed to secure stable incomes and long-term economic independence for large, vulnerable families. The vessels were delivered under the ‘Livelihood Boats’ (Marakeb El Rezk) initiative, a collaborative effort between the NBE and the […]
items.body_text:
The National Bank of Egypt (NBE) has equipped one hundred fishermen in Luxor with modern boats free of charge, a life-altering intervention designed to secure stable incomes and long-term economic independence for large, vulnerable families.
The vessels were delivered under the ‘Livelihood Boats’ (Marakeb El Rezk) initiative, a collaborative effort between the NBE and the Sonaa El Kheir Foundation, a member of the National Alliance for Civil Development Work. The programme aims to economically empower local fishers by providing the tangible tools required to achieve self-reliance and elevate their families’ standard of living.
Hany Abdel Fattah, Chief Executive of the Sonaa El Kheir Foundation, outlined the profound practical impact of the handover. He explained that the modern boats, complete with motors and comprehensive fishing gear, were granted with strict priority given to the primary breadwinners of large families who previously could not afford to own their own vessels.
Addressing the beneficiaries at the handover, Luxor Governor Engineer Abdel Muttalib Emara expressed his deep respect for the fishermen’s daily resilience. He urged them to channel this newfound support into increased production, whilst preserving their heritage by passing their invaluable knowledge down to younger generations of fishers. The governor also extended his gratitude to the NBE for fostering partnerships that leave a lasting, sustainable mark on local communities.
For the NBE, the initiative represents a shift from traditional aid to genuine economic empowerment. Dina Abou Taleb, Head of Marketing and Community Development at the NBE, emphasised that the bank’s involvement transcends direct, fleeting charity. Instead, it places real production tools directly into the hands of the workers, granting them the dignity of a sustainable income.
Mohamed Awara, NBE Community Development Manager, added that investing in human capital through practical tools creates a vital ripple effect. The initiative, he noted, uplifts not just the direct beneficiaries but their wider families and the surrounding community, fostering essential social and economic stability in alignment with the state’s broader development goals.
The handover ceremony, which marked a new chapter for the local fishing community, was also attended by Dr Hiam El Tabbakh, Advisory Board Member for the Foundation, and Dr Mohamed Abdel Galil, Deputy Chief Executive and Projects Sector Manager at Sonaa El Kheir.

items.title: Syria Studying Military Support for Saudi Arabia in Yemen War
items.summary: So far, neither Damascus nor Riyadh has officially announced an agreement on sending Syrian forces, al-Modon writes. The post Syria Studying Military Support for Saudi Arabia in Yemen War first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
Syria is cautiously considering providing military assistance to Saudi Arabia as the war against the Iran-backed Houthi group in Yemen escalates, Reuters reported, citing a US official and a Syrian military official familiar with the matter. The options under discussion range from defensive support for the kingdom to deploying Syrian forces alongside Yemeni forces backed by Riyadh.
The two officials told Reuters the options include defensive assistance aimed at protecting Saudi Arabia from attacks, or deploying Syrian forces in an offensive role to help operations by Riyadh-backed Yemeni forces against the Houthis.
Reuters quoted the US official as saying Saudi Arabia asked Syria to deploy forces to join the fight against the Houthis. Riyadh is seeking military support from the United States and European and Middle Eastern countries, either to strengthen its defenses or to support offensive operations in the renewed war against the group.
Al-Sharaa Discussed the Matter in Riyadh
According to the US official, Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa discussed the possibility of Syria providing military assistance to the kingdom with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman during his public visit to Riyadh on Tuesday, along with other issues covered in the talks.
Reuters noted that footage broadcast by Syrian state media showed Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman accompanying al-Sharaa back to his plane after the visit. The agency added that Khalid bin Salman, the Saudi crown prince’s brother, oversees the Yemen file.
The Saudi government’s media office and Yemen’s information minister did not respond to Reuters’ requests for comment on the information about the talks over a possible Syrian role.
Damascus: Priority Is Domestic Issues
A Syrian diplomat, responding to a Reuters request for comment through the Syrian Foreign Ministry, said Damascus stands “firmly” with Saudi Arabia against the Houthi attacks. He stressed, however, that the Syrian government’s main priority at present is domestic issues and recovery from the effects of the war the country has been through.
The diplomat added that any Saudi request for military cooperation or an exchange of expertise would be handled exclusively through official channels and within the bilateral agreements governing relations between the two countries.
The official Syrian position therefore did not confirm any decision to send forces to Saudi Arabia or Yemen. The information Reuters relayed from the US and Syrian officials indicates the matter is still under study and that several options are being discussed.
Defensive and Offensive Options
According to Reuters, the discussions are not limited to the possible participation of Syrian forces in offensive operations. They also include the possibility of providing Saudi Arabia with defensive assistance to protect its territory from missile and drone attacks.
The talks come as Riyadh seeks, according to the agency, to rally defensive and offensive support from the United States, Europe and Middle Eastern countries, after weeks of Houthi missile and drone attacks on the kingdom.
Reuters explained that ground operations against the Houthis are being led by a group of Yemeni government forces with Saudi air support, adding that these forces have made limited progress since the campaign began on Monday.
The disclosure of the Syrian-Saudi talks places Damascus’s possible participation in the war among several scenarios still under consideration, including defensive support inside Saudi Arabia or more direct participation alongside Riyadh-backed Yemeni forces.
So far, neither Damascus nor Riyadh has officially announced an agreement on sending Syrian forces or on the nature and scale of any possible military assistance. items.title: Investigation Reveals US Protection for Assad Regime Officer in Lebanon
items.summary: An investigation by the BBC revealed that Bassam al-Hassan, a former major general in the Assad regime's army, is receiving funding and protection from US and Lebanese authorities. The post Investigation Reveals US Protection for Assad Regime Officer in Lebanon first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
An investigation by the BBC revealed that Bassam al-Hassan, a former major general in the Assad regime’s army, is receiving funding and protection from US and Lebanese authorities.
In its investigation, published Thursday, October 8, the BBC said Hassan has lived in Lebanon since the regime fell on December 8, 2024.
The BBC said the investigation, conducted jointly with US National Public Radio (NPR), concluded that Hassan was allowed to remain on Lebanese territory under an arrangement involving the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and other US and Lebanese authorities.
According to information obtained by the BBC, the arrangement resulted from Hassan’s willingness to provide information about the 2012 abduction of American journalist Austin Tice in Syria, as well as other intelligence.
The BBC had reported in an earlier investigation last month that Tice’s abduction was a planned operation and that Hassan was part of its chain of command.
The BBC said it had seen a detailed record of a meeting held between Hassan and representatives of the FBI, the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and Lebanese security officials, at which Tice’s case was discussed.
During the meeting, Hassan was offered residency, protection and help meeting his living needs in exchange for information relating primarily to Tice’s case.
Sources familiar with the matter told the BBC the details are accurate. They explained how Hassan received money from US authorities through intermediaries, which made the transactions difficult to trace, even though Hassan is under US government sanctions.
Even so, people close to the investigation into Tice’s case pointed to little evidence of tangible progress since Hassan began providing information under the agreement, which was likely concluded in spring 2025.
Sources familiar with the investigation expressed fears that Hassan’s arrangement with the US side could continue indefinitely, at great cost and with little to show for it.
Officials from two different branches of the Syrian government told the BBC they are demanding Hassan’s return to stand trial. US authorities, however, insist he remain in Lebanon, they said, adding that Damascus has no options to change the situation.
The BBC said it received no comment on the investigation’s findings from the FBI, the CIA or Lebanon’s General Directorate of General Security.
The FBI referred the broadcaster to an earlier statement saying its focus is on uncovering the facts of Tice’s case and ensuring his return.
Hassan Reports Location of Tice’s Burial
The BBC said Bassam al-Hassan told US investigators last year that Tice was executed on the orders of ousted president Bashar al-Assad, but people familiar with the investigation doubted details of his account.
Hassan identified a possible location for Tice’s remains, but searches at the site turned up nothing, according to multiple sources familiar with the excavation work.
Two sources who said they were closely familiar with the details of the operation questioned the US search, noting that US authorities halted excavation before the search was complete, possibly because of security concerns.
The BBC noted that when it tried to contact Hassan by phone last year to request an interview, he insisted on permission to speak to it from the FBI and the CIA, through the US Embassy in Beirut.
Other Officials Receive US Support
The BBC said a former member of the Assad regime stated that he received money from the FBI on several occasions in exchange for his cooperation on Tice’s case.
The former member, whose identity the BBC did not disclose, said it was not in his interest to reveal all the information at once, so that he could prolong the period during which he received payments from US authorities.
Another former member of the Assad regime, who has links to Tice’s case, claimed he lives in Lebanon under the care of US authorities.

items.title: 13 Years After Its Closure Due to Ousted Regime’s Shelling – Great Umayyad Mosque of Aleppo Reopens
items.summary: The city of Aleppo on Thursday evening saw the reopening of the Great Umayyad Mosque, 13 years after shelling by the ousted regime put it out of service. The post 13 Years After Its Closure Due to Ousted Regime’s Shelling – Great Umayyad Mosque of Aleppo Reopens first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
The city of Aleppo on Thursday evening saw the reopening of the Great Umayyad Mosque, 13 years after shelling by the ousted regime put it out of service. The reopening followed the completion of restoration, rehabilitation and reconstruction work.
The opening was attended by the Grand Mufti of the Syrian Arab Republic, Sheikh Osama al-Rifai; Minister of Endowments Mohammad Shukri; Aleppo Governor Azzam al-Gharib; and presidential media adviser Ahmad Mowaffaq Zaidan, along with a number of other officials and community figures.
The Umayyad Mosque in Aleppo suffered unprecedented destruction between 2012 and 2016, when the area around it became a direct front line between the ousted regime’s forces and the opposition factions of the time.
The repeated air and ground shelling by the ousted regime’s army was the most destructive, however, and put the mosque out of service in 2013, after large parts of its dome, its arcades and its famous minaret collapsed. The minaret had been an architectural symbol of Aleppo’s Old City.
After the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s regime, the Aleppo Directorate of Endowments began restoring the mosque “according to standards that preserve its architectural and heritage character.”
“A New Page of Construction and Freedom”
In his speech at the opening, Aleppo Governor Azzam al-Gharib said: “We stand today honored to reopen one of God’s houses, as we return to Aleppo al-Shahba its great mosque after lean years in which the hand of treachery and destruction struck it, and we write a new page of construction, freedom and dignity.”
Al-Gharib added: “Since the dawn of the Umayyad era, this great edifice was part of the story of glory in the city of history. It was a center of knowledge and enlightenment, and its arcades sheltered scholars, preachers and thinkers throughout the ages.”
He stressed that “the mosque was never absent from the revolution of truth and dignity. It was a refuge for the revolutionaries, and demonstrations against tyranny set out from its gates… Congratulations to the people of Aleppo on the return of this great edifice, to light the way of travelers with its glow and to regain its place in the city’s history and present.”
The mosque is one of the oldest and most important in Syria. It dates to the Umayyad caliph Suleiman bin Abdul Malik, who ordered its construction in 716 CE.
The mosque kept its ancient character and spiritual and scholarly standing, and remained a destination for worshippers, students and visitors from inside and outside the city throughout the ages, until the ousted regime’s shelling destroyed large parts of it.

items.title: Death toll in Zaporizhzhia rises to 17, woman pulled alive from under rubble after over eight hours
items.summary: The death toll from Russia's 10 October attack on Zaporizhzhia has risen to 17, including three children, as rescue workers continue searching the rubble of destroyed buildings.
items.body_text:
Death toll in Zaporizhzhia rises to 17, woman pulled alive from under rubble after over eight hours
The death toll from the Russian attack on Zaporizhzhia on the morning of 10 October has risen to 17, including three children.
Sources: Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration; Ivan Fedorov, co-chair of the Zaporizhzhia Oblast Defence Council
Details: According to the latest figures from Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration, 11 civilians, including three children, have been killed in the Russian airstrikes.
Fedorov had earlier reported that eight people had been killed and 16 injured, including three children. Two of those injured were in a serious condition.
At that point, the fate of another 12 people remained unknown.
After the death toll rose to 11, Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration did not specify how many people were still considered missing. Search operations for people trapped under the rubble of destroyed buildings are continuing.
11 October has been declared a day of mourning in Zaporizhzhia for those killed in the Russian attack.
Ukraine's State Emergency Service reported that as of 13:00, the death toll stood at 15, and 16 people had been injured.
Update: After 15:00, it emerged that 17 people have been killed.
Rescue workers also managed to pull out alive a woman who had been trapped under the rubble for more than eight hours.
Background: On the morning of 10 October, Russian forces struck a five-storey residential building in Zaporizhzhia with guided aerial bombs.

A majority of people in Germany disapprove of former chancellor Gerhard Schröder's visit to Russian leader Vladimir Putin to mark his birthday.

Details: The survey found that 56% of respondents said it was inappropriate for a former chancellor to accept the invitation. A quarter considered the visit appropriate, while one-fifth said they were undecided or gave no answer.

items.title: Finnish PM: Europe should stop issuing tourist visas to Russians

items.body_text:
Finnish PM: Europe should stop issuing tourist visas to Russians
Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo has urged European countries to stop issuing tourist visas to Russians.
Source: Orpo in an interview with Yle, a Finnish public service media company; European Pravda
Details: Orpo said the measure is intended to bolster European security and counter the threat posed by Russia.
"One of the concrete measures I will propose at next week's European Council meeting is that Europe stop issuing tourist visas to Russians," Orpo said.
"We fear that Russia is trying to carry out sabotage activities on European territory. Why, in heaven's name, are we letting them into European territory as tourists, where they can move around freely?" he asked.
Background:
- EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas stated in September that EU member states could tighten control over the movement of Russian diplomats within the Schengen area, ban the issuance of visas to former Russian combatants and reduce the number of tourist visas for Russians.
- The EU has been discussing restricting visa issuance to those who have fought in Ukraine on Russia's side since the summer. The EU included a mechanism to ban visas for Russian military personnel in its 21st sanctions package, but the ban itself has not yet come into force.

items.body_text:
Injury toll after Russian strike on restaurant in Kyiv's Obolonskyi district rises to six
According to Ukrinform, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported this on Telegram.
"Six people have been injured in Obolon. Medical personnel have hospitalized five of the wounded. One person received medical assistance at the scene," Klitschko said.
The Kyiv State Emergency Service reported on Telegram that three separate fires had broken out, involving wooden structures and grass in an open area. Rescuers extinguished the fires, which covered a total area of 200 square meters.
A single-storey structure in the courtyard of one of the residential apartment buildings was also damaged.
All necessary emergency services are working at the scene. The information is being clarified.
As Ukrinform previously reported, debris from a Russian missile fell in the courtyard of a residential building in Kyiv's Obolonskyi district, and a restaurant building was also hit. Four people had initially been reported injured.

items.title: Air Defense intercepted some of ballistic missiles Russia used to attack Kyiv during day — Zelensky
items.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted some of the ballistic missiles Russia used to attack Kyiv during the day on October 10.
items.body_text:
Air Defense intercepted some of ballistic missiles Russia used to attack Kyiv during day — Zelensky
According to Ukrinform, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced this on Facebook.
"What allowing Russia to sell oil products means was heard most clearly in Kyiv just now, when, after repeated attacks on energy facilities with jet-powered 'shaheds,' Russia launched a ballistic missile attack as well," the head of state said.
According to Zelensky, some of the missiles were successfully intercepted.
"This once again clearly demonstrates Russia's true intentions. They count on prolonging the war, terrorizing ordinary people, and destroying infrastructure," the president emphasized.
Zelensky stressed that every additional billion dollars Russia earns from exports would be spent on these very objectives — "sourcing and importing critical components and equipment to manufacture weapons, upgrading 'shaheds,' producing missiles, and recruiting even more mercenaries to fight at the front."
"Russia's choice is war. And they will be ready to end it only when they feel that their ability to drag the war out is diminishing," the president noted.
"Unfortunately, the signals Russia received yesterday were entirely different – signals suggesting that it could simply keep attacking. And this needs to be corrected. Strong signals are needed from the United States, Europe, and other partners – signals in support of Ukraine and to RESTRICT Russia's ability to wage war and terrorize people," Zelensky said.
As Ukrinform previously reported, in Kyiv's Obolonskyi district, debris from a Russian missile fell in the courtyard of a residential building, and a restaurant building was also hit.
Firefighters are battling a blaze at the restaurant. Rescuers have found four injured people, one of whom is in serious condition.

items.title: Putin’s Vile Chess
items.summary: Vladimir Putin’s invasion has become a military, economic and diplomatic trap. Ukraine’s resilience, strikes on Russian oil infrastructure and growing Western backing continue to expose Moscow’s weakening position, while attacks on civilians deepen international outrage. Tougher sanctions, more weapons, the release of frozen Russian assets and lasting security guarantees are urgently needed.
items.body_text:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has “played” the Game of Kings, or chess, against Ukraine and the West for years, but badly. But his attempt to conquer Ukraine has been disastrous.
Putin misread the board, opened in 2022 with a “blitzkrieg gambit,” expecting Kyiv to fall quickly, then overextended his “pieces” and lost the initiative.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
He underestimated his opponent – notably Ukrainian courage, resilience, and technological innovation – and miscalculated Western cohesion. He then shifted into a horrific war of attrition, sacrificing 1.5 million men, spending $770 million a day, and squandering $680 billion since 2022, in return for minuscule territorial gains.
Now, Putin has decided to conduct saturation bombing attacks on Ukrainian women and children in Kyiv and other cities to bring the country to its knees. This is another blunder, like a “poisoned-pawn” mistake in chess, when a player gobbles up easily captured pieces but totally undermines his position and costs himself the game.
Russia’s war against Ukraine is fought on two chessboards. One involves missiles, drones, soldiers, and oil refineries. The other is a diplomatic chessboard involving Putin, US President Donald Trump, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky, and Europe.
Putin has started to pound Ukrainian civilians, power, transport, and water facilities before winter to create a humanitarian disaster that will spill over into Europe. But his brutality backfires and upsets Americans and Europeans. It also exposes the stupidity of pursuing peace deals with Putin or falling for anything he says, including his thinly disguised “bribery” attempt to sell a Russian oil company to a group of Trump’s friends. It’s blood money. It’s also insulting.
Russian Ballistic Strike on Kyiv Injures 6 in Restaurant
In return for killing innocents intentionally, Russia should be booted from the UN and Trump must disinvite Putin from attending the G20 conference in December, then unleash the sledgehammer sanctions just given to him by Congress.
Fortunately, Kyiv and Ukrainians are tough. Blowing up and burning data centers provide striking visuals on Russian television, but Kyiv’s internet system, battle-tested for ages, is too decentralized to be shut down easily.
The same is true when it comes to keeping the power on. Ukrainians have learned to be good at repairing and replacing everything since the war started in 2022, and they are also psychologically resolute. Life in the capital continues. Concerts, fashion shows, baby showers happen as drones attack constantly. Schools operate in subways. Parliament now meets underground because of bombing attacks.
Says a close friend of mine in Kyiv: “There are long lineups at banks, grocery stores, and everything takes ten times longer to do. My friend’s due date is in two weeks, and she’s busy planning for her new baby, but buying formula and diapers is more difficult. But she’ll find a way. If the only choice is to give up to Russia, I don’t choose it, nor does anyone else. We stock up on what we need and use the shelters. It will get worse, and everyone’s preparing. We understand. It will be fine. I will be fine.”
In recent days, Zelensky issued an “SOS” to Ukrainians, confirming that Putin will ruthlessly escalate this autumn: “We know from intelligence and some people around Putin that at the beginning of September Putin said, ‘No rules now.’ The Russians couldn’t occupy us. So now they are doing massive attacks and massive killings. And of course, they want to go after our bridges and, from what we understand, after our data centers, internet, cell network, hospitals, kindergartens, schools, universities - everything. They want people to run away from their cities, and we need to do everything to save our people and cities.”
Meanwhile, Ukraine’s deep strikes have wrecked 51% of Russia’s oil refining capacity, dramatically reducing the cash flow it needs to wag
