items.summary: RAMALLAH, Oct 10 - Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday cancelled legislative elections scheduled for November due to worsening conditions within the Palestinian territories and set a date of September 11, 2027 for both presidential and legislative elections, the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
items.body_text:
Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
RAMALLAH, Oct 10 - Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday cancelled legislative elections scheduled for November due to worsening conditions within the Palestinian territories and set a date of September 11, 2027 for both presidential and legislative elections, the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
Abbas' decree cited "obstacles posed by Israeli measures" to holding elections in November and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions for "free, fair and inclusive elections". It called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza to participate in the polls.
There had been serious doubts that the Palestinian Authority vote would go ahead in late November. The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-06, after which Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas' rival, the Islamist group Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists.
The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel's continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created challenges to preparing for and holding elections on the previous date.
In Gaza, the decree pointed to "exceptional security and humanitarian conditions", the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police.
Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said.
The decision to postpone followed a resolution by the Palestine Liberation Organisation's executive committee and consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address challenges facing the electoral process. REUTERS

items.title: Ethiopian forces regain control of border city after reported Eritrean incursion
items.summary: Oct 10 - Ethiopian government forces and their militia allies entered Adigrat, near the border with Horn of Africa neighbour Eritrea, on Saturday, three residents said, days after Eritrean troops were pushed back from the strategic city.
items.body_text:
Ethiopian forces regain control of border city after reported Eritrean incursion
Oct 10 - Ethiopian government forces and their militia allies entered Adigrat, near the border with Horn of Africa neighbour Eritrea, on Saturday, three residents said, days after Eritrean troops were pushed back from the strategic city.
The incursion by Eritrean troops, which Eritrea has denied and Reuters could not independently verify, has raised fears of a return to all-out war along Ethiopia's northern border where the two nations have clashed before. Conflicts elsewhere in the region and tensions across the Red Sea have further raised the stakes.
Three Adigrat residents told Reuters they had seen the Ethiopian army and an allied militia in the city on Saturday morning, with one of the residents saying they saw soldiers on patrol along with military vehicles.
Reuters could not confirm whether the army was in control of Adigrat, which is located 30 km (19 miles) from the border with Eritrea. Ethiopia's military did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and city officials were not reachable on Saturday.
Ethiopia said in a letter to members of the UN Security Council this week that Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 km (37 miles) inside Tigray in recent days, warning that the presence of foreign forces left it with no option but to defend itself.
Eritrea has said reports of an Eritrean incursion are false and part of an Ethiopian plan to justify a war of aggression.
Explosions were reported near Adigrat on Wednesday and Thursday as the US-based conflict monitor ACLED said Ethiopia used drone strikes against Eritrean forces, who then withdrew from positions near the city.
The explosions continued on Friday, according to an Adigrat resident, who told Reuters they had heard repeated explosions overnight and into the morning several kilometres outside town.
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s spokesperson and Eritrea's Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
ETHIOPIAN SEA ACCESS A FLASH POINT
Yemane said on Friday that Eritrea had shown restraint, accusing landlocked Ethiopia of declaring a war of aggression against his country by stating in 2023 it would acquire sovereign access to the sea.
Ethiopia had access to a coastline for decades until Eritrea gained independence from Addis Ababa in 1993. Ethiopia argues that restoring sea access is an existential issue but has said it would be restored through peace and dialogue.
Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of backing the rebel alliance that has been battling government troops since September 23 in its northern regions of Tigray, Amhara and Afar. Eritrea has denied doing so.
After years of war, Eritrea and Ethiopia made peace in a 2018 agreement that earned Ethiopia's Abiy the Nobel Peace Prize. Eritrea fought in support of Ethiopia’s federal government during a 2020-2022 civil war in Tigray, but relations soured again toward the end of that conflict.
The fighting that broke out last month has been the biggest escalation of violence since the Tigray war, in which hundreds of thousands died. REUTERS

items.title: Astronaut Pikachu logs 67 days and 1,040 orbits aboard ISS – now catch him on Earth
items.summary: He joins an elite club of plush space travellers that includes Snoopy and Grogu.
items.body_text:
Astronaut Pikachu logs 67 days and 1,040 orbits aboard ISS – now catch him on Earth
- Astronaut Pikachu spent 67 days and 1,040 orbits on the ISS, then returned to Earth and began a Europe tour to promote space exploration.
- ESA and The Pokemon Company launched a World Space Week campaign with a travelling exhibition and Pokemon Go events at six European science and space museums.
- French astronaut Sophie Adenot filmed Pikachu’s ISS tour, and ESA said the project aims to inspire future generations through a fun, engaging space experience.
AI generated
After 67 days and 1,040 orbits on board the International Space Station (ISS), Pikachu is back on Earth and on tour across Europe to stoke interest in space exploration.
The spacesuit-clad, yellow, plush space traveller was at the orbiting laboratory from April 11 to June 17 with crew members from the European Space Agency (ESA).
A YouTube video posted on Oct 6 that has since been viewed over a million times shows French astronaut Sophie Adenot giving the plush toy a tour of the ISS.
Pikachu is seen being guided through the station, with visits to its water dispenser, laboratory freezers and crew quarters.
Adenot closes the video by telling Pikachu that, even in space, “you have a tendency to hide everywhere”.
“Yeah, I know you like this game,” she tells him.
Adenot returned to Earth on Oct 8, splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off California aboard SpaceX’s Dragon capsule with three other Crew-12 astronauts.
Her 237-day mission set a record for the longest single spaceflight by a European astronaut.
Pikachu’s space adventure is part of a wider ESA-Pokemon collaboration marking World Space Week from Oct 4 to 10.
The partnership includes a travelling, family-friendly exhibition combining space science with Pokemon storytelling. Displays explain how Europe launches spacecraft, supports astronauts, studies the sun and explores the solar system.
“Inspiring future generations is a key part of ESA’s mission,” said Josef Aschbacher, the agency’s director-general. “Through this collaboration with Pokemon, we are unlocking new ways for people across Europe to connect with space through a unique and engaging experience.”
For fans who prefer their scientific outreach with something to catch, Pokemon Go offered an Astronaut Pikachu through one-star raids and timed research at six European science and space museums.
The locations included London’s Science Museum; Cité de l’espace in Toulouse, France; Deutsches Museum in Nuremberg, Germany; Museu de les Ciències in Valencia, Spain; Space Expo in Noordwijk, Netherlands; and Euro Space Center in Transinne, Belgium.
The event ran through Oct 10. A rare Shiny version of Astronaut Pikachu was also offered.
Pikachu joins an elite club of plush space travellers that include Snoopy, who was on NASA’s uncrewed Artemis I lunar mission, and Grogu, the mascot on SpaceX’s Crew-1 flight.

- Strait war risk exaggerated: US official A SHARED GOAL: The US and China do not want conflict, US diplomat Michael DeSombre said, adding that Xi was a ‘rational actor’ who calculates strategic risks
  - Staff writer, with CNA
Global investors are overestimating the likelihood of a conflict across the Taiwan Strait by next year, a senior US diplomat told CNBC on Thursday, adding that robust cross-strait deterrence and the prospect of severe repercussions would prevent Beijing from acting. Markets have exaggerated reports that Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) has instructed the Chinese People’s Liberation Army to be prepared for an invasion of Taiwan by next year, US Assistant Secretary of State for East Asian and Pacific Affairs Michael DeSombre said. “I actually think the most mispricing is with regard to Taiwan, where actually I think people are overpricing the risk of something happening across the Taiwan Strait,” DeSombre said, expressing confidence that diplomatic and military deterrence would hold. US Assistant Secretary of State for East Asian and Pacific Affairs Michael DeSombre speaks during a ceremony in Washington on July 27. Photo: EPA / Yonhap “Both China and the US don’t want conflict, and we’re able to deter conflict,” he said, adding that market anxieties are “priced at too high a level.” Xi is a “rational actor” who calculates strategic risks, he said. “To the extent that he realizes that it can’t be done, or it can’t be done without substantial consequences, it won’t happen,” he added. Separately, the US Department of State on Thursday described China’s activities in the east of Taiwan as deeply destabilizing and urged Beijing to stop pressuring Taipei, following a report of a Chinese maritime militia boat in the area in August. “[The US] remains concerned by China’s activity east of Taiwan,” a department spokesperson said. “China’s actions are deeply destabilizing. By asserting authorities around maritime areas that Taiwan has peacefully administered for over 70 years, China only exacerbates tensions and undermines the peaceful resolution of issues that it claims to seek.” They also urged Beijing to engage in meaningful dialogue with Taipei’s democratically elected authorities. The statement followed a Reuters report on Thursday that a Chinese maritime militia boat, the Minfudingyu 07902 (閩福鼎漁07902), had been spotted by Apex Aviation more than 30 nautical miles (55.6km) off Hualien County in mid-August. The Minfudingyu, which Apex identified as a fishing vessel that doubles as a Chinese maritime militia vessel, was accompanied by a China Coast Guard cutter and a research vessel at the time, Reuters said. The Ministry of National Defense said China was using law enforcement and scientific research as pretexts to expand its activities without triggering a conflict, create the impression that it had jurisdiction over the waters and challenge Taiwan’s maritime law enforcement authority. The Coast Guard Administration said all the Chinese vessels in question were operating outside Taiwan’s restricted waters and that it had monitored their movements throughout and responded appropriately.

items.body_text:
- King Mswati III pledges deeper Taiwan-Eswatini ties
  - Staff writer, with Reuters and CNA
Eswatini’s king yesterday pledged to deepen his country’s “enduring friendship” with Taiwan during a return visit to Taipei after President William Lai’s (賴清德) trip to the southern African nation in May that China tried to block. King Mswati III arrived early yesterday for a state visit until Saturday next week. He is to attend today’s Double Ten National Day celebrations in Taipei. The trip is his 20th visit to Taiwan and comes as the two countries celebrate 58 years of diplomatic ties. President William Lai, front left, welcomes King Mswati III of Eswatini, front right, with full military honors at Liberty Square in Taipei yesterday. Photo: Tu Chien-jung, Taipei Times Eswatini would continue to advocate for Taiwan’s meaningful participation in the UN, the monarch said. “We deeply value the enduring friendship and cooperation between our two countries, and we look forward to strengthening these bonds for the benefit of our peoples,” the king told a welcoming ceremony on Liberty Square. Lai said the two sides had always collaborated from a position of trust and were partners who “support each other and grow together.” Cooperation with Eswatini has expanded under Taiwan’s diplomatic initiative to promote shared prosperity with its allies, with increasingly close exchanges between the two countries’ peoples, Lai said. In separate remarks, Lai thanked the king for supporting the establishment of a Taiwan Industrial Innovation Park in Eswatini and expressed hope that more Taiwanese companies would invest there, making the country a gateway to African markets. The two leaders also witnessed the signing of an agreement on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters, which Lai described as a milestone in law enforcement cooperation. Mswati emphasized turning existing bilateral agreements into practical cooperation and encouraging partnerships between businesses. “We need to put them into action,” he said, calling for officials to study how the agreements could be implemented effectively. Mswati’s itinerary includes observing a joint ground-air military exercise alongside Lai, a visit to an agricultural research center and an investment dinner hosted by Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung (林佳龍), the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said. Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokeswoman Mao Ning (毛寧) said the king was interfering in China’s internal affairs and “ignoring the long-term interests of his people.” The former Swaziland is one of just 12 small states, mostly in Latin America, the Caribbean and the Pacific, that have formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan. In April, Taiwan accused China of pressuring three other African countries to block overflight permission for Lai’s aircraft, causing him to postpone a plan to join celebrations of the 40th anniversary of the king’s accession. That was the first time a Taiwanese president had canceled an entire foreign trip due to denial of airspace access, an apparent new Chinese strategy to curb the nation’s international ties. Lai made a surprise trip in May, using an “arrive, then announce” approach.

items.title: Taiwan offers much more than tech, Tsai Ing-wen says
items.body_text:
- Taiwan offers much more than tech, Tsai Ing-wen says THREATS: Democracies face domestic divisions, outside authoritarian influence and technology that make it easy to spread disinformation across borders, the ex-president said
  - Staff writer, with CNA, SAN FRANCISCO
Taiwan offers the global democratic community much more than just semiconductors, former president Tsai Ing-wen (蔡英文) told an audience at Stanford University’s Hoover Institution in San Francisco on Thursday, while defending her “boring” leadership style as a necessary asset to find common ground. Tsai spoke about how Taiwan has managed differences, responded to crises and built societal resilience. Discussions about Taiwan often focus on semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), cross-strait relations, the risk of conflict and occasionally touch on its popular food and drinks, she said. Former president Tsai Ing-wen points to a drawing of herself at the Startup Island Taiwan Silicon Valley Hub in Palo Alto, California, on Thursday. Photo: CNA However, those topics are only part of the story, Tsai said, pointing to the nation’s 23 million people and their experience of building a democracy under challenging circumstances. “That experience has shaped who we are and continues to shape how we approach the future,” she said. Democracies face growing challenges from outside and within, as increasingly sophisticated authoritarian influence campaigns coincide with domestic populism and political polarization, she said. The domestic divisions make it harder to reach a consensus on how to respond to outside threats, she added. Tsai also warned that advances in AI have lowered language barriers, making it easier to spread disinformation across borders. “Ill-intentioned actors, especially from outside, use social media platforms to spread false and misleading information to drive a wedge between fellow citizens, between societies and their governments, and even between countries,” she said. However, decades of external pressure and intense domestic political competition have taught Taiwan how to safeguard democracy while keeping its institutions open and its society resilient, Tsai said. Taiwan has moved from authoritarian rule to its first direct presidential election in 1996 to become the vibrant democracy it is today, she said. “That transition taught us how to confront deep political differences without allowing those differences to make democratic progress impossible,” she said. Managing relations with China has required preparedness and restraint, Tsai said, adding that decades of pressure from Beijing have made Taiwan more resilient and pragmatic. Although Taiwanese hold differing views on what form relations with China should take, there is a consensus on maintaining the cross-strait “status quo,” avoiding unnecessary provocation, and protecting Taiwan’s democracy and security, she said. “Democracy, resilience and partnership are the foundation of our collective future,” Tsai said, adding that no amount of threats or coercion would shake Taiwan’s determination to engage with and contribute to the world. While some people described her as “boring” during her time as president, Tsai said that “being boring can be useful” in an era of increasing political polarization in which provocation attracts more attention than restraint. This is especially true when needing to ensure Taiwan’s security while finding enough common ground to keep democracy moving forward, she added. Tsai arrived in the US on Monday and is scheduled to return to Taiwan tomorrow. Additional reporting by Su Yung-yao

items.title: China’s new development plan includes AI safety goals – Xinhua
items.summary: A new broad set of economic development guidelines adopted by Chinese leadership includes demands for establishing artificial intelligence safeguards while expanding the use of AI across industries, state news agency Xinhua reported Friday. Xinhua said that the Chinese Communist Party’s Central Committee and the State Council had issued a set of guidelines “aimed at accelerating […]
items.body_text:
China’s new development plan includes AI safety goals – Xinhua
The guidelines “outline 19 key measures in five areas”, Xinhua said, including “advancing scientific and technological innovation” and “deepening the integration of sci-tech and industrial innovation”.
A new broad set of economic development guidelines adopted by Chinese leadership includes demands for establishing artificial intelligence safeguards while expanding the use of AI across industries, state news agency Xinhua reported Friday.
Xinhua said that the Chinese Communist Party’s Central Committee and the State Council had issued a set of guidelines “aimed at accelerating the development of new quality productive forces”.
The guidelines “outline 19 key measures in five areas”, Xinhua said, including “advancing scientific and technological innovation” and “deepening the integration of sci-tech and industrial innovation”.
Among the guidelines is the full implementation of China’s “AI Plus” initiative to transform industries with the new technology through a broad expansion of its use across the economy.
They also note that “efforts are also needed to establish systems for technology monitoring, early risk warning and emergency response to ensure that AI is safe, reliable and controllable,” Xinhua said.
The new development guidelines come after President Xi Jinping said this summer that AI should be “always under human control”, calling for more “laws and regulations, technological monitoring, early warning, and emergency response systems”.
US President Donald Trump, viewing the technology as a key area of competition of China, has instead urged more limited government regulation of AI.
Top US tech leaders signed an agreement on self-regulation during a meeting with Trump late last month, which the president said was “morally binding”.
China already has a complex, evolving set of rules on how AI is used, including by children.
Regulations on AI companion bots took effect in July, aiming to curb emotional dependency and banning the creation of digital clones of real people without their consent.

items.title: Taiwan’s leader says increasing defence spending to ‘deter war’
items.summary: Taiwan aims to “deter war” by increasing its defence spending, the democratic island’s leader said on Saturday, as China uses military pressure to assert its territorial claims. Taiwan’s 23 million people live under the constant threat of an attack by China, which insists the island is part of its territory and has threatened to use […]
items.body_text:
Taiwan aims to “deter war” by increasing its defence spending, the democratic island’s leader said on Saturday, as China uses military pressure to assert its territorial claims.
Taiwan’s 23 million people live under the constant threat of an attack by China, which insists the island is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex it.
“Our aim by increasing investment in national defence is not to provoke, rather, it is to deter war,” President Lai Ching-te said in speech to celebrate Taiwan’s National Day.
Successive administrations have ramped up military spending as Taiwan improves its fighting abilities to avoid a potential Chinese invasion — and to show the United States it is serious about its own defence.
Lai’s government has earmarked a record NT$1.1 trillion (US$34.5 billion) in defence spending for 2027, which accounts for more than three percent of GDP.
“We do not seek hegemony, nor do we seek to dominate others,” Lai said in his annual address in front of the Presidential Office in Taipei where thousands of people, including foreign diplomats, were gathered.
“However, peace cannot rely solely on wishes, and tolerance cannot become a pretext for aggressors to encroach ever further,” Lai said, noting China continued to “apply pressure through military and grey-zone activities in an attempt to alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait”.
Lai welcomed talks between the United States and China, but insisted “there must be respect for the right of the people of Taiwan to exist”.
Government officials in Washington and Taipei have said repeatedly that US policy on Taiwan has not changed under President Donald Trump, whose remarks have at times jangled nerves.
‘US support is extremely important’
While the United States switched official diplomatic relations from Taipei to Beijing nearly 50 years ago, Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer.
Trump’s suggestion in May following a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip with China set off alarm bells across the world.
Taiwan is waiting for Trump’s signature on US$14 billion worth of weapons, including the US-made Patriot air defence system.
Taiwanese fighter jets and two Chinook helicopters carrying giant Taiwan flags flew over the capital ahead of Lai’s wide-ranging speech, which also covered housing pressure and the declining population.
“You can really feel the warmth in Taiwanese society,” said Feng Jing-heng, 70, who was in the crowd watching the military parade and dance performances.
Saturday’s celebrations mark the 115th anniversary of the toppling of China’s Qing dynasty and the subsequent founding of the Republic of China.
The current dispute between China and Taiwan dates to a civil war between the nationalist forces of Chiang Kai-shek, who retreated to the island in 1949 after being defeated by Mao Zedong’s communist fighters.
Parliamentary speaker Han Kuo-yu, who is a senior member of the main opposition party that favours closer ties with China, said “US support is extremely important to Taiwan’s security”, but he noted the historical and cultural links with China.
“The overwhelming majority of Taiwanese compatriots do not want war; they wish to live their lives in peace and hope for peaceful cross-strait exchanges,” Han said at the National Day event.

Gone are the days when mainland visitors were drawn to Hong Kong’s high-end shopping. Now, many are descending on once-sleepy neighbourhoods and scenic country parks to “check in” on social […]
items.body_text:
HKFP Lens: 1.4 million visitors flock to Hong Kong over China’s Golden Week holiday
Gone are the days when mainland visitors were drawn to Hong Kong’s high-end shopping. Now, many are descending on once-sleepy neighbourhoods and scenic country parks to “check in” on social media apps like Xiaohongshu.
Over 1.4 million tourists from across the Chinese mainland visited Hong Kong over the weeklong “Golden Week” holiday marking National Day, official statistics have shown.
Gone are the days when mainland visitors were drawn to Hong Kong’s high-end shopping. Now, many are descending on once-sleepy neighbourhoods and scenic country parks to “check in” on social media apps like Xiaohongshu.
On the anniversary of the day the People’s Republic of China was founded in 1949, tourists crowded a Sai Kung trail that offers dramatic views of the Po Pin Chau sea stack, a popular ecotourism site.
Like many other scenic spots in the Hong Kong countryside, the trail was popularised by the Instagram-like Xiaohongshu. On New Year’s Eve last year, a young man from mainland China fell to his death while taking photos from the viewing platform.
Authorities have since introduced a booking system for the Po Pin Chau trail in an effort to curb overtourism.
However, environmental group Greenpeace has reported continuing overcrowding in spite of the new measures. The NGO last week pointed to soil erosion, damage to vegetation, and rampant littering at the site.
Sharp Island, another hotspot in Sai Kung, also saw large crowds of tourists over the Golden Week holiday.
On Sunday, around 3,010 people came ashore at the island’s Half Moon Bay, with many harvesting marine life in the intertidal zone – a practice Greenpeace warns threatens the local environment.
Meanwhile, travellers from mainland China continued to pour into established attractions like Mong Kok and the Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade, as well as sites more recently promoted by the government like the colonial-era Yau Ma Tei Police Station.
New “check-in points” have also sprung up in neighbourhoods that used to be off the beaten path.
In Kennedy Town, visitors posed across the street from a popular café and gathered in a basketball court that went viral for its view of the street below leading down to the harbourside.
According to Immigration Department numbers, the seven-day holiday saw over 1.4 million arrivals by mainland tourists – the second-highest ever recorded for the week, exceeding the government’s original projection of 1.29 million mainland arrivals.

items.body_text:
現身陶藝市集 蘇巧慧：推「老街觀光券」讓新北29區持續發光
民進黨參選人蘇巧慧出席「2026鶯歌產地開放日」陶藝市集，與民眾熱情互動。（記者羅國嘉攝）
民進黨新北市長參選人蘇巧慧今（10日）出席「2026鶯歌產地開放日」陶藝市集，與民眾熱情互動，在祈福牆寫下「2026新北慧贏」、「慧聚鶯歌」。她說，5年來一路攜手在地青年爭取資源打響品牌；隨著捷運三鶯線通車，未來將力推「老街觀光券」與「季季有活動」，串聯產業讓新北29區持續發光。
蘇巧慧今天參加「2026鶯歌產地開放日」陶藝市集，一到場就吸引許多人上前打招呼、爭相合照。她在陶次瓦代代合作會理事長呂家瑋陪同下，逐攤欣賞鶯歌在地品牌的精美陶器，與店家熱情交流，在「鶯式祈福」許願牆陶片寫下「2026新北慧贏」、「慧聚鶯歌」，許下對新北及鶯歌未來發展的期許，期盼讓更多人看見鶯歌的魅力，也讓新北29區持續發光。
蘇巧慧提到，這5年來，她一路陪伴「鶯歌產地開放日」成長，也和在地「陶次瓦代代合作會」的青年們共同努力，持續向中央爭取相關資源，建立鶯歌在地品牌。她強調，鶯歌不只有傳統陶瓷工藝，更有一群充滿行銷創意與行動力的青年，透過新觀念、新方法讓在地產業有新面貌，帶動更多人走進鶯歌、認識鶯歌。
蘇巧慧說，隨著捷運三鶯線通車，不僅讓三峽、鶯歌居民往來更加便利，也串聯起沿線豐富的文化、觀光及藝文景點，為地方帶來更多觀光人潮。未來她將大力推動「老街觀光券」及「老街季季有活動」，結合在地商圈、特色產業與城市行銷，讓更多人走進地方、認識在地品牌，帶動地方消費與產業發展。

items.title: 入住飯店「這些房號」最好避開 旅遊專家曝原因只有一個、而且並非迷信
items.summary: 〔財經頻道／綜合報導〕一位資深旅遊專家分享了他出國入住飯店時盡量避免選擇的一個房間號碼，這與迷信無關。大多數度假者更關心的是房間的景觀、床的大小或是否包含早餐，但飯店房卡上的一個小細節，卻可能預...…
items.body_text:
多數度假者更關心的是房間的景觀、床的大小或是否包含早餐，但飯店房卡上的一個小細節，卻可能預示著你的住宿體驗或許不如預期般寧靜。（歐新社）
〔財經頻道／綜合報導〕一位資深旅遊專家分享了他出國入住飯店時盡量避免選擇的一個房間號碼，這與迷信無關。大多數度假者更關心的是房間的景觀、床的大小或是否包含早餐，但飯店房卡上的一個小細節，卻可能預示著你的住宿體驗或許不如預期般寧靜。
根據歐洲私人旅遊公司 （Europe Private Tours）的旅遊專家阿米爾·蘇德拉 （Amir Sudra） 介紹，房間號以01結尾的房間，例如 101、201、301 或 401，通常值得在入住前詢問清楚。他表示，這條規則並非適用於所有飯店，但他曾多次陪同顧客遊歷歐洲各地，入住過各種類型的飯店，發現同樣的問題反覆出現。
阿米爾解釋說：「每次拿到尾號為01的房間，我都會仔細看兩遍。這並不是因為我迷信，也不是因為這個數字本身有什麼含義。而是因為在很多酒店裡，這些房間通常都靠近電梯、樓梯間或走廊的起點。」他表示：「這意味著你可能會在任何時間聽到客人進出的聲音、電梯門打開的聲音、行李箱被拖過門的聲音，有時甚至在清晨還能聽到工作人員使用附近服務區的聲音。」
他說：「我陪客戶去歐洲旅行時，人們最容易低估的一點就是酒店的佈局對整個旅程的影響。你可以在巴黎、羅馬、巴塞隆納或維也納預訂一家漂亮的酒店，但如果你的房間就在電梯或樓梯旁邊，你可能整晚都在聽其他客人的動靜，而不是睡覺。」
阿米爾指出，在歐洲一些較老的飯店裡，這個問題可能會更加棘手，因為隔音效果可能與建築風格不符。
飯店佈局因飯店而異，但阿米爾指出，房間號尾數較小的房間通常位於每層樓的主要入口附近。利物浦迴聲報（Liverpool Echo）報導稱，雖然這對於不想從電梯走很長一段路的客人來說很方便，但對於任何想要安靜休息的人來說，這都遠非理想之選。
阿米爾表示，客人無需感到尷尬或提出過度要求就能提高入住安靜房間的幾率。他建議在領取房卡前，禮貌地向前台詢問是否有遠離電梯、樓梯和服務區域的房間。
他說：「最好的辦法是在上樓前詢問。一旦你打開行李箱、給手機充電、安頓下來，再走動就會感覺麻煩得多。我通常會簡單地問：『請問能否安排一個遠離電梯或樓梯的安靜房間？』這樣聽起來禮貌、合理，前台也容易理解。」；你不需要說「我不要301房間」，最好解釋一下你真正的顧慮，那就是噪音。

老台北《人間3》重返 吳念真謝幕「什麼流」掀話題
人間3《台北上午零時》重啟巡演，「洋流」也意外成為吳念真（右2）受關注的話題。（綠光劇團提供）
〔記者凌美雪／台北報導〕吳念真的「人間條件」系列已經發展到第8，聚焦台灣土地的故事，尤其刻畫大時代的小人物，無論是虐心的姊妹情、228事件中化母愛為大愛的女人、或是每天買彩券夢想發財的退休老人，不管痛哭流涕或爆笑連連，可說部部都感動人心，且叫好叫座。不過，似乎也有不少觀眾更期待謝幕時吳念真的致詞，一句「最近不是到處有什麼流的嗎？」竟引起台下一陣歡呼。
人間條件3《台北上午零時》9日起第3度登上國家戲劇院，吳念真於當天下午總彩排時，就被問到關於名人挺「洋流」引發後續效應的問題，吳念真回應，「每個人都會做自己的選擇，也要承擔相應的責任。」
9日晚間的首演謝幕，吳念真一如往常上台談談自己對作品重返舞台的想法，但或許因為《人間3》本身演的就是台北的故事，也或許因為對時事仍有所感，吳念真以低調不張揚的語氣緩緩說道，自己今天要出門時，老婆問他是不是要去游泳？他聽得一頭霧水，結果老婆說：「最近不是什麼流～～」
台下觀眾馬上回報熱烈掌聲；之後，在社群平台上有人留言：「我好愛綠光的溫度和那些在戲裡經常對於時事恰到好處的言語」。

items.body_text:
More than 70% of Americans support the U.S. military defending South Korea in the event of a North Korean attack, according to an annual think tank survey published Thursday.
Seventy-seven percent of Republicans and 73% of Democrats back U.S. military support of its longtime ally, according to the survey conducted by the Washington-based Korea Economic Institute of America (KEI) and YouGov.
The poll surveyed 1,207 adults from Aug. 21 to Sept. 1 and had a margin of error of 3.6 percentage points.

items.title: Interview: How bribery holds North Korea’s market economy together
items.summary: A few years ago, two researchers – Dr. Andrew Yeo (Brookings Institution) and Dr. Justin Hastings (University of Sydney) – conducted a series of interviews with North Korean defectors to explore how marketization had changed interpersonal relationships in North Korean society. The vast majority of interviewees alluded to an extensive system of bribery and kickbacks, […]
items.body_text:
A few years ago, two researchers – Dr. Andrew Yeo (Brookings Institution) and Dr. Justin Hastings (University of Sydney) – conducted a series of interviews with North Korean defectors to explore how marketization had changed interpersonal relationships in North Korean society. The vast majority of interviewees alluded to an extensive system of bribery and kickbacks, but virtually none of them expressed any outrage at the “corruption” of the system. Paying (and taking) bribes was simply part of daily life.
This unexpected attitude led Dr. Yeo and Dr. Hastings to conduct a follow-up investigation exploring what exactly North Koreans mean when they use the word bribe (뇌물) and the function that bribery plays in North Korea’s hybrid socialist-market system.
The Unification Media Group’s Rose Adams recently attended a seminar presenting their research and interviewed them about their findings. The interview (edited for clarity) is below.
Q: Could you define what “bribery” means in North Korea? What might be unexpected about it, or different from the definition our English-language readers know?
Andrew: One explanation that stood out came from a merchant we interviewed. He compared bribes to paying taxes in the South Korean system. In other words, bribes are just part of the cost of doing business.
When defectors talk about bribery in daily life, they usually mean a way to get something in short supply or to cut through administrative red tape. In the markets, almost every part of private business is illegal in North Korea, so the “service” the bribe recipient provides is often simply looking the other way.
Q: It’s easy to see the appeal of bribery when both parties get something in return. But what about the bribes people pay to avoid jail time after they’re caught doing something illegal?
Justin: We think of bribery in North Korea as falling broadly into two categories: horizontal and vertical. Horizontal bribes happen between people who are roughly peers, such as ordinary residents and low-level local officials. Here’s an example from the literature. One defector described the expectation that you give your doctor a pack of cigarettes as thanks for a vaccine. The patient does this because he knows the doctor isn’t paid enough to make a living. By staying in his government-assigned post and providing a public service, the doctor also misses out on more lucrative business opportunities.
These bribes are driven less by coercion or quid pro quo than by a shared understanding of what the other person gives up and how hard it is to make a living. Horizontal bribes are part of what we call the moral economy, where things like etiquette and empathy shape economic decisions. They work as a kind of mutual social support, based on the understanding that everyone at this level needs to survive. They also make North Korean society more stable and resilient. They keep services running that the state can’t support, and they let people run the private businesses they need to make a living.
Vertical bribery is different. These bribes aren’t between peers. They happen within hierarchies, where the recipient has significant power over the person paying. That doesn’t make them inherently extortionate. Sometimes you need to pay off someone high up with the authority to get a difficult task done, like moving a large volume of cargo or reducing a harsh prison sentence.
We spoke to North Koreans and to Chinese businessmen who traded with North Korean officials. In vertical relationships, both groups often drew the moral line at necessity. A demand for a bribe was generally seen as reasonable if the amount fit the task, or if the recipient asked for necessities like food or firewood. Participants called it “corruption” or extortion only when bribes were excessive or too frequent for the service provided, or when recipients asked for luxuries like alcohol or designer goods.
In reality, of course, these interactions are complex, and horizontal and vertical

items.title: South Korean-style natural makeup catches on among young North Koreans
items.summary: Young North Koreans in cities such as Chongjin are embracing a subtle, natural South Korean makeup style in 2026 that arrived through people who travel back and forth to China, despite Kim Jong Un’s sweeping crackdown on outside influences. “These days in Chongjin and many other areas, young people do their makeup so naturally that […]
items.body_text:
Young North Koreans in cities such as Chongjin are embracing a subtle, natural South Korean makeup style in 2026 that arrived through people who travel back and forth to China, despite Kim Jong Un’s sweeping crackdown on outside influences.
“These days in Chongjin and many other areas, young people do their makeup so naturally that you can’t even tell,” a source in North Hamgyong province told Daily NK on Friday. “There’s a strong feeling that heavy makeup looks rural and comes across as unsophisticated.”
According to the source, the style first came in through ethnic Chinese traders who frequently cross into China. North Korean workers who returned home after working in Chinese restaurants also helped bring it in. Ethnic Chinese living in North Korea, known as hwagyo, hold Chinese citizenship and can travel across the border far more freely than ordinary North Koreans.
These travelers brought back stories of an effortless look that is popular among young South Koreans. The goal is to appear polished without seeming to have tried at all. As word of the trend spread, light South Korean-style makeup quickly gained a following in North Korean cities.
Some women in their 20s in Chongjin now say that Chinese and South Korean makeup styles are completely different. A common remark among them is that one glance at someone’s makeup shows whether the person is South Korean or Chinese.
“Young people see South Korea as more developed and better off than China, so they want to copy it,” the source said. “As stories spread that South Koreans wear their makeup naturally, more and more young people are following their lead.”
South Korean makeup spreads to high school students
The trend has now reached teenagers in senior middle school, the North Korean equivalent of high school. In the past, most young women in North Korea started wearing makeup only after they had graduated.
“Now it’s easy to spot second- and third-year students wearing makeup just like working adults,” the source said. “Teenagers care a lot about their looks at that age, and they especially want to copy the light South Korean style.”
A source in Ryanggang province described a similar shift among students walking the streets of Hyesan, a city on the Chinese border. “Until a few years ago, a lot of students wore thick powder and heavy eye makeup,” the source said. “They look much better now that the softer South Korean style has caught on.”
High school students and young working women with darker complexions pay close attention to brightening their skin. Many use products such as “Bishong” for this purpose, according to the Ryanggang source. They also keep their lip color natural instead of bold, so makeup overall has become noticeably lighter.
Heavy makeup still prevails in the North Korean countryside, however, because the urban trend has yet to reach farming communities. Many women in rural areas continue to wear dark lipstick and thick layers of powder on their faces.
“It will take some time for the trend to reach the countryside,” the source said. “Farming villages usually pick up a fashion only when it is already fading in the cities.”
The spread of South Korean beauty habits comes as Pyongyang enforces the Reactionary Ideology and Culture Rejection Law. North Korea enacted the law in December 2020 to stamp out foreign media and culture, especially from South Korea. Authorities have since repeatedly punished young people for copying South Korean speech, hairstyles and clothing.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s visit to South Korea on August 19-20, 2026, received relatively little international attention, despite being a consequential meeting for the Korean Peninsula. As China’s top diplomat and a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, Wang Yi delivered Beijing’s strategic foreign policy objectives toward the Korean Peninsula in an unusually candid way, not coded in diplomatic language.
Wang’s visit underscored China’s five closely connected foreign policy objectives. First, Beijing seeks to maintain permanent peace and stability on the Peninsula. Second, China categorically rejects North Korea’s nuclear weapons and maintains denuclearization as a long-term objective. Third, Beijing opposes the emergence of competing security blocs, whether a Russia-DPRK-China alignment or a consolidated U.S.-South Korea-Japan bloc. Fourth, China seeks to reduce U.S. military influence on the Peninsula and ultimately secure the removal of U.S. ground troops. Finally, China strives to build a regional security environment more conducive to its long-term objective of unification with Taiwan. These objectives appear not only in official statements but also in prominent publications from Chinese scholars.
First, North Korea’s belligerent behavior threatens peace and stability in the region. Missile launches and continued nuclear development provide justification for greater U.S-South Korea-Japan security cooperation and expanded military deployments in Northeast Asia. As Yijong Zheng states, “Beijing fundamentally opposes not merely North Korea’s possession of nuclear weapons, but the broader evolution of Northeast Asia’s security structure toward what may be called “deterrence normalization”: a situation in which North Korea’s nuclear status is increasingly accepted, while U.S. extended deterrence and regional military integration are continually reinforced.”[1]
Second, during his visit to Pyongyang on April 9-10, 2026, Wang Yi made it clear that North Korea’s belligerent behavior will come at a cost. As Zheng Jiyong argues, China “does not believe its nuclear status should be cost-free” and will use North Korea’s economic dependence to obtain “specific acts of restraint” from Pyongyang.[2] In exchange, Beijing will condition humanitarian assistance, access to border trade, energy supplies, infrastructure investment, and political backing on North Korean restraint. In practical terms, this means that further nuclear and missile provocations, military escalation, or actions that trigger expanded U.S., South Korean, and Japanese military deployments can come at the cost of diminished Chinese economic support and cooperation. Conversely, broader cooperation with Beijing requires Pyongyang to meet China’s requirements for “border stability, crisis communication, and military restraint.”
Third, China rejects bloc politics and the creation of Cold War-like architecture in Northeast Asia. The Russia-DPRK relationship contributes to a more divided security environment in Northeast Asia. Beijing categorically rejects joining a Russia-DPRK bloc[3] and does not want South Korea to become deeply integrated into a U.S.-Japan-South Korea military alliance. As Zheng Jiyong argues, “for Beijing, the biggest risk of closer North Korean-Russian cooperation is that it provides an excellent pretext for Japan, South Korea, and the U.S. to accelerate the integration of their bloc.” Encouraging South Korea to preserve its strategic autonomy and avoiding bloc confrontation are central to China’s objectives.
Moreover, China and South Korea share fundamental interests in peace, stability, and economic prosperity on the Korean Peninsula, while their economies remain deeply interconnected. During his visit, Wang called for the “resumption of a dialogue, and restoration of mutual trust” and for peaceful coexistence between South Korea and the DPRK, ultimately leading to lasting peace and stability.[4] In

items.title: Zach Bates qualifies on pole for Bathurst 1000
items.summary: Zach Bates has qualified on pole for Sunday's Bathurst 1000, topping the time sheets during the Top 10 Shootout at Mount Panorama.
items.body_text:
Bathurst 1000: Zach Bates wins Top 10 Shootout, qualifies on pole at Mount Panorama
In short:
Zach Bates has qualified on pole for Sunday's Bathurst 1000, topping the time sheets during the Top 10 Shootout at Mount Panorama.
Qualifying king Brodie Kostecki failed to become the first driver to snare four straight pole positions, finishing second.
What's next?
ABC Sport will have a live blog of the Bathurst 1000 from lights out to the chequered flag on Sunday, October 11.
Supercars rookie Zach Bates — not qualifying king Brodie Kostecki — will start the Bathurst 1000 in pole position.
Kostecki was on track to become the first driver to snare four straight pole positions after laying a mighty lap of two minutes and 4.4912 seconds as the fifth driver in Saturday's top-10 shootout.
Proven race winners Will Brown, David Reynolds and Anton De Pasquale tried, but failed to beat Kostecki's time.
But provisional pole-sitter Bates refused to waver, proving his mettle as the last driver with a searing lap around the famous Mount Panorama track.
A day after becoming the fastest Gen3 racer, the 22-year-old clocked 2:04.2062 to deny Kostecki by 0.285 seconds.
Bates had earlier become the first to go below the 2:04 benchmark in the Gen3 era after taking provisional pole with a time of 2:03.9376.
In just his second pursuit of the holy grail of Australian motorsport, Bates is the third rookie to claim pole position after Klaus Ludwig (1987) and Marcos Ambrose (2001).
The Canberra local is the son of former rally and Supercars driver Rick Bates, and the nephew of four-time Australian Rally champion Neal Bates.
His surprise success comes after his mother Alison Drower died from cancer weeks before his Bathurst 1000 debut last year, in which he finished 10th as part of the Triple Eight Race Engineering wildcard with the great Craig Lowndes.
Team 18 driver De Pasquale will start in the second row with fourth-fastest Cooper Murray, while series leader Matt Payne was 10th.
But Grove Racing star Payne will be far from disheartened, given he had started from 18th en route to last year's epic wet-weather triumph with former co-driver Garth Tander.
Reynolds will start on the grid in eighth after a family of ducks threatened to derail his bid for a second Bathurst 1000 title.
Tickford co-driver Mark Winterbottom was forced to a sudden halt when ducks were spotted crossing the track at Conrod Straight during practice on Friday.
Winterbottom's sudden braking caught out Reynolds' co-driver James Courtney, who locked up and slammed into the rear of the Tickford Ford Mustang.
But both cars were able to return to complete the 60-minute practice session before the shootout.
Defending Supercars champion Chaz Mostert was among the big names to miss out on the top-10 shootout and will start from 16th for the best qualifying result in the Toyota Supra.
Payne's teammate Kai Allen fell agonisingly short in 11th, while title contender Broc Feeney was 12th ahead of Cam Waters in 13th.
Kostecki's rookie teammate Rylan Gray will start from the back row with Ryan Wood after the duo crashed out in separate incidents in Friday's first practice session.
ABC Sport will have a live blog of the Bathurst 1000 from lights out to the chequered flag on Sunday, October 11.
BATHURST 1000 TOP 10 SHOOTOUT RESULTS:
1. Zach Bates/Aaron Seton (No.10 Matt Stone Racing)
2. Brodie Kostecki/Todd Hazelwood (No.17 Dick Johnson Racing)
3. Anton De Pasquale/Lee Holdsworth (No.18 Team 18)
4. Cooper Murray/Lachie Dalton (No.99 Erebus Motorsport)
5. Jack Le Brocq/Harri Jones (No.4 Matt Stone Racing)
6. Will Brown/Scott Pye (No.888 Triple Eight Race Engineering)
7. Jayden Ojeda/David Russell (No.31 PremiAir Racing)
8. David Reynolds/James Courtney (No.48 Team 18)
9. James Golding/Richie Stanaway (No.7 Blanchard Racing Team)
10. Matt Payne/Will Davison (No.19 Grove Racing)

items.title: Live: Matt Renshaw nearing 200 as Aussie rearguard action continues in Durban
items.summary: Australia's remarkable day is continuing in Durban, with Matt Renshaw pushing towards a maiden Test double century and the tourists, somehow, closing in on 400. Follow live.
items.body_text:
Sat, 15 Aug, 11:00 pm, Final score, AUS 198 & 284, BAN 426 & 1/57
live
South Africa–Australia first Test live updates: Matt Renshaw notches Durban century
Australia's remarkable day is continuing in Durban, with Matt Renshaw pushing towards a maiden Test double century and the tourists, somehow, closing in on 400.
Follow all the action in our live blog below, keep up with all the stats in our ScoreCentre, and tune in to our live radio call on the ABC Listen app.
Submit a comment or question
Live updates
Live: South Africa vs Australia — first Test in Durban
New: Filters
Choose what information you see below by using filters
Key Event
TEA: Australia 9-390 (Renshaw 190*, Hazlewood 5*)
Expert Test batting by Matthew Renshaw has Australia in complete control as the teams head off for the tea break.
Clouds loom overhead, so hopefully we aren't deprived of a final session, but the Aussies will be pretty gleeful in the sheds for sure.
137th over - Wiaan Mulder rumbles in again
Renshaw appears to be surviving easily. My thinking is he wants to get to 200, get Australia to 400 (11 runs short of both), then he might get a bit more aggressive.
OH he's almost chopped on! Just luck saves him there. South Africa is getting very unlucky today.
Renshaw takes the easy single to deep cover off the fifth ball. He moves to 190.
Hazlewood makes it through, and that's tea.
136th over - Harmer to Renshaw
The reverse sweep is out but he's not timing it as well as he was earlier. Perhaps some fatigue creeping in.
Down leg and clipped away, but again they reject the single. He almost picked the gap there.
Fourth ball, still no single taken as he pushes to long-on. Interesting choice.
He takes it on the fifth ball.
Hazlewood vs Harmer for one delivery. And the Aussie wins.
135th over - Renshaw faces Wiaan Mulder
And he chunks a drive into his front pad to start.
A few better strokes, but no runs being taken against the spread field.
Fifth ball and Renshaw gets across to clip a single to the leg side. Hazlewood has to navigate one Mulder ball. And he does.
134th over - The spin is back
Simon Harmer bowling to Matt Renshaw, who cracks him wide of long-off. I think Anrich Nortje has done enough to save the boundary. But no! The initial stop was fine, but then he touched the ball as it rebounded off his quad and that's four for Renshaw!
He moves to 186 and that's his highest Test score!
Was that a drop? Renshaw tries a reverse sweep and mistimes it. Kyle Verreynne sticks a gloves out to bat it down, but did Renshaw get some bat on it? Harmer looks frustrated but perhaps not enough to suggest any willow on leather.
And Renshaw turns the single to end the over and keep the strike.
133rd - Renshaw hunting his highest Test score
That single to end the last over took Renshaw to 181 off 370. His highest Test score is 184.
Jansen around the wicket is causing him problems when he defends, but he hooks well. Straight to deep square leg, though. And it's too early in the over for Renshaw to take the single.
Loading
Fourth ball and Renshaw works off his hip behind square. They take the single this time and Hazlewood has two balls to negotiate.
FOUR! Hazlewood backs away and carves through cover. Jansen is going to rip his hair out.
132nd over - Anrich Nortje resumes to Matt Renshaw
Will Renshaw try to attack a bit, or is he focused on trying to make it to 200? And getting Australia to 400?
Beaten on the outside edge. Anrich Nortje has bowled a few of them, and keeps coming back for more. Credit where it's due.
But there have been A LOT of leaves by the Aussies. How many balls would've hit the stumps from the South African seamers today? Not many I'd wager.
BANG! Short and crushed on the hook by Renshaw with a gorgeous stroke for four. Perfectly played by a tall man.
And he gets the luck as a thick edge flies too fine for the lone slip in place. But hey, he's the reason the field is so spread. The epitome of 'you make your own luck'.
131st over - Marco Jansen to pepper

items.title: St Kilda end the drought to send Dal Santo out a winner
items.summary: It's been an AFLW season to forget for St Kilda, but Saturday's win over Collingwood has given departing Saints coach Nick Dal Santo a perfect send-off.
items.body_text:
St Kilda gave departing AFLW coach Nick Dal Santo the perfect send-off with a drought-breaking two-point home win over Collingwood.
With the bottom-of-the-table Saints holding a 0-8 record, Dal Santo announced on Friday he was standing down and took charge of the team for the final time in Saturday's game at Moorabbin Oval.
After scoring just one point last week and tallying five behinds in the first half on Saturday, the Saints kicked five second-half goals on their way to a 5.9 (39 ) to 5.7 (37) win.
Loading Twitter content
Jesse Tawhiao-Wardlaw kicked two goals and Tyanna Smith bagged 25 touches and 12 clearances for the Saints, who ended an 11-match losing streak stretching back almost a full year.
Collingwood (1-8) kicked the only two goals of the first half, the first to captain Ruby Schleicher, who later came off the ground with an injury to her right shoulder.
The other major went to Sabrina Frederick in her 100th AFLW game, as Collingwood stretched a two-point lead after a goalless first quarter to 12 at half-time.
With the wind at their backs, the Saints rallied In the third quarter, kicking three straight goals and four for the term to lead by 10 points at the last change.
Ashley Centra, who gathered 25 touches for the Pies, kicked a goal in the final 30 seconds to cut the gap to two points, but the Saints held on.
"I understand this is my last game, but that was a really good game by the girls. I thought we fought really hard," Dal Santo told Fox and Kayo.
"I'm really proud of this group. It's been a delight and I'm really grateful for being a part of their journeys.
"I've loved it. Five years and the time is right," added Dal Santo, who finished with a 23-39 win-loss record.
AAP

Superquiz, Sunday, October 11
Welcome to the new-look Superquiz! Easier to play on your mobile, the new quiz features a fresh design and more interactive features.
Click here to tell us what you think of the new format. Got questions or want to know more? Scroll past the quiz to see our FAQs.
By Michelle Stillman
Why has the quiz changed?
Our new quiz format is faster, smoother and easier to play on your mobile.
We’ve also introduced several new features. For the first time, you’ll see how other players scored in real time and be able to share your result with friends and family on Facebook, X and WhatsApp. We have more exciting updates on the horizon too.
Tell us what you think about the new experience here. We’re keen to hear from you.
Although it has a new look, this is the same Superquiz you know and love. Our regular quizmaster is excited to put your general knowledge to the test with a new set of 15 crafty questions every day.
Can I see the number of questions in the quiz?
Yes, the total number of questions is displayed next to the progress bar at the top of the quiz. The number of your current question is also shown (e.g. 3/15).
Want to keep track of your score? You can find a running tally in green at the top right of the quiz.
Can I see all the quiz questions at a glance?
No, we challenge players to complete the quiz one question at a time.
When I answer a question, there’s a percentage next to the correct and incorrect answers. Why?
Thanks for noticing! This is a new addition to the quiz. It lets you track how your score compares to other readers by showing the percentage of players who chose that particular answer. It will also help you gauge the difficulty of each question after you’ve answered.
Can I reset the quiz for other players on my device?
Yes, click or tap ‘Play Again’ at the end of the results screen to reset the quiz.

items.title: Australia Cup final as it happened: South Melbourne claims Australia Cup on record-breaking night
items.summary: South Melbourne equalised with three minutes left in extra time, then defeated Melbourne Victory on penalties to become the first team from outside the A-League to lift the cup.
items.body_text:
South Melbourne have become the first non A-League team to win the Australia Cup after beating Melbourne Victory on penalties in an emotion-charged blockbuster final.
In one of the greatest nights in Australian domestic soccer history, former NSL powerhouses South first took Victory to extra time then fought back from 1-0 down to level it at 1-1 at the death before winning 4-3 on penalties in front of a pumping sellout crowd of 29,911 fans at AAMI Park.
South Melbourne, who have long craved an A-League licence, only strengthened their bid for that with a win that capped off an extraordinary evening.
Denis Genreau scored an athletic, improvised half-volley in the 95th minute to put Victory in front, before Max Mikkola forced home an equaliser in the 117th minute to send the game to penalties and the crowd into ecstasy.
In the penalty shootout, South goalkeeper Javier Lopez was the hero, denying former South captain Harrison Sawyer, before Victory skipper Jason Davidson hit his must-score penalty over the bar.
In becoming the first NPL team to win the Australia Cup, Sinisa Cohadzic’s South succeed where Heidelberg last year and Sydney United 58 in 2022 could not.
With the win, South also technically claim a berth in next season’s Asian Champions League 2 competition.
The defeat also extends Victory’s silverware drought, with the club’s most recent trophy the 2021 Australia Cup.

items.body_text:
Australia’s energy minister has said Russia “should not be rewarded for their illegal and immoral invasion of Ukraine” after the US president, Donald Trump, struck a deal with Vladimir Putin to buy diesel from the country.
The energy and climate change minister, Chris Bowen, said on Saturday Australia did not “need or want Russian fuel” while updating reporters on the country’s fuel reserves.
But One Nation leader Pauline Hanson said it was “important to work with countries, if we can have the resources we need”, not ruling out supporting Australia making such a deal of its own.
Trump wrote on social media on Saturday morning Australian time that after a “highly successful discussion” with Putin, Russia had agreed to immediately supply “300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel” to US and global markets, which would be followed by 500,000 tons in November rising later to 3m tons, depending on “the condition of [Russia’s] diesel refineries”.
The deal was criticised by Democrats and some Republicans. Trump is under political pressure due to high diesel prices in the US ahead of next month’s midterm elections.
Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said the deal “plays into Russia’s hands – allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world”.
During a regular Saturday morning press conference to update Australians on the country’s fuel reserves, Bowen, who will lead negotiations at next month’s UN climate talks in Turkey, said: “We don’t need or want Russian fuel in Australia.”
“We have the arrangements in place as best as we possibly can with our trading partners to ensure that Russian fuel doesn’t flow to Australia.
“We do not want Vladimir Putin to benefit from this war in the Middle East. What the United States does is a matter for them. But we won’t be changing our approach.
“We’ll continue to have the very, very firm view that Russia should not be rewarded for their illegal and immoral invasion of Ukraine by any arrangements put in place as a result of the Middle East crisis … policies for other countries are a matter for them.”
Hanson, asked whether she would support Australia taking similar action to Trump, said she wanted to see more oil supply.
“If it’s going to get supplied all throughout the world, because a lot of countries are suffering from this lack of oil, I think it’s important to work with countries, if we can have the resources that we need,” she said at a press conference on the sidelines of the CPAC convention in Brisbane.
“We cannot see countries come to an absolute standstill, businesses shutting down, the cost to the consumer … I think it’s important that all countries must consider that it’s about delivering oil.”
Hanson did not answer a follow-up question about whether that should specifically include Russian oil. During her speech to CPAC, the One Nation leader called for Australia to “produce our own fuel as the world becomes more dangerous”.
Uncertainties remain in the Middle East as a result of Trump’s protracted war with Iran. He this week promised he would not launch more attacks on Iran before the midterm elections.
Bowen said the “situation internationally remains difficult” but Australia had 43 days’ worth of petrol and 31 days’ worth of diesel, which was consistent with recent updates.
“We have 51 ships on the way to Australia with fuel, and we have 3.2bn litres of the various types of fuel locked in and contracted to be delivered over the next four weeks.”
Bowen said he had met with senior Saudi Arabian representatives during a meeting in Fiji to prepare for the UN climate talks in Turkey.
“Obviously we continue to see attacks in Saudi Arabia,” he said. “But I do have confidence that the Saudi Arabian government is taking steps to ensure that the fuel is flowing as well as it possibly can be.

items.summary: Liberal leader says Coalition ‘got some things wrong’ in signing up to net zero and increasing immigrationGet our new political email, free app or daily news podcastPauline Hanson has labelled Angus Taylor a “smarmy management consultant” and told attendees of a major conservative conference that they should not trust the Coalition, as the Liberal leader came under fire from hecklers in the crowd.But Hanson has reiterated her offer to work together with the Coalition to defeat the Labor governme
items.body_text:
Pauline Hanson has labelled Angus Taylor a “smarmy management consultant” and told attendees of a major conservative conference that they should not trust the Coalition, as the Liberal leader came under fire from hecklers in the crowd.
But Hanson has reiterated her offer to work together with the Coalition to defeat the Labor government, suggesting attendees of the annual Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) Australia in Brisbane put the Liberals or Nationals second on their ballot papers, behind One Nation.
Hanson’s insults aimed at the Coalition came moments after Taylor had given a mea culpa to the conference, criticising past Liberal governments – in which he was a key minister – for signing up to a net zero climate target, increasing immigration, and public spending during the pandemic.
“Your frustrations about where we let you down in the recent past are understandable and reasonable. Believe me, I share those frustrations,” the opposition leader said.
CPAC Australia heard from Taylor, Hanson and Nationals leader Matt Canavan on its opening morning on Saturday. It is the first time a sitting Liberal leader has addressed the event, and comes amid One Nation consistently outpolling the Coalition.
Hanson was the best received of all three conservative leaders, receiving a standing ovation from most of the crowd as she took the stage and an even more raucous applause as she finished. Taylor’s speech received a standing ovation from less than half the crowd.
While Taylor took a more conciliatory tone toward One Nation in his speech, Hanson’s address repeatedly slammed what she called the “uniparty”, referring to Labor and the Coalition.
“Australians despise [prime minister Anthony] Albanese … and quite frankly, they don’t want some smarmy management consultant taking his place either,” Hanson said.
Taylor, according to his own website, worked as a management consultant before entering politics, including at global consulting firm McKinsey.
Hanson told CPAC: “The uniparty have taken turns running this country into the ground. Both must be held accountable for the position they’ve put us in.”
She went on to point out the former Coalition government had made a commitment to net zero – a pledge since abolished by Taylor – and instituted the eSafety commissioner, both of which elicited boos from the audience.
“They [Liberals] signed us up to [net zero], so why would we trust them to get us out of it?” she said.
Hanson also said One Nation wanted a royal commission into net zero, including into “every decision the uniparty has made”.
But despite repeated criticism of the Coalition, Hanson said she was still keen for the conservative parties to cooperate.
“I know there are people in this room who support the Liberals and Nationals. I won’t walk away from what One Nation believes, but I will make you one comment. One Nation will work with the Liberals and Nationals to remove this Labor government,” Hanson said.
Taylor, speaking directly before Hanson, began his speech by admitting Coalition governments “got some important things wrong”. Taylor – who served in the Turnbull and Morrison ministries, including as energy minister – said they had “made the mistake of signing up to net zero”, and allowed “immigration numbers to creep up”.
He urged conference attendees to stick by the Coalition, claiming the Liberals and Nationals were “the most credible alternative government”. Taylor did not directly mention One Nation, but conceded “some of you may have doubts” about the Coalition.
“The Coalition is once again conviction-led and unashamedly on the right,” he said.
Taylor lauded the Coalition’s newly announced immigration policy, but received a small smattering of boos from the crowd when he mentioned his net overseas migration target of 130,000 then 160,000 in years three and four of his plan.

items.title: Flydubai co-pilot began radicalisation in Australia, UAE prosecutors say
items.summary: Hammam al-Hammami’s shift towards extremism began while he was a student in Melbourne, according to Emirati attorney generalGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastThe co-pilot who tried to seize control of a flydubai jet flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv last week had been radicalised while studying in Australia, prosecutors in the United Arab Emirates said on Friday.Passengers and crew on the 30 September flight, which had 182 people onboard, intervened to stop 29-year-old Omani
items.body_text:
The co-pilot who tried to seize control of a flydubai jet flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv last week had been radicalised while studying in Australia, prosecutors in the United Arab Emirates said on Friday.
Passengers and crew on the 30 September flight, which had 182 people onboard, intervened to stop 29-year-old Omani national Hammam al-Hammami’s alleged attempt to hijack the plane on its way to Israel.
Dr Hamad Saif al-Shamsi, attorney general of the UAE, said al-Hammami’s shift towards extremism and terrorism began while he was studying at RMIT University in Melbourne.
During his time in Melbourne, he was influenced by the hardline takfiri ideology through reading extremist literature and online content glorifying terrorist organisations and suicide attacks, the attorney general said.
The statement was shared on UAE government social media and first reported by the state-run Emirati news agency, known as WAM.
According to the statement, al-Hammami allegedly told prosecutors he adopted ideas advocating violence and terrorism and drew inspiration from the 9/11 terrorist attacks of 2001.
“The idea of carrying out a similar operation using an aircraft became firmly established in his thinking,” the statement said.
Al-Hammami allegedly prepared himself both psychologically and physically to carry out the alleged terror plot by intensifying his exposure to material promoting terrorism and training in boxing under a private coach.
Last weekend, Australian security agencies launched an investigation after it emerged al-Hammami spent about two years in the country as a student until 2017.
On Monday, RMIT University confirmed that he had studied at its Melbourne campus, but “did not successfully complete an engineering qualification”.
Contacted by Guardian Australia on Saturday, RMIT said it did not have any further comment to make while an investigation led by the Victorian joint counter-terrorism team was ongoing.

items.title: Hundreds of thousands lose power as Hurricane Isaias batters Florida, Alabama
items.summary: Hundreds of thousands of people in Alabama and the Florida Panhandle were without power early Saturday after Isaias crashed into the U.S. Gulf Coast as a dangerous hurricane and left flooded roads and downed trees in its wake as it moved inland.
items.body_text:
World
Hundreds of thousands lose power as Hurricane Isaias batters Florida, Alabama
Isaias marks the first hurricane of the Atlantic season
Hundreds of thousands of people in Alabama and the Florida Panhandle were without power early Saturday after Isaias crashed into the U.S. Gulf Coast as a dangerous hurricane and left flooded roads and downed trees in its wake as it moved inland.
The storm made landfall Friday as a Category 2 hurricane, then quickly moved north through Alabama as its wind speeds dropped sharply.
But the possibility of life-threatening storm surges still loomed for parts of the Florida Panhandle, along with heavy rain and potential flooding for much of the region over the weekend and into Monday.
Isaias was about 40 kilometres south-southwest of Montgomery, Ala., and nearly 170 kilometres south of Birmingham, Ala., with maximum sustained winds of 55 km/h, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) said Saturday.
Forecasters also warned that conditions could stir up tornadoes across parts of the Florida Panhandle and into Georgia and the Carolinas.
Isaias made landfall near Destin, Fla., as the first hurricane of the Atlantic season.
The storm's rapid intensification was fuelled by record-warm waters in the Gulf of Mexico. The Gulf has seen substantial warming over the past few decades, and experts say the current marine heatwave was made far more likely due to human-caused climate change.
While the warm waters provided the abundant energy that Isaias needed, its formation was also made possible by favourable atmospheric conditions, including weak upper-level winds that would otherwise have disrupted the burgeoning storm.
But just before landfall, upper-level wind shear increased, causing the storm to weaken slightly, dropping it back to Category 2 and making it more disorganized, expanding the area hit by damaging winds.
Hurricane-force winds lashed the Gulf shoreline in the low-lying coastal area known for powdery white-sand beaches dotted with vacation homes, waterfront bars and seafood shacks.
"The storm is here. Buckle down at this point. Don’t be getting out on the roads," Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said at a news conference Friday.
Roads in Destin were flooded, while in nearby Pensacola, police warned residents to stay off the streets because of debris across roadways. While the extent of the damage was not immediately known, many area residents posted pictures online of downed trees and power lines, and one social media video showed a roof being ripped off an inn in Pensacola.
Some Panhandle counties temporarily suspended emergency response Friday night because of dangerous conditions.
Parts of southern Alabama also were flooded, with officials in Mobile reporting downed trees and power lines. Roads in Houston County, which is in the southeastern corner of the state, were closed because of similar conditions.
More than 726,000 customers in Florida and Alabama were without power early Saturday, according to poweroutage.com.
A man tries to push a car as waves wash over the road on Friday ahead of the arrival of Hurricane Isaias, in Englewood, Fla. (Facebook/Reuters)
Tim Mowry, who rode out the storm from his home in Pensacola, said the wind was so intense it sounded like a train whistle as it whipped through a crack in his patio door. He lost power around 4:30 p.m. but was able to rely on a generator. Standing water also covered his backyard, and parts of his fence were ripped down, but overall he said the storm wasn’t as bad as he expected.
"As far as Pensacola-wise, we really got fortunate," Mowry said.
Mowry said his son, who lives about 15 minutes away, tried to drive to his home after losing power but had to turn around because downed trees and power lines blocked the roads.
Weakened storm threatens region with floods
Despite weakening, heavy rain is forecast as Isaias moves inland, with 10 to 20 centimetres or even more expected through the weekend from southern Alabama, the Florida Panhandle and Big Bend

items.title: Netanyahu faces fresh allegations he ignored warnings about Oct. 7 — right before an election
items.summary: Just weeks before a potentially pivotal election, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is defending against new allegations that he ignored high-level warnings from Arab allies that might have prevented the Hamas-led attacks on Oct. 7, 2023.
items.body_text:
World·New
Netanyahu faces fresh allegations he ignored warnings about Oct. 7 — right before an election
'Complete hoax,' says Israeli PM as calls grow for an inquiry
With just weeks before Benjamin Netanyahu is set to face a potentially pivotal election, the Israeli prime minister is defending against new allegations that he ignored high-level warnings from Arab allies that might have prevented the Hamas-led attacks on Oct. 7, 2023.
In a new book excerpted in Israel's Haaretz newspaper, journalists Shlomi Eldar and Ruth Yuval contend that the United Arab Emirates President Mohamed bin Zayed telephoned Netanyahu 10 days prior to the attack to warn of a potential significant move by the militant group against Israel.
"The [worst thing] was that Netanyahu heard his warning and didn't deliver it to the security echelon," Eldar told CBC News at his home near Tel Aviv.
"Not the chief of staff, not the head of the Shin Bet, not the head of the Mossad," he said, referring to the country's internal security and spy agencies, respectively. "And also not the defence minister."
The Oct. 7 attacks would prove to be the deadliest in Israel's history. Some 1,200 people were killed, including more than 800 civilians, with 251 people taken back into Gaza as hostages.
Israel's subsequent war in Gaza has killed more than 74,000 people, according to Gaza's Health Ministry.
Eldar says, according to his sources, the U.A.E.'s warning was not specific about a date, only that Hamas's leader in Gaza at the time, Yahiya Sinwar, was planning something "very big."
A new book co-authored by Israeli journalist Shlomi Eldar contends that United Arab Emirates President Mohamed bin Zayed called Netanyahu more than a week before attacks to warn of a potential significant move by Hamas. (CBC)
Shortly after Haaretz published the allegations, other media outlets including the Wall Street Journal and The Atlantic reported that Egypt's intelligence head, Abbas Kamel, had delivered similar warnings in the days just prior to Oct. 7.
Netanyahu has dismissed the allegations as fabrication by political opponents and regional actors he accuses of trying to scupper his chances of winning another term in office when Israelis go to the polls on Oct. 27.
"I didn't ignore any warnings because I didn't receive any warnings, I mean that's a complete hoax," Netanyahu told CBS News. "It's politically propagated by certain countries or certain elements abroad, but they're completely false."
The U.A.E. has not confirmed or denied the allegations contained in Eldar's and Yuval's book Hostages: 843 Days of Abandonment.
But they've added fuel to the fire for Israelis who have been demanding a state commission of inquiry into Israeli security failings for three years now.
A protester dressed as Netanyahu kneels on a sheet covered with red paint with a sign in Hebrew announcing the 'untimely death of responsibility' on the third anniversary of the attacks, in Tel Aviv, on Monday. (Avi Ohayon/Reuters)
This year's memorial ceremonies for the victims of Oct. 7 were accompanied by protests in Jerusalem and Tel Aviv demanding accountability from Netanyahu.
Some demonstrators held signs reading: "No forgiveness for failure, no forgiveness for abandonment."
Others read: "The people will remember Oct. 7 on Oct. 27," referring to the election.
The face of Eyal Eshel's 19-year-old daughter Roni now graces a memorial stone along the Israeli/Gaza boundary, close to the Nahal Oz base where she and 14 other young women performing their Israeli military service were killed on Oct. 7.
